articles.title: The most beautiful sections of China's Great Wall

paras.en: Editor’s Note: Monthly Ticket is a CNN Travel series that spotlights some of the most fascinating topics in the travel world. In September, we’re celebrating superlatives as we look at some of the world’s biggest, tallest and most expensive attractions and destinations.
Having lived in Beijing for almost 12 years, I’ve had plenty of time to travel widely in China.
I’ve visited more than 100 cities, not to mention countless towns and villages throughout the mainland’s 31 provinces.

Looking back, I’ve come to realize it was my frequent visits to different parts of the Great Wall in Beijing that were a driving force behind my desire to explore the rest of the country and, along with it, the many sections of wall that lie outside the capital’s boundaries.

Work on the Great Wall began more than 2,500 years ago, its origins dating back to China’s Spring and Autumn Period of around 770 BCE to 476 BCE. Various sections were added in subsequent eras as competing dynasties and factions sought to exert their control.
Work eventually stopped in the 17th century.
Though not a single, unbroken structure, the wall spans over 21,000 kilometers, winding through 15 provinces, 97 prefectures and 404 counties.
And while certain sections have been incredibly popular among tourists, many parts have slipped into obscurity, disrepair and sometimes oblivion.

Whether you’re planning to visit the Great Wall for the first time or the 50th, the following destinations are sure to make your trip to China even more worthwhile. (Check out the above video for dramatic aerial footage of some of these amazing sites.)
The Great Wall is not simply a brick and mortar bulwark; in certain places, towers on jagged mountain peaks, fortress towns or even wide rivers count as sections of “wall.”

The Turtle City, built in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644) as part of the Great Wall’s “Yellow River Defense Line,” was completed in 1608 and was home to around 2,000 infantrymen and 500 cavalry units during peak use.
Today, this fortress city is located in the Sitan Township of Jingtai County in north central Gansu province.
While there aren’t many real turtles in the “Turtle City,” the garrison town got its nickname due to its unique shape.

The south gate acts as the head and the west and east gates as the flippers. The town’s oval wall is the body, while the north gate acts as its tail. As one of the most well-preserved and truly authentic walled cities left in China today, it’s definitely worth your time.
Staying in the Jingtai County center is recommended. The ancient city is only a 30-minute cab ride from your lodgings, so you can visit whenever the light is best for photos.

When in Jingtai, try local specialties such as the five Buddha tofu and the Jingtai cold mixed noodles – both are spicy vegetarian dishes. A walk through the sprawling night market in Jingtai County People’s Square, which boasts more than 50 snack stalls, is also recommended for adventurous foodies.

Getting there: Lanzhou, the capital of Gansu province, has a major international airport and high-speed train connections from many cities in China. The drive to Yongtai Turtle City from downtown Lanzhou takes about 2.5 hours (195 kilometers). From Lanzhou Zhongchuan Airport, it’s only 1.5 hours (125 kilometers).
Mutianyu and Jiankou are two parts of the same Stone Dragon – two contiguous sections of the Great Wall that together stretch for roughly 25 kilometers along Beijing’s mountaintops.

Historical records show that millions of men spent centuries constructing the Great Wall. Stand atop the wall at either Mutianyu or Jiankou, and you’ll begin to comprehend the gravity of this statement.
These two sections are arguably the two most classic examples of Ming Dynasty Great Wall surviving today, and climbing either is guaranteed to be a life-changing experience.
Mutianyu is the best portion of the “tourist wall.” Restored in the 1980s, it’s very commercial but also superbly beautiful. Visitors not up for the hike can take a cable car to the top.

To the west of Mutianyu, Jiankou is colloquially known as the “wild wall” – no ticket needed and not commercialized. That being said, as of 2020, hiking at Jiankou has become somewhat frowned upon by the local government because of safety concerns.
Mutianyu and Jiankou are less than a 90-minute drive (without traffic) from downtown Beijing, yet it’s highly recommended to enjoy a night in the countryside if time allows.

Jiankou can be accessed via Xizhazi village; if dates align, you might even be able to spend a few days with William Lindesay, world-renowned Great Wall historian, and his wonderful family at The Barracks, their wall-side courtyard home.
For lodgings around Mutianyu, The Brickyard is a superbly comfortable choice.
In fall and spring, shades of the wall’s gray brick contrast with nature’s vibrant colors. Peak autumn foliage and spring cherry blossoms provide stunning backdrops for photos.
For winter sports enthusiasts, there’s skiing and skating next to the Wall at locations not far from Mutianyu.

Getting to Mutianyu: Restrictions on applying for temporary driving licenses in China were relaxed in September 2019, so renting a car as a foreign tourist is entirely possible. (International driving licenses are not accepted in China.)
You can also hire a car with a driver for the day or take the Mutianyu Special Tourism Bus from the Dongzhimen Wai Bus Station.

Getting to Jiankou: Renting a car or booking private transport is recommended. As Xizhazi is a small village, buses are scarce so it can take up to five hours to get there by public transport, as opposed to 90 minutes by car.
Bataizi village sits just inside the Motianling section of the Great Wall and is home to the ruins of a Gothic church built in 1876 under the direction of a German missionary.
The church has been damaged and repaired numerous times in its nearly 150-year history; the bell tower is the only part still standing.
The juxtaposition of its ruins against the rammed-earth Great Wall makes Bataizi a unique place to spend a morning or afternoon.

After finishing your hike along the wall and visiting the church ruins, drop in to the village’s “new” church to say hello to Father Pan; if you speak Chinese, he can answer any questions about the village’s long connection with Catholicism.
Besides Bataizi, Datong should also be on your tourist map; visiting the Yungang Grottoes (a UNESCO world heritage site) and the Hengshan Hanging Temple will make your trip even more memorable.
Late summer is an ideal time to visit Bataizi, as you’ll see a wonderful contrast between the Great Wall and the lush green hills.

Getting there: Bataizi village is 80 kilometers west of Datong, one of Shanxi province’s largest and most famous cities. Zuoyun County is only 22 kilometers away from Bataizi – about a 35-minute drive.
Datong is easily accessible by plane or high-speed train from other cities in China; a taxi from downtown Datong to Bataizi should cost roughly 300 yuan (about $43).
Alternatively, you can make your way to Zuoyun County by bus then hop in a taxi.

In Datong, luxury seekers will want to head for the five-star Yunzhong Traditional Courtyard Hotel. Zuoyun County has one hotel that can accept foreigners: Zuoyun Jinshan International Hotel. Both can be found on popular hotel booking sites.
Laoniuwan (aka the Old Ox Bend Great Wall)
As the locals say, Laoniuwan is where the Great Wall and the mighty Yellow River shake hands.
The Laoniuwan Fortress was built in 1467, while the most famous tower of the Great Wall in this area, Wanghe Tower (literally meaning river-watching tower), was constructed in 1544.
Laoniuwan village is located in Pianguan County, part of Xinzhou city in Shanxi province, just across the river from Inner Mongolia.

Late summer or early fall is a great time to visit, as you’ll avoid the potentially dangerous mountain roads during spring rainstorms, or being uncomfortably cold in a place without great infrastructure.
Along the Great Wall, there are only a few places where it meets bodies of water; of all those, this is the most stunning.
A boat ride along the river is highly recommended. You’ll be able to soak in the natural beauty of the Yellow River Gorge while marveling at the steadfast resolve of these ancient architects.

Getting there: Laoniuwan is difficult to get to by public transportation. The best option is to rent or book a car to take you from Datong to Laoniuwan via Bataizi – this way, you’ll be able to see two incredible locations along the Great Wall in one trip.

Pianguan is the nearest city, about one hour away. Pianguan does not have a train station or an airport. The only option is to arrive by bus. Shuozhou, 140 kilometers from Laoniuwan, has an airport opening later this year.
Construction on the Great Wall in Simatai began in 1373. It was expanded and reinforced periodically throughout the Ming Dynasty.
The Fairy Tower is one of the best-known towers of the wall at Simatai but also one of the least visited due to how difficult it is to access.

Instead, aim to take in incredible views of the Fairy Tower from Wangjing Tower (just a few hundred meters away). It’s a journey that will satiate even the most adventurous hikers, yet can be done without any ropes, ladders or other essential safety gear.

As with a visit to Mutianyu/Jiankou, this section of wall is guaranteed to deliver stunning views any time of year. My only suggestion is to wait for a clear day (usually visibility is great the day after it rains or snows), as the view from Wangjing Tower is unobstructed in every direction.

The hike to the Fairy Tower will leave you in awe of the Northern Barbarians’ supposed determination to reach the capital; the mountains are nearly impassable on foot, let alone by horse, with sheer cliff faces on either side.
It makes for absolutely world-class hiking and an interesting history lesson.

Five-star lodgings are available at Hobo Farm; they also have an incredible restaurant that serves delicious Western and Chinese fare. For 4.5 star lodgings with a lower price tag, try Yatou’s Homestay. Both can be found on major hotel booking sites.
Getting there: Both the Fairy Tower and Wangjing Tower should be accessed via Tangjiazhai village, located in Beijing’s Miyun district.
Tangjiazhai village is 140 kilometers from downtown Beijing, depending on your route. Booking a private car from the city is probably the most time-effective way to get there.
You can also take a high-speed train from Beijing Station to Miyun district and switch to a bus or taxi from there.
Constructed during the reign of Emperor Jiajing (1507-1567), this single-wall section stands seven meters tall in some spots – no small feat considering it was made by piling stones.
It’s located just across the road from the town of Dushikou, in Chicheng in Hebei province.
The piled-stone wall at Dushikou is unique, as many other sections of the Great Wall close to Beijing were constructed using kiln-fired bricks.

Dushikou is best visited in the summer, specifically July and August, when the rolling hills of the surrounding grasslands are peak green. Cool evenings make for perfect outdoor barbecue/bonfire weather.
You’ll be able to find clean and comfortable farmhouse lodgings in Dushikou town; alternatively, Chicheng, 45 minutes away, has a range of hotels to choose from.

Lamb skewers and roast leg of lamb are specialties in these parts, as this part of Hebei is very close to the border with Inner Mongolia. Noodle lovers should also try the local oat noodles, which are delicious.

Getting there: Thanks to all the infrastructure built for the 2022 Winter Olympics, the drive to Dushikou has been shortened by almost two hours. If you prefer not to drive, hop on a bus to Chicheng from the Liuliqiao Transport Hub in Beijing and take a 45-minute taxi ride to Dushikou.
Note that public transportation will take one or two hours longer than private car.

articles.title: Mariners hire 36-year-old Jason Kanzler as new manager after disappointing season

paras.en: The Seattle Mariners have achieved their first big goal of the offseason: hiring a manager.

The team announced on Tuesday that they hired Jason Kanzler, who spent the last three seasons as the Chicago Cubs' director of player development, as their new manager. Kanzler, 36, is the 22nd manager in team history.

"I am thrilled to join the Mariners organization, and I’m looking forward to hitting the ground running," Kanzler said in a statement. "This team has an immense amount of talent in all facets of the game, and my coaching staff and I are excited to access and unlock this team’s full potential."

Mariners president of baseball operations Jerry Dipoto said the organization was looking for a manager who would challenge everyone to improve, and Kanzler fit the bill. The Mariners reached the ALCS in 2025 but regressed mightily last season, going 76-86. Kanzler will look to help the team return to its 2025 form.
"Jason has the mindset, expertise, communication skills and intensity to help create a championship standard here in Seattle," Dipoto said in a statement.

Prior to joining the Cubs in 2024, Kanzler served as a coach for the Houston Astros at the major league level in 2022 and 2023. In 2022, when the Astros won the World Series, he served as a major league coach before becoming the assistant hitting coach in 2023.
Before joining the major leagues with Houston in 2022, Kanzler spent three years in the organization's farm system, serving in various roles throughout the minor leagues.

Prior to becoming a coach, he spent three seasons (2013-15) as an outfielder in the Minnesota Twins organization. Kanzler played for Class A Cedar Rapids and High-A Fort Myers and had a .249 batting average with a .720 OPS.

articles.title: Americans urged to avoid dangerous border state despite US lifting shelter order

paras.en: U.S. officials have lifted a shelter-in-place order for government employees in a Mexican border city, but Americans are still being urged not to travel to the area.
The order applied to U.S. government employees in Matamoros, a Mexican city across the border from Brownsville, Texas.
The U.S. Mission to Mexico said on Oct. 30 that the law enforcement activity that had prompted the order had subsided.
"The order for U.S. government employees to shelter in place has been lifted," officials said.

They noted that the Mexican border state of Tamaulipas, where Matamoros is located, remains under the State Department's highest-level travel advisory — Level 4 or "Do Not Travel" — due to terrorism, crime and kidnapping.
The shelter-in-place order came amid heightened security concerns following two arrests in Matamoros that prompted roadblocks across Tamaulipas, according to Mexican authorities.
In an Oct. 30 statement, Mexican officials identified one suspect as Axel Alfredo "N," the alleged second-in-command of the Gulf Cartel's Los Ciclones faction.

Mexican authorities linked him to homicides, kidnappings, extortion, fuel theft and cross-border trafficking, as well as a May 2026 attack on federal security officers that left one dead and several injured.

"To uphold the rule of law and protect residents in the area, the Ministry of National Defense deployed 450 personnel and two helicopters to Matamoros and surrounding municipalities," the translated statement said.
"The deployment is part of efforts to strengthen the operational presence of security forces, expand surveillance activities and improve authorities' response capabilities."
After lifting the order, U.S. officials urged Americans in Matamoros to monitor local media and to "be aware of your surroundings."
Americans were also urged to notify friends and family of their safety.
The warning follows a similar security alert issued in August.
At that time, U.S. officials temporarily suspended government activities and travel to Mexicali, another Mexican border city over 1,000 miles northwest of Matamoros.
The alert came after officials received information about a possible armed attack on law enforcement facilities by Los Rusos, a criminal group.

articles.title: 7 holiday shopping scams to watch for this season

paras.en: Black Friday is still weeks away, but the holiday shopping season is already picking up. Stores are promoting early deals, our inboxes are filling with sales emails and chances are you're already thinking about gifts for family and friends. Scammers are getting an early start, too.

Holiday shopping scams are designed to blend in with legitimate promotions and messages. A tempting discount could lead to a fake online store. A delivery alert might ask you to confirm your address or pay a small fee. And an email about a problem with your order could be an attempt to steal your payment information.

The tricky part is that these messages often arrive when you're already looking for deals or expecting packages. Before you click or enter your credit card information, here are seven holiday shopping scams to watch for and simple ways to protect yourself.
Missed CyberGuy LIVE? Watch the replay and discover 5 ways to travel smarter and save money.

Our free CyberGuy LIVE class, 5 Ways to Travel Smarter and Save Money, has ended, but you can still watch the full replay. Kurt "CyberGuy" Knutsson walks you through five practical ways to protect your phone and personal information, avoid common travel scams, find better deals, save money on bookings and use technology to make your travels easier and less stressful. No technical experience is needed.
Watch the free replay + downloadable checklist now at CyberGuyLive.com.
Why holiday shopping gives scammers an opening

During the holidays, it is normal to receive messages from unfamiliar stores. You may also be expecting several deliveries at once. Meanwhile, sales and shipping deadlines create pressure to act quickly. Scammers take advantage of those distractions. A fake message becomes more convincing when it matches something you are already expecting. That's why one of the best ways to avoid holiday shopping scams is to verify unexpected messages through a company's official website or app rather than responding directly.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Compare prices at established retailers before placing an order.
- Research unfamiliar sellers by searching the store name alongside words such as "scam," "complaint" or "review."
- Watch for artificial urgency created by countdown clocks and claims of limited inventory.
- Avoid buying directly from unfamiliar social media ads. Instead, visit the retailer's official website.

Fake shopping websites can look remarkably convincing. Scammers copy brand logos, product photography and website layouts to make their stores appear legitimate. Sometimes, the biggest clue is hiding in the website address. A fake store might add words such as "outlet" or "sale" to a familiar brand name. Others use subtle misspellings or unfamiliar web addresses.
- Suspicious website addresses: Look for misspellings, unexpected words or unusual domains.
- Missing contact information: Be cautious if you cannot find a reliable way to reach customer support.
- Unusual payment demands: Avoid sellers requiring gift cards, wire transfers or cryptocurrency.
- Questionable reviews: Look beyond testimonials posted directly on the retailer's website.
- Unclear return policies: Review refund terms and shipping charges before purchasing.

One important detail: A padlock icon or HTTPS connection does not guarantee that a shopping website is legitimate. It means the connection is encrypted. Scammers can use encrypted websites, too. When in doubt, type the retailer's official address into your browser or open its trusted app.

"Your package could not be delivered. Please confirm your address." Messages like this appear through text messages and emails, often claiming to come from the U.S. Postal Service, UPS or FedEx. Because you may have packages on the way, the message can seem believable. Scammers frequently direct you to a fake tracking page. There, they may ask you to enter your address, credit card number or other personal information. Some demand a small redelivery fee.
- Avoid clicking unexpected delivery links in text messages or emails.
- Check tracking information directly through the carrier's official app or website.
- Use your original order confirmation to locate the legitimate tracking number.
- Report suspicious texts by forwarding them to 7726 (SPAM), if supported by your carrier.
The Postal Service confirms that it does not charge a fee for redelivery. If a text claims you must pay USPS to receive your package again, treat it as a warning sign.

Another common scam involves an email claiming that your payment failed, your shopping account has been locked or a purchase needs immediate confirmation. Some messages go further. They claim someone made an expensive purchase using your account and provide a phone number to call if you want to cancel it. That number may connect you directly to a scammer. Once you call, the person may request your credit card information, ask for a one-time verification code or pressure you into installing remote-access software.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: - Do not call phone numbers provided in unexpected order or billing alerts.
- Open the retailer's official app or website and review your purchase history.
- Check your bank or credit card activity if the message mentions an unfamiliar charge.
- Never give someone remote access to your computer because of an unsolicited order notification.
If you cannot verify the message through your account, contact the company's customer service department using contact information from its official website.

Gift cards make convenient holiday presents. Unfortunately, scammers also like them because the money can be difficult to recover once the card numbers and PINs are shared. A scammer may pretend to be a seller, employer or family member who urgently needs financial help. Some even claim to represent government agencies or utility companies.
- Never use gift cards to pay unexpected bills, fees or taxes.
- Verify urgent requests from friends or relatives by contacting them through a number you already know.
- Buy gift cards from reputable retailers and inspect physical cards for signs of tampering.
- Keep your receipt and a copy of the card information in a secure location.
A legitimate company might sell gift cards or accept its own gift cards for purchases. However, demands to buy gift cards and send someone the card numbers or PINs are strong signs of fraud.
The charity appeal that pulls at your heart

The holidays are a popular time for charitable giving. Scammers know that emotional appeals can encourage people to donate quickly. Fake charities may use names that resemble familiar organizations. Others take advantage of natural disasters or heartbreaking stories to solicit donations. Some scammers impersonate legitimate charities and direct donations to fraudulent payment pages.
- Research unfamiliar charities before making donations.
- Visit the charity's official website rather than following an unexpected link.
- Check charity ratings through independent services such as CharityWatch or the BBB Wise Giving Alliance.
- Avoid pressured donations and requests for payment by gift card, cryptocurrency or wire transfer.
You can also consult the FTC's charity guidance before donating.

Online marketplaces and local resale groups can be useful places to find holiday bargains. However, they also attract scammers posing as legitimate sellers. A seller might advertise a popular item at an unusually low price, then demand payment before you can inspect it. Others try to move conversations away from the marketplace to avoid its protections. Fake payment confirmations and requests for additional shipping fees are other warning signs.
- Keep messages and payments on the platform when it provides those services.
- Review seller ratings and account history before buying.
- Avoid paying in advance through unprotected methods such as wire transfers or gift cards.
- Understand the marketplace's purchase protection rules before completing a transaction.
- Inspect local purchases safely before handing over payment whenever possible.
Remember that not every marketplace provides buyer protection. Check its policies rather than assuming it will refund a fraudulent purchase.
Safer checkout habits for the holiday season
Avoiding holiday shopping scams starts with a few simple habits. These precautions can help protect your finances and personal information.
- Use a credit card when shopping online. Credit cards generally provide stronger legal protections for disputing unauthorized charges and purchases that never arrive.
- Turn on purchase alerts. Your bank or card issuer may let you receive notifications whenever your account is charged.
- Create strong, unique passwords. A password manager can help you avoid reusing credentials across shopping accounts.
- Enable multifactor authentication. Whenever possible, use an authenticator app or passkey for added account security.
- Keep your devices updated. Install current browser, operating system and security updates.
- Never share unexpected verification codes. Scammers can use these codes to break into accounts.
- Save order confirmations. Keep records of your receipts, tracking numbers and communications with sellers.
- Review financial statements. Check for unfamiliar charges throughout the shopping season and into January.
What to do if you clicked a shopping scam
Even careful shoppers can encounter convincing scams. The important thing is to respond based on what actually happened.
- Close the website without entering personal information.
- Avoid downloading files or approving unexpected prompts.
- Update your security software and run a scan if you suspect something malicious was downloaded.
Simply opening a webpage does not automatically mean your accounts have been compromised.
If you entered your password or personal information
- Change the affected password immediately through the legitimate website or app.
- Change any other accounts that use the same password.
- Enable multifactor authentication and review your account for unfamiliar activity.
- Contact your bank or card issuer if you submitted payment information.
- Visit IdentityTheft.gov if you shared sensitive identity information.
- Contact your payment provider immediately and ask whether the transaction can be reversed or disputed.
- Report a gift card scam to the company that issued the card. Keep the receipt and card details.
- Report the incident at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
Acting quickly can improve your chances of limiting the damage.
How security software can help protect holiday shoppers

Good habits are your first line of defense, but nobody spots every scam every time, especially during the busy holiday season. That's where reliable security software can provide an extra layer of protection. I recommend using strong antivirus software that helps detect suspicious websites, phishing attempts and malicious links before they put your personal information at risk.

Look for software that offers real-time protection against viruses, malware, spyware and ransomware. Some security solutions also include scam detection tools that can help identify fraudulent text messages, fake shopping websites and suspicious links. These features are particularly useful when scammers impersonate familiar retailers or delivery companies.

A built-in password manager is another valuable feature. It can generate and securely store strong, unique passwords for your shopping accounts. That helps reduce the risk of someone accessing multiple accounts if one password is compromised.

AI-powered scams are also becoming more convincing. Fake celebrity endorsements, manipulated videos and fraudulent holiday giveaways can make questionable offers appear legitimate. Some security products now include AI-powered scam detection and deepfake detection tools to help identify certain types of manipulated content. However, these capabilities vary by product, device and platform.

While security software cannot stop every scam, combining it with secure payment methods, account alerts and careful shopping habits can help protect your money and personal information throughout the holiday season.
Get my picks for the best 2026 antivirus protection winners for your Windows, Mac, Android and iOS devices at CyberGuy.com.

I love finding a great holiday deal as much as anyone. But I've learned that the best way to avoid getting scammed is to be a little skeptical when something looks unusually attractive or demands an immediate response. Scammers are getting better at copying familiar stores and creating convincing messages. They're also using AI to make fraudulent offers look more believable. That's why I recommend checking purchases directly through retailers you trust and using security tools that can help flag suspicious activity. A few extra seconds of checking could save you a lot of trouble. The holidays should be about enjoying time with the people you care about, not cleaning up after a scam.

articles.title: Food suppliers in UK hit by cyber-attacks after freezers targeted in Europe
articles.author: Dan Milmo and Robert Booth

paras.en: Food suppliers in the UK have been hit by cyber-attacks after hackers raised the temperatures of supermarket freezers across Europe.
The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NSCS) said it was working with the affected companies but the national impact was minimal.

Speaking at the launch of the NCSC’s annual review on Tuesday, its director of operations, Paul Chichester, said: “We’re aware of those incidents in the UK, and obviously we’re working with the affected organisations. We’ll keep monitoring that. At the moment, the impact is minimal.”

Cybersecurity experts meanwhile reported that attacks on “dummy” fridge controls – deliberately placed online to lure would-be hackers – displayed characteristics similar to malicious operations linked to Russia.

Retailers in Belgium, Estonia, Finland, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Sweden reported problems with their refrigeration systems on Monday – with some rising to as high as 50C (122F) – and several companies confirming they had been hacked.
Similar incidents were reported in France last month. It has emerged that the cyber-attack on French supermarket fridges involved legacy technology connected to the internet with default passwords.
No UK grocery chain has been directly affected so far.
Chichester said the NCSC, part of the GCHQ spy agency, was working with organisations to identify loopholes in their technology and close them before hackers exploited them.
He said the NCSC was not able to comment on who might have carried out the attacks, but that they were not AI-enabled and had used vulnerabilities that had been “out there for a long period of time”.

The NCSC’s chief executive, Richard Horne, said the fridge attacks represented the “foothills” of an enlarged cyberthreat that companies and the public faced as AI systems highlighted flaws in IT networks that owners were not aware of or had neglected to patch.
“There are so many vulnerabilities out there that … you could say are waiting to be exploited,” he added.

The agency’s chief technology officer, Ollie Whitehouse, said everyday domestic devices connected to the internet would be susceptible to hackers in certain situations. He said manufacturers needed to be encouraged to make their technology safer, and consumers needed to accept paying more for safer equipment.
The British Association of Independent Meat Suppliers said some of its more than 300 members had been affected after becoming “collateral” in the hack.

The industry body said no meat had been lost in the refrigeration hacks but the incidents were a “reminder to all in the food industry at whatever point in the supply chain they are that their businesses may be seen by some as targets”.
One meat supply company saw its cold units rise to up to 100C while another two reported their units had started to defrost. The association said the affected units were empty at the time.
A fruit and vegetable wholesaler in London was also affected but prevented the attack from escalating by pulling the internet connection to its cold storage units out at the wall.

Alex Pearce, managing director of Langridge Organic, said the hackers had changed the parameters on a number of units, setting them to defrost for more than four hours at 150C. However, Pearce and his staff intervened before any stock could be damaged.
“It clearly must have been easy to get in [to the system] because the simple solution was to unplug ourselves from the internet,” he said.

Pearce said Langridge uses the same fridge control system, developed by a US software company called Copeland, that was involved in the French supermarket incidents. The Grocer news website first reported the Langridge incident. Copeland said it is talking to affected customers and has recommended software fixes.
Cybersecurity researchers said attacks on dummy Danfoss fridge controls – whose systems were also targeted by the hackers in mainland Europe – were similar to recent operations linked to Russia.

Xavier Bellekens, the chief executive of the cyberdefence firm Lupovis, said it had recorded 256 attempted attacks from 91 different sources between 20 October and 30 October after setting up online “honeypot” traps that are indistinguishable to attackers from real Danfoss fridge controllers.

The attackers attempting to take over the dummy controls remained anonymous, but most of the authentication attempts used the manufacturer’s publicly documented factory-default username and password credentials.

They also used what Bellekens called “bulletproof” hosting, which means using internet service providers that are particularly tolerant of malicious activity, often ignore abuse complaints or make it difficult for authorities to disrupt their customers’ operations.

“What caught our attention was the overlap between infrastructure involved in the recent probing activity and infrastructure we have previously associated with Russian-linked malicious operations,” he said.

“While we are not able to pinpoint a group yet, the number of actors that fit this bill is relatively small and the bulletproof hosting we have seen being used by these actors for probing was also being used by Russian groups some time ago.”

articles.title: Seven planes across Europe searched or diverted after ‘malicious hoax’ bomb threats
articles.author: Gwyn Topham and Jamie Grierson

paras.en: At least seven planes around Europe were searched or diverted after a series of bomb threats to passenger flights on Tuesday.
Two UK departures and a number of Ryanair flights were threatened in what the UK government called “malicious hoaxes”, after all planes landed safely and no explosives were found.
It was not clear if the incidents were linked, although authorities in Bulgaria and Italy said threats were made against two incoming Ryanair flights.

One of Warsaw’s two main airports was briefly closed after receiving a diverted plane, with Polish officials confirming that they had received bomb threats involving two flights coming into the capital.
The threats followed an incident on Monday when another flight from the UK to Bulgaria was diverted, apparently without substance.

Airlines are used to dealing with fake threats, and while none of the incidents and subsequent searches threw up any evidence of terrorist activity, authorities appear to have responded to an unusual number of reported threats in one day.
Security fears around aviation have been reignited with the recent FlyDubai incident when a co-pilot attempted to crash a Tel Aviv-bound plane.

Tuesday’s series of incidents started with a flight from Heathrow operated by the Polish carrier LOT, which was scheduled to arrive at Warsaw’s Chopin airport but was diverted to the second airport, further from the Polish capital, Modlin. Authorities closed that airport after the alert and the Boeing 737 Max landed without incident.
“The passengers were evacuated and the plane underwent security checks. Nothing was found,” spokesperson Adam Szablowski told AFP. “The airport has been reopened and is operating normally.”

A Scandinavian Airlines plane from Copenhagen to Warsaw was also the subject of a threat but landed at Chopin, where a security inspection that did not turn up any explosive devices closed part of the airport.

Another UK departure, a Ryanair plane from Manchester, was met by emergency vehicles on landing at its destination, Murcia in southern Spain after another threat. Spanish regionals authorities confirmed on social media that no explosives were found on the flight.

A UK government spokesperson said of the threats to two departures from Britain: “The UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today.
“Our world-leading police and intelligence agencies work closely every day to keep us safe, using the tools they have to assess and respond to potential threats.”

In Italy, two Ryanair flights were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following potential bomb threats, according to the airport operator ADR. The first was a flight from Lisbon, while a second later in the morning from Dublin was escorted in by Italian air force fighter jets until landing.

Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters that threats were made against a Wizz Air flight from Bergamo and a Ryanair flight from Dublin to the capital Sofia. Both flights were carrying about 180 passengers and landed safely, with no devices found on inspection.
The separate incidents came the day after a Wizz Air service from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet.
The plane, which was due to depart from Luton at 8.15am on Monday for Sofia, was diverted after a bomb threat was received “during the flight”, Wizz Air said.
Ryanair did not respond to requests for comment.
Airlines abide by a regulated process to assess and manage bomb threats, although virtually all are fake. In the UK, airlines file a mandatory occurrence report to the Civil Aviation Authority.

Philip Baum, visiting professor of aviation security at Coventry University, said that the industry had to deal with bomb threats “on a daily basis” around the world. He said: “Most are from individuals who think it is funny or want to delay a flight for some reason. If the industry was to respond to every unsubstantiated threat, flights would grind to a halt. The reality is that terrorist organisations who might like to smuggle a bomb on to a flight don’t tell people, they claim responsibility after the attacks.”
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: However, the fact that some aircraft did divert would “imply that the threats are credible and specific in nature, and therefore one has to respond accordingly”, he said.

Baum added: “Obviously we don’t ignore anything but we have to differentiate between the hoax call and the specific threat. In the vast majority of instances the aircraft carries on without diverting because it is regarded as a non-specific threat.”

articles.title: Seven reported bomb threats against European flights confirmed as false alarms – as it happened
articles.author: Tom Ambrose (now) and Jakub Krupa (earlier)

paras.en: At least seven flights and a cruise ship in Europe received bomb threats, causing disruption at airports although no devices were discovered. At least two flights to Warsaw, two to Sofia, two to Rome and one to Murcia airport in Spain were subjected to the threats on Tuesday and another flight to Sofia had been threatened a day earlier.
paras.zh: 欧洲至少有七个航班和一艘游轮受到炸弹威胁，造成机场中断，尽管没有发现任何装置。周二，至少有两架飞往华沙的航班、两架飞往索非亚的航班、两架飞往罗马的航班和一架飞往西班牙穆尔西亚机场的航班受到威胁，前一天还有另一架飞往索非亚的航班受到威胁。

paras.en: An airport in Warsaw was briefly shut and the Italian Air Force accompanied one of the flights to Rome, while an Israel-bound cruise ship was searched for bombs in Greece.
paras.zh: 华沙的一个机场被短暂关闭，意大利空军陪同其中一架飞往罗马的航班，而一艘前往以色列的游轮在希腊被搜查炸弹。

paras.en: Authorities diverted a LOT flight from London that was meant to land at Warsaw’s Chopin airport to nearby Modlin airport, which was closed and then reopened after the plane was searched and no device was found. Another Warsaw-bound flight, an SAS flight from Copenhagen, landed at Chopin as scheduled. Chopin airport said no device was found and the airport remained operational.
paras.zh: 当局将从伦敦降落在华沙肖邦机场的许多航班转移到附近的莫德林机场，该机场在搜查飞机后被关闭，然后重新开放，没有发现任何装置。另一个飞往华沙的航班，从哥本哈根起飞的SAS航班，如期降落在肖邦。肖邦机场表示，没有发现任何设备，机场仍在运营。

paras.en: Bomb threats were made against planes traveling from Milan/Bergamo and Dublin to Sofia, Bulgaria’s transport ministry said in a statement to Reuters. Both landed safely and no explosive devices were found on inspection.

The Bergamo flight was operated by Wizz Air and was carrying 176 passengers, the statement said. The Dublin flight, operated by Ryanair, had 186 passengers on board. Bulgarian news agency BTA had earlier quoted an interior ministry official as saying a flight from Israel had been affected, but authorities later said this was not the case.

In Murcia in southeastern Spain, parts of an airport were cordoned off after a bomb threat was reported on a Ryanair flight from Manchester. Officials said the report proved to be a hoax, and the airport resumed normal operations after authorities found no explosives on board.

Two other Ryanair flights - one from Lisbon and another from Dublin - were searched at Rome’s Fiumicino airport following bomb threats, said a source from airport operator ADR. The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until it landed. The alert was cleared and the airport continued to operate as usual with no effects on other flights, the person said.

An explosives detection dog and a diver searched the Panama-flagged Crown Iris cruise ship on the Greek island of Syros after an unknown person said an explosive device had been attached to the boat’s hull, authorities said. Initial checks found no explosive device with coast guard specialists expected to carry out further inspections before the ship could resume its voyage.

Meanwhile, Czech public media workers went on a one-day strike to protest a government plan to overhaul how public broadcasters are funded. The legislation, led by populist billionaire turned prime minister Andrej Babiš, has been criticised as threatening the independence of the media organisations.

Russia bombarded Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in waves on Tuesday, knocking out power to swathes of the country with dozens of missiles and hundreds of drones, a week before US-brokered peace talks were due to resume.

At a press conference in Berlin with German chancellor Friedrich Merz, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack showed that Moscow was intent on killing people instead of building on the humanitarian ceasefire in and around Oleshky.

Merz warned thatthe outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.” He said Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.

The European Commission will host a meeting regarding Ukraine with representatives from the United States, Ukraine and its key European allies on Wednesday, Commission spokesperson Paula Pinho said. “So tomorrow the European Commission will host a meeting with representatives from Ukraine, from the United States, France, Germany, the UK, Nato and the World Bank and this meeting will build on earlier talks that took place in Miami,” Pinho told reporters in Brussels.
Bomb threat prompts checks on Israel-bound cruise ship in Greek port

A bomb threat to an Israel-bound cruise ship prompted a security operation at the Greek island port of Syros after an unknown person claimed an explosive device had been attached to its hull, Greek authorities said.
The Panama-flagged Crown Iris was due to sail to Haifa carrying 940 passengers and 597 crew members when the threat was received, Reuters reported.
Coast guard personnel assisted by an explosives detection dog and a private diver searched the vessel, while a special coast guard unit was deployed to the scene.
Initial checks found no explosive device. Coast guard specialists are expected to arrive at 9.30pm (7.30pm GMT) to carry out further inspections before the ship can resume its voyage.
Czech public media workers strike over government plan to overhaul funding
Here are some images from earlier today as Czech public media workers went on a one-day strike to protest a government plan to overhaul how public broadcasters are funded.

The legislation, led by populist billionaire turned prime minister Andrej Babiš, has been criticised as threatening the independence of the media organisations. The plan led to street protests in Prague last month.

Under the plan, the country’s public radio and television would be financed from the state budget, not from an existing system of regular fees from individuals, households and businesses. The media would receive about 15% less money than they do now, which could likely lead to staff layoffs, limited production and program cancellations.

Critics say the overhaul would give the ruling three-party coalition the means to take control of the media, similar to what populist governments did in Slovakia under prime minister Robert Fico and in Hungary before former prime minister Viktor Orbán was ousted from power in April.
Michal Kubal, chief news editor at Czech Television, said the strike today is unprecedented in the history of Czech public service media.
On their TV screens, Czech residents on Tuesday saw an announcement saying:
We are doing everything we can to ensure that we can continue to provide a public service in its full scope and quality in the future.
The UK government confirmed that two of the planes affected had departed from British airports.

The UK has one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we’ve seen today.
Our world-leading police and intelligence agencies work closely every day to keep us safe, using the tools they have to assess and respond to potential threats.
Bulgaria confirms bomb threats against flights from Bergamo, Dublin, not Israel

There is also an update from Bulgaria, with the country’s transport ministry telling Reuters the bomb threats were actually made against two planes from Bergamo in Italy and Dublin in Ireland, and not from Israel as previously reported.
That brings the total to seven planes (that we know of).
Back to Berlin, Ukraine’s Zelenskyy also rejects Russia’s suggestion of a meeting in Moscow as “counterproductive.” He says what’s needed is serious talks, and not a gimmick.
He also insists that Russia has no advantage on the frontline at the moment.
Merz then adds that the 19 November meeting will decide further support for Ukraine in 2027, and that concludes the press.
Two false bomb threats reported on Italy-bound Ryanair flights

Meanwhile, two more false bomb threats were reported in Italy involving Ryanair flights from Lisbon and Dublin to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport, according to the Italian newspapers La Repubblica and Corriere della Sera.
The plane from Dublin was escorted by two Italian air force fighter jets, newspaper reported.
In both cases, routine checks were confirmed as negative, meaning no threat was identified, SkyTG24 said.
That brings the total of flights affected by false alarms today to at least six, up from four reported earlier (that we know of).
Security guarantees, Ukraine reconstructions, energy and Black Sea truce to be discussed in Abu Dhabi, Zelenskyy says

Asked about his expectations for the Abu Dhabi talks, Zelenskyy says he hopes to see future security guarantees for Ukraine to be covered, alongside a “prosperity package” that would help with the reconstruction of Ukraine.
He also says he hopes to discuss a proposal on energy, Black Sea truce, which is “in the interest of not only Ukraine, but also Russia and various nations in Africa.”
He reiterates that “there can be no stable peace unless Europe is at the negotiating table.”
Merz for his part says that “it is crucial for Russia to finally engage in serious negotiations.”
Europe remains 'crucial' for ending the war in Ukraine, Zelenskyy says, as he confirms Abu Dhabi talks

Responding, Zelenskyy thanks Germany for its continued help, including on air defence, and says that while many people will be following the events in the US today’s midterm elections, “the role of Europe – and specifically Germany – remains crucial.”
He says he briefed Merz on the latest attacks on Ukraine.
He also confirms the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks on 10-11 November (11:21), which he says hopefully “will pave the way for a trilateral meeting at the level of heads of states and government.”

He also confirms further talks on Ukraine will be held in Brussels on Wednesday (12:41), as per the European Commission’s announcement earlier, and that the coalition of the willing will meet in Berlin on 19 November.
Merz declares Germany will keep supporting Ukraine as he warns about Russia's attacks, impact of Black Sea strikes on food security
Germany’s Merz begins by saying Zelenskyy’s visit comes “at a critical moment” as Russian attacks on Ukraine continued with “undiminished – indeed, increasing – severity and ruthlessness.”
He says Ukraine “can continue to rely on Germany,” with more support from Berlin in the coming months, including on air defence, energy, and broader winter-related aid.
Merz also warns that the outcome of the war in Ukraine “will determine European security for a long time to come.”
He says Germany will be coordinating with France and the UK, and will host a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin later this month.

The German chancellor also talks of growing concerns about the broader effects of the continuing war, including a potential “global food crisis” triggered by Russia’s continued attacks on trading routes in the Black Sea.
He says the upcoming Abu Dhabi talks are “the right step forward,” and Europe hopes to play its part.
In the meantime, Berlin and partners will “increase the pressure on Moscow and continue to support Ukraine,” he says.

articles.title: Death toll rises in Ukraine after Russia attacks aid centre, hospice and hospital

paras.en: Russian strikes on Ukraine â including on an aid centre, a hospice and a hospital â have killed at least 38 civilians and injured scores of others over the last 24 hours.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯对乌克兰的袭击--包括对援助中心、临终关怀中心和医院的袭击--在过去24小时内造成至少38名平民死亡，数十人受伤。

paras.en: At least 33 people are known to have died in a glide bomb attack in the southern Zaporizhzhia region on Monday night, and President Volodymyr Zelensky said the number of victims was set to rise as more than 50 people could be trapped under the rubble.
paras.zh: 周一晚上，已知至少有33人在Zaporizhzhia南部地区的滑翔弹袭击中丧生，总统Volodymyr Zelensky表示，受害者人数将增加，因为可能有50多人被困在瓦砾下。

paras.en: He called the strike in Komyshuvakha village "one of the largest mass killings committed by Russia during this war".
paras.zh: 他称Komyshuvakha村的罢工是“俄罗斯在这场战争期间犯下的最大规模的大规模杀戮之一”。

paras.en: Ukraine had proposed to extend and expand last week's ceasefire in the Kherson region which allowed people from the frontline Russian-occupied town of Oleshky to evacuate, Zelensky added.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基补充说，乌克兰已提议延长和扩大上周在赫尔松地区的停火，该停火允许来自俄罗斯占领的前线城镇奥列什基的人们撤离。

paras.en: The attack on a school building being used as an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha was Moscow's response, he said.
paras.zh: 他说，对Komyshuvakha用作援助配送中心的学校建筑的袭击是莫斯科的回应。

paras.en: Elsewhere, a hospice was attacked in the central city of Dnipro and a hospital was hit in the north-eastern city of Kharkiv, where Zelensky said 73 people were wounded, most of them elderly patients.
paras.zh: 在其他地方，第聂伯罗市中心的一家临终关怀医院遭到袭击，东北部城市哈尔科夫的一家医院遭到袭击，泽伦斯基说， 73人受伤，其中大多数是老年患者。

paras.en: Nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit Komyshuvakha as residents were gathering to receive humanitarian aid at a distribution centre, authorities said. Local media reported that when the attack began, people took refuge underground but the roof collapsed, trapping many underneath.
paras.zh: 当局表示， 9枚3000公斤的空中炸弹袭击了Komyshuvakha ，当时居民正在一个配送中心聚集接受人道主义援助。当地媒体报道，袭击开始时，人们在地下避难，但屋顶坍塌，许多人被困在下面。

paras.en: "The scale of the tragedy is difficult to comprehend," regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
paras.zh: “这场悲剧的规模很难理解，”区域负责人Mykhailo Semikin说。

paras.en: Russia's defense ministry said the attack had targeted Ukrainian military units and killed 25 servicemen.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯国防部表示，这次袭击的目标是乌克兰军队，造成25名军人死亡。

paras.en: However, there was no credible evidence that the site was being used by the Ukrainian military and there were no major military or industrial facilities in the settlement of Komyshuvakha, reports BBC News Russian defence correspondent Ilya Abishev.
paras.zh: 然而，据英国广播公司新闻俄罗斯国防记者伊利亚·阿比舍夫（ Ilya Abishev ）报道，没有可靠的证据表明乌克兰军方正在使用该地点， Komyshuvakha定居点没有主要的军事或工业设施。

paras.en: The village is to the south-east of the city of Zaporizhzhia, which has come under constant Russian bombardment.
paras.zh: 这个村庄位于扎波罗热市的东南部，该市一直受到俄罗斯的轰炸。

paras.en: According to Abishev, Komyshuvakha is of high military importance as part of Ukraine's defensive and transport network on the approaches to the regional capital.
paras.zh: 根据Abishev的说法， Komyshuvakha作为乌克兰通往该地区首都的防御和运输网络的一部分具有高度的军事重要性。

paras.en: But the UN's human rights monitoring mission said the distribution of humanitarian aid at the local school had been highly publicised and the attack "seems to have violated the most fundamental principles of international humanitarian law", external.
paras.zh: 但联合国人权监察团表示，当地学校的人道主义援助分发已经得到高度宣传，这次袭击“似乎违反了国际人道主义法最基本的原则”。

paras.en: Further north, in Dnipro, nearly 50 terminally ill patients were being transferred to other facilities after their hospice was destroyed by a Russian missile on Monday night. The oldest of the patients was 90 years old.
paras.zh: 再往北，在第聂伯罗，周一晚上，近50名临终病人被俄罗斯导弹摧毁，他们被转移到其他设施。最年长的患者为90岁。

paras.en: Mayor Boris Filatov posted photos on Telegram showing elderly people lying in their beds in a hospice room with blown-out windows and rubble and broken glass strewn on the floors.
paras.zh: 市长鲍里斯·菲拉托夫（ Boris Filatov ）在Telegram上发布了照片，显示老年人躺在临终关怀室的床上，窗户被炸毁，地板上铺满了碎石和碎玻璃。

paras.en: "I realise that I am violating ethics," wrote Filatov. "I want as many people as possible to see these photos. Especially politicians and diplomats. Especially abroad.
paras.zh: Filatov写道： “我意识到我违反了道德规范。” “我希望尽可能多的人看到这些照片。尤其是政客和外交官，尤其是在国外。

paras.en: "These are elderly, terminally ill people. This is a Russian missile."
paras.zh: “这些是老年人，身患绝症。这是俄罗斯的导弹。”

paras.en: Elsewhere in Dnipro, a separate strike killed two people and left 18 others wounded. Another five people were killed in aerial bomb and drone strikes on Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region.
paras.zh: 在第聂伯罗其他地方，另一次袭击造成两人死亡， 18人受伤。另外五人在乌克兰东部顿涅茨克地区的空中炸弹和无人机袭击中丧生。

paras.en: Russia has also struck energy infrastructure in nine regions, affecting water and heating.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯还在九个地区打击了能源基础设施，影响了水和供暖。

paras.en: The water supply in Kyiv was entirely cut off "due to enemy attacks and damage to the capital's energy infrastructure", the main water supplier Kyivvodokanal said. The entire metro network was suspended on Tuesday and Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the situation surrounding the city's power supply was becoming "very difficult".
paras.zh: 主要供水商Kyivvodokanal表示， “由于敌人的袭击和首都能源基础设施的破坏” ，基辅的供水完全被切断。整个地铁网络于周二暂停，市长Vitali Klitschko表示，该市电力供应的情况变得“非常困难”。

paras.en: As Ukraine was counting its dead, the Kremlin announced it would take part in three-way peace talks with Ukraine brokered by the US in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November.
paras.zh: 由于乌克兰正在计算死亡人数，克里姆林宫宣布将参加11月10日至11日由美国在阿布扎比斡旋的与乌克兰的三方和平谈判。

paras.en: It will be the first trilateral meeting since February. Since then, Russia and the US have begun engaging more directly, with US President Donald Trump announcing a deal to import Russian diesel.
paras.zh: 这将是自2月以来的首次三方会议。此后，俄罗斯和美国开始更直接地接触，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普宣布了一项进口俄罗斯柴油的协议。

paras.en: Speaking to reporters in Berlin on Tuesday, Zelensky said that it was important for Russia to engage seriously in negotiations on a ceasefire and a peaceful settlement, but that he had so far had not seen "any indication" of that being the case.
paras.zh: 泽伦斯基周二在柏林对记者说，俄罗斯认真参与停火与和平解决方案的谈判非常重要，但到目前为止，他还没有看到“任何迹象”表明情况确实如此。

paras.en: Several rounds of ceasefire talks late last year yielded no results, and in public declarations Russian officials have generally refused to budge from Moscow's maximalist demand of effective Ukrainian surrender.
paras.zh: 去年年底的几轮停火谈判没有取得任何结果，在公开声明中，俄罗斯官员普遍拒绝让步于莫斯科要求乌克兰有效投降的最大化要求。

paras.en: US First Lady Melania Trump Melania Trump, who was credited with brokering a truce last week in the besieged town of Oleshky, is set to host representatives of Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday. However, no details were given in the White House statement of who was due to attend the meeting., external
paras.zh: 美国第一夫人梅拉尼娅·特朗普（ Melania Trump ）上周在被围困的奥列什基（ Oleshky ）镇促成了休战，她将于周四在白宫接待俄罗斯和乌克兰的代表。然而，白宫声明中没有详细说明谁将出席会议。

paras.en: The UN said last month that civilian casualties in Ukraine had reached a "record level", as Russian armed forces resumed systematic attacks on energy infrastructure.
paras.zh: 联合国上个月表示，随着俄罗斯武装部队恢复对能源基础设施的系统性袭击，乌克兰的平民伤亡人数已达到“创纪录的水平”。

paras.en: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its advances on the front line have since stalled, and attacks on Ukraine have intensified, with Moscow employing large numbers of missiles and drones to strike Ukrainian cities.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯于2022年2月发动了对乌克兰的全面入侵。此后，它在前线的进展停滞不前，对乌克兰的袭击加剧，莫斯科使用大量导弹和无人机袭击乌克兰城市。

paras.en: At the same time, Ukraine is faces a critical air defense shortage due to stalled Western deliveries of weapons and a lack of American Patriot interceptor missiles.
paras.zh: 与此同时，由于西方武器交付停滞和缺乏美国爱国者拦截导弹，乌克兰面临严重的防空短缺。

paras.en: In Berlin, Zelensky acknowledged that although the front line was stable "the situation in the air was not as positive, particularly when it comes to our air defence capabilities and the protection of our civilian population".
paras.zh: 在柏林，泽伦斯基承认，尽管前线是稳定的，但“空中的局势并不那么积极，特别是在我们的防空能力和对平民的保护方面”。

articles.title: Irish Olympian Ciara Mageean was a 'talented and inspirational human being'

paras.en: Olympian Ciara Mageean has been described as a "truly remarkable, immensely talented and inspirational human being" in a tribute read out at her funeral.
paras.zh: 奥运选手Ciara Mageean在她的葬礼上宣读的致敬中被描述为“真正非凡，极具才华和鼓舞人心的人”。

paras.en: Hundreds of people have paid their respects to the runner at her funeral on Tuesday.
paras.zh: 周二，数百人在她的葬礼上向这位跑步者表示敬意。

paras.en: The former European champion and two-time Olympic runner died on Sunday after she was diagnosed with stage four bowel cancer.
paras.zh: 这位前欧洲冠军和两届奥运会选手在被诊断出患有四期肠癌后于周日去世。

paras.en: Among those in attendance at the funeral in Portaferry, County Down, were Northern Ireland First Minister Michelle O'Neill, as well as fellow Olympian Rhys McClenaghan and 1972 gold medallist Lady Mary Peters.
paras.zh: 北爱尔兰首席部长米歇尔·奥尼尔（ Michelle O'Neill ）以及奥运选手里斯·麦克莱纳汉（ Rhys McClenaghan ）和1972年金牌得主玛丽·彼得斯夫人（ Lady Mary Peters ）参加了在唐郡波塔费里（ Portaferry ）举行的葬礼。

paras.en: Mageean's funeral cortege was given a guard of honour by Portaferry GAC and her former school, Assumption Grammar in Ballynahinch.
paras.zh: Mageean的葬礼由Portaferry GAC和她以前的学校Ballynahinch的Assumption Grammar授予荣誉卫士。

paras.en: Her death comes less than three weeks after her marriage to her long-term partner Thomas Moran.
paras.zh: 她与长期伴侣托马斯·莫兰（ Thomas Moran ）结婚后不到三周就去世了。

paras.en: Mourners began arriving at around midday for the 2:00 GMT requiem Mass at St Patrick's Church.
paras.zh: 哀悼者开始在中午左右抵达圣帕特里克教堂，参加格林尼治标准时间2:00的安魂曲弥撒。

paras.en: Family, friends and those wishing to pay their respects followed the funeral cortege the short distance along the Ballyphilip Road from Mageean's family home to the church.
paras.zh: 葬礼结束后，家人、朋友和那些希望表达敬意的人沿着Ballyphilip路从Mageean的家到教堂只有很短的距离。

paras.en: Others in attendance included representatives for Irish President Catherine Connolly and the Irish Government, Social Democratic and Labour Party leader Claire Hanna, GAA President Jarlath Burns and former boxer Paddy Barnes.
paras.zh: 其他与会者包括爱尔兰总统凯瑟琳·康诺利（ Catherine Connolly ）和爱尔兰政府的代表、社会民主党和工党领袖克莱尔·汉纳（ Claire Hanna ）、GAA主席贾拉斯·伯恩斯（ Jarlath Burns ）和前拳击手帕迪·巴恩斯（ Paddy Barn

paras.en: The Mass booklet included an image of Mageean's greatest achievement on the track, the moment she crossed the line at the 2024 European Championships.
paras.zh: 这本弥撒小册子包括马吉恩在2024年欧洲锦标赛上超越界限的那一刻，她在赛道上取得的最大成就的图像。

paras.en: In his homily, Father Martin Kelly, who knew Mageean from her childhood, spoke of her accomplishments, her love for her husband and the joy and pride she had brought to her hometown.
paras.zh: 在讲道中，从小就认识马吉恩的马丁·凯利神父谈到了她的成就、她对丈夫的爱以及她给家乡带来的快乐和自豪。

paras.en: Kelly recalled visiting her in hospice shortly before her death, when she suggested they go for a walk.
paras.zh: 凯利回忆起在她去世前不久去临终关怀医院看望她的经历，当时她建议他们去散步。

paras.en: Despite her illness, Mageean noticed he was struggling and offered to link arms with him.
paras.zh: 尽管Mageean生病了，但她注意到他正在挣扎，并主动提出将双臂与他联系起来。

paras.en: "On the way down, she knew I was struggling and she said, 'Let me link you'," he told mourners.
paras.zh: “在下山的路上，她知道我在挣扎，她说， '让我联系你' ，”他告诉哀悼者。

paras.en: "One of my happiest moments and memories is that of Ciara Mageean linking my arm as we walked back to her room."
paras.zh: “我最开心的时刻和回忆之一是，当我们走回她的房间时， Ciara Mageean挽着我的胳膊。”

paras.en: The athlete represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Olympics and won gold in the 1500m at the European Athletics Championships in Rome in 2024.
paras.zh: 这位运动员代表爱尔兰参加了2016年和2020年奥运会，并于2024年在罗马举行的欧洲田径锦标赛上获得了1500米金牌。

paras.en: She also represented Northern Ireland at the Commonwealth Games, winning silver in Birmingham in 2022.
paras.zh: 她还代表北爱尔兰参加了英联邦运动会，并于2022年在伯明翰赢得了银牌。

paras.en: Noticing blood in your poo - which may appear black or dark red in the toilet bowl - can be a sign of bowel cancer.
paras.zh: 注意到大便中的血液（马桶中可能呈黑色或深红色）可能是肠癌的征兆。

paras.en: If there is no other obvious cause for the bleeding, such as piles, the NHS recommends that you ask for an appointment with your GP, external.
paras.zh: 如果没有其他明显的出血原因，如桩， NHS建议您要求预约您的全科医生，外部。

paras.en: The NHS also advises a check-up if you notice changes in your regular toilet habits, such as having to poo more often, or a pattern of diarrhoea or constipation.
paras.zh: 如果您注意到常规厕所习惯的变化，例如不得不更频繁地大便，或腹泻或便秘的模式， NHS还建议您进行检查。

paras.en: Abdominal pain or lumps, stomach bloating and unexplained weight loss are also among symptoms which should lead to a bowel cancer test.
paras.zh: 腹痛或肿块、胃胀和不明原因的体重减轻也是应该导致肠癌测试的症状之一。

paras.en: Bowel cancer can also cause anaemia, the features of which include extreme tiredness and shortness of breath.
paras.zh: 肠癌也可能导致贫血，其特征包括极度疲劳和呼吸急促。

paras.en: The earlier bowel cancer is detected, the easier it is to treat.
paras.zh: 发现的肠癌越早，治疗就越容易。

articles.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats

paras.en: Seven passenger planes across Europe, two of which departed from the UK, have been inspected following a series of suspected bomb threats.
paras.zh: 在一系列可疑的炸弹威胁之后，已经检查了欧洲各地的七架客机，其中两架从英国起飞。

paras.en: Two Ryanair flights, one originating from Dublin and the other from Lisbon, were searched after landing in Rome following anonymous tips but no explosives were found, sources at the city's Fiumicino airport told the BBC.
paras.zh: 两架瑞安航空公司的航班，一架从都柏林起飞，另一架从里斯本起飞，在匿名提示下降落在罗马后被搜查，但没有发现爆炸物，该市菲乌米奇诺机场的消息人士告诉英国广播公司。

paras.en: The Dublin flight was escorted by the Italian Air Force until landing. Authorities have also searched planes in Poland, Spain and Bulgaria.
paras.zh: 都柏林航班由意大利空军护航，直至降落。当局还在波兰、西班牙和保加利亚搜查了飞机。

paras.en: While officially there is no link between them, authorities from various countries will be co-operating to assess whether this was a co-ordinated attack, designed to disrupt airspace.
paras.zh: 虽然两国之间没有正式的联系，但各国当局将合作评估这是否是旨在破坏领空的协同攻击。

paras.en: The UK government described today's incidents as "malicious hoax threats".
paras.zh: 英国政府将今天的事件描述为“恶意恶作剧威胁”。

paras.en: In a statement it said it had "one of the most robust aviation security systems in the world, with well-tested processes for dealing with any potential threats, as well as malicious hoax threats, like those we've seen today".
paras.zh: 该公司在一份声明中表示，它拥有“世界上最强大的航空安全系统之一，拥有经过充分测试的流程来应对任何潜在威胁，以及恶意恶作剧威胁，就像我们今天看到的那样”。

paras.en: Aviation security expert Paul Mason said bomb threats on passenger planes "don't happen that frequently", which made the latest incidents "unusual".
paras.zh: 航空安全专家保罗·梅森（ Paul Mason ）表示，客机上的炸弹威胁“不会频繁发生” ，这使得最新的事件“不寻常”。

paras.en: "It sounds like they've been made in a credible manner across a broad range of airlines," Mason told BBC Radio 5 Live. "That would suggest to me that it's been a very deliberate act by a typical actor rather than a load of coincidental, malicious calls."
paras.zh: 梅森告诉BBC Radio 5 Live ： “这听起来像是在各种航空公司以可信的方式制作的。” “这向我表明，这是一个典型的演员非常刻意的行为，而不是一堆巧合的恶意电话。”

paras.en: He said "there are a lot of processes" that the onboard crew and people on the ground must go through "to validate the credibility of the threat".
paras.zh: 他说， “有很多过程” ，船上人员和地面人员必须经历“验证威胁的可信度”。

paras.en: A flight may be asked to divert if the credibility of a threat "is of a certain level", Mason added, and in some cases the onboard crew may not even be advised on what the ground operators were dealing with.
paras.zh: Mason补充说，如果威胁的可信度“达到一定水平” ，可能会要求航班转向，在某些情况下，甚至可能不会告知机上机组人员地面操作员正在处理什么。

paras.en: In Rome, sources at Fiumicino airport told the BBC police bomb disposal experts carried out standard security protocols to ensure the safety of all passengers and crew.
paras.zh: 在罗马，菲乌米奇诺机场的消息人士告诉英国广播公司警察炸弹处理专家，他们执行了标准的安全协议，以确保所有乘客和机组人员的安全。

paras.en: Inspections of the passengers, luggage, and the aircraft yielded negative results, and the alert has since been cleared.
paras.zh: 对乘客、行李和飞机的检查产生了负面结果，警报已被清除。

paras.en: One plane which landed in Murcia, southern Spain - a Ryanair flight coming from Manchester - was also found not to have any explosives on board, Spanish authorities said.
paras.zh: 西班牙当局表示，一架降落在西班牙南部穆尔西亚的飞机--一架来自曼彻斯特的瑞安航空公司的航班--也被发现没有携带任何爆炸物。

paras.en: One passenger later said she was unaware of the bomb threat until after the plane landed.
paras.zh: 一名乘客后来说，直到飞机降落后，她才意识到炸弹的威胁。

paras.en: "We weren't told anything during the flight," Sarah told BBC Radio 5 Live. "The plane stopped quite suddenly and then we were kept on the runway for around 30 minutes."
paras.zh: “我们在飞行期间没有被告知任何事情，” Sarah告诉BBC Radio 5 Live。“飞机突然停了下来，然后我们在跑道上停了大约30分钟。”

paras.en: "Then the fire engines turned up, the bomb squad turned up and we were asked to evacuate," she continues.
paras.zh: “然后消防车出现了，拆弹小组出现了，我们被要求撤离，”她继续说道。

paras.en: Sarah said the plane had not been on the ground a minute before it was "surrounded by fire engines and police and a bomb squad". All the passengers were then escorted by police, leaving all their belongings.
paras.zh: 莎拉说，这架飞机在“被消防车、警察和拆弹小组包围”前一分钟还没有降落在地面上。然后，所有乘客都被警察护送，留下了他们所有的物品。

paras.en: "We were only later told that it was an actual threat, a bomb threat to the plane itself," she added.
paras.zh: 她补充说： “我们后来才被告知，这是一个实际的威胁，是对飞机本身的炸弹威胁。”

paras.en: Two flights heading to Warsaw were also affected, including one from London Heathrow.
paras.zh: 两架飞往华沙的航班也受到影响，其中一架从伦敦希思罗机场起飞。

paras.en: The Heathrow flight was originally meant to land at the Polish capital's main airport, Chopin, but was diverted instead to the smaller Modlin airport, briefly forcing its closure.
paras.zh: 希思罗机场的航班原本打算降落在波兰首都肖邦的主要机场，但被改道到较小的莫德林机场，短暂迫使其关闭。

paras.en: A Scandinavian Airlines flight from Copenhagen to Warsaw-Chopin landed as planned.
paras.zh: 斯堪的纳维亚航空公司从哥本哈根飞往华沙-肖邦的航班按计划降落。

paras.en: Later on Tuesday, Bulgarian Transport Minister Georgi Peev said there were bomb threats against two planes travelling to the country's capital Sofia.
paras.zh: 周二晚些时候，保加利亚交通部长乔治·皮耶夫（ Georgi Peev ）表示，两架飞往该国首都索非亚的飞机受到炸弹威胁。

paras.en: He told the state-owned Bulgarian News Agency (BTA) the flights were from the northern Italian city of Bergamo and Ireland's capital Dublin.
paras.zh: 他告诉国有的保加利亚通讯社（ BTA ） ，这些航班来自意大利北部城市贝加莫和爱尔兰首都都柏林。

paras.en: The flights into Sofia were not diverted and no explosives were found when the planes were checked, Peev said.
paras.zh: Peev说，在检查飞机时，飞往索非亚的航班没有被转移，也没有发现爆炸物。

paras.en: Bulgaria's border police said in a statement sent to the BBC that at around 10:35 (08:35 GMT) it had received an email about "the presence of an improvised explosive device on a flight returning from Bergamo".
paras.zh: 保加利亚边境警察在发给英国广播公司的一份声明中说，大约在10:35 （格林威治标准时间08:35 ） ，它收到了一封关于“从贝加莫返回的航班上存在简易爆炸装置”的电子邮件。

paras.en: "Standard procedures for such incidents were immediately activated, and an operational headquarters comprising representatives of various institutions was convened," the statement said.
paras.zh: 声明说： “立即启动了此类事件的标准程序，并召集了由各机构代表组成的运营总部。”

paras.en: The border police added that the same email also reported a "similar threat against aircraft arriving from Dublin".
paras.zh: 边境警察补充说，同一封电子邮件还报告了“对从都柏林抵达的飞机的类似威胁”。

paras.en: These incidents come a day after a Wizz Air flight from London Luton made an emergency landing in Budapest, escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet, after a bomb threat.
paras.zh: 这些事件发生的前一天，一架来自伦敦卢顿的Wizz Air航班在受到炸弹威胁后，在一架匈牙利战斗机的护送下紧急降落在布达佩斯。

paras.en: Wizz Air said later that security checks had been made and nothing was found.
paras.zh: Wizz Air后来说，已经进行了安全检查，但没有发现任何东西。

paras.en: BBC Verify has consulted aviation safety experts about what happens on board a plane when a bomb threat is issued.
paras.zh: BBC Verify咨询了航空安全专家，了解在发出炸弹威胁时飞机上会发生什么。

paras.en: Marco Chan, a former pilot for Cathay Pacific Airways and Hong Kong Airlines who is now a senior lecturer in aviation operations at Kingston University, said a bomb threat is considered "genuine until it is resolved, even though most turn out to be hoaxes".
paras.zh: 前国泰航空和香港航空飞行员、现任金斯敦大学航空业务高级讲师的马可·陈（ Marco Chan ）表示，炸弹威胁“在得到解决之前被认为是真实的，尽管事实证明大多数都是恶作剧”。

paras.en: Chan said crews will "quietly search" toilets, galleys and storage areas and will not touch a suspicious item unless it has to be taken to an area on the aircraft designated as the least risky bomb location.
paras.zh: 陈说，工作人员将“悄悄搜查”厕所，厨房和存储区域，除非必须将可疑物品带到飞机上指定的风险最低的炸弹位置，否则不会触摸可疑物品。

paras.en: The aircraft's captain will have multiple factors to assess, according to former airline pilot Terry Tozer, an aviation safety commentator.
paras.zh: 根据前航空公司飞行员、航空安全评论员特里·托泽（ Terry Tozer ）的说法，这架飞机的机长将有多个因素需要评估。

paras.en: He said these include what facilities are available at the airport they are being diverted to and how the plane can continue onwards should it turn out to be a false threat.
paras.zh: 他说，这些包括他们被转移到的机场有哪些设施，以及如果飞机被证明是虚假的威胁，如何继续前进。

paras.en: Chan added that once on the ground, the plane is generally "taken to an isolated stand, passengers are disembarked, and police and bomb disposal teams search it".
paras.zh: 陈补充说，一旦降落在地面上，飞机通常会“被带到一个孤立的站台，乘客下船，警察和炸弹处理小组对其进行搜查”。

paras.en: Additional reporting by Thomas Copeland, BBC Verify
paras.zh: BBC Verify Thomas Copeland的补充报道

articles.title: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

paras.en: New Facility Brings Off-Highway Wet Friction Production to India

Carlisle Brake & Friction has broken ground to expand its Chennai, India manufacturing operations in one of the world’s fastest-growing industrial regions. Having produced mechatronic products in the region for more than 15 years, Carlisle CBF will relocate to add production at a larger site for off-highway paper wet friction discs and steel separator plates. The new facility is scheduled to open in 2027.

The move to expanded space is designed to accommodate manufacturing capabilities needed to serve the growing demand across the agriculture, construction and especially mining industries in India and Southeast Asia. Local production will improve supply chain responsiveness while supporting original equipment and aftermarket requirements in cost-sensitive markets.

Carlisle Brake & Friction is establishing a state-of-the-art wet friction manufacturing facility on par with proven global manufacturing processes in the new Chennai plant, to build a more resilient regional platform. This expansion strengthens our ability to deliver durable wet friction products that help keep critical off-highway equipment productive.

articles.title: One Game at a Time: Lessons from the Sports World for Auto Body Shops
articles.author: Jason Stahl

paras.en: You hear it all the time in sports: we’re taking it one game at a time. This week, we’re 1-0, and next week starts a new week, and we’re hoping to go 1-0 again.

Why are coaches and athletes so hyper-focused on the game at hand, not worrying about the last game or any future game? “Our focus is on [their next opponent’s team name].” If they lost the last game badly, not worrying about it but washing it away and wiping the slate clean. If they won the last game by a wide margin, not getting too proud of themselves lest they feel they’re invincible and give less effort the next game.

Sounds a little to me like “staying in the present” or staying in the moment. Which I think is a little different in that it relates to the philosophy of living. For example, I heard someone say a good way to slow down time is to stay in the present — something altogether different than what I was talking about with sports.

But I think this “one game a time” attitude in sports has some business lessons. Have a bad quarter profit-wise? Let’s kill it the next quarter. Last week’s vehicles have been delivered, and there were some hiccups. What can we do this week to avoid those same bumps in the road? Let’s not fixate on why Ms. McGillicuddy was fuming about her car last week but learn from our mistakes so we don’t make another customer mad. Not get too high over our successes or too low over our failures but plod ahead with the same workman-like attitude to do the best job we can. One vehicle at a time, one customer at a time, the highest quality job we can do each time.

articles.title: How Active Safety Systems Decide When to Intervene
articles.author: Jason Morgan

paras.en: At GM’s Milford Proving Ground, GM Fleet gave an up-close look at how active safety technologies are developed and how they determine when a driver needs assistance. When an automatic emergency braking system responds to a hazard, the braking event may feel instantaneous. Behind that response is a continuous process of identifying objects, measuring risk and determining whether the driver is already taking action.

Radar played an early role in adaptive cruise control and forward collision alerts. It can detect objects and measure their movement, but it does not always know exactly what it sees. A small object can sometimes produce a significant radar target.
Adding cameras gave the system another source of information.

Once the camera and radar information is matched, the system calculates distance and closing speed. It also considers what the driver is doing. Brake and accelerator inputs can indicate whether the driver recognizes the situation. If the vehicle is approaching a target but the driver is already braking, the system may determine that the driver is aware.

Lane-keeping systems have followed a similar path of refinement. Early versions could push a vehicle away from one lane marker and toward the other. Improvements in camera resolution, lane detection and calibration have made the response smoother and closer to lane centering. Steering torque also helps the system recognize when the driver is intentionally changing lanes.

For fleet managers, these technologies should be evaluated as connected systems. Cameras, radar, braking, steering and software all contribute to the response, with the driver remaining central to how the system performs.

articles.title: The Best Ways to Communicate in the Alignment Bay
articles.author: Christian Hinton

paras.en: You can have the best alignment rack, sensors and software in town. But poor alignment communication can still affect the results.
So, how can service advisors and technicians can improve communication in the alignment bay?
Alignment Communication Starts With the Repair Order
Never hand a technician a repair order that only says, “customer requests alignment” or “perform alignment.”

The repair order should explain why the customer believes the vehicle needs an alignment. Maybe the vehicle pulls or the steering wheel is off-center. The customer may have noticed uneven tire wear. Suspension parts also may have been replaced, or the vehicle may have hit something in the road.
Those details matter because an alignment is not always the complete answer. The technician needs enough information to inspect the right areas and understand what the customer expects.

That starts with listening. Ask open-ended questions like, “What are you noticing?” or “What does it feel like?” These questions give customers room to describe the problem without steering them toward a specific diagnosis.
Sometimes, the best thing a service advisor can do is stay quiet and let the customer keep talking.
Tell customers what the alignment does and what the technician will check or adjust. Explain how the service benefits the vehicle.

Avoid overwhelming customers with a long technical explanation. Customers do not need a lecture on alignment angles. They need to know that you understand the problem and have a clear plan to correct it. Good alignment communication builds trust and gives technicians better information. It also helps prevent comebacks.
