paras.zh: David Yurman 对众星云集的节日活动并不陌生，因此，就在 11 月日历敲响之际，该奢侈品牌推出了 2026 年礼品季的最新款式。 《Obsession》的 Inde Navarrette 和 Bridgerton 的 Yerin Ha 与奥斯卡金像奖获奖演员兼 David Yurman 全球品牌大使 Michael B. Jordan 一起参与了这一名为“分享温暖”的电影季节性广告活动，该活动在整个白雪皑皑的城市中拍摄了一系列典型的纽约小插曲。

paras.en: Of course, the trio is adorned in some of the brand’s most striking designs — a combination of new releases and recognizable DY favorites. The campaign video and imagery, unveiled Monday, Nov. 2 on DavidYurman.com, are accompanied by a collection of curated holiday gift guides, organized by price, style and recipient: gifts for her, gifts for him, symbolic gifts, classic gifts, statement gifts and so on.
paras.zh: 当然，这三款产品采用了该品牌一些最引人注目的设计——新发布的产品和广受认可的 DY 最爱的组合。该活动视频和图像于 11 月 2 日星期一在 DavidYurman.com 上发布，并附有一系列精心策划的节日礼物指南，按价格、款式和收件人进行组织：给她的礼物、给他的礼物、象征性礼物、经典礼物、个性礼物等。

paras.en: “Recognized for their distinct creative perspectives and culture-defining performances in 2026, Navarette and Ha embody David Yurman’s unwavering commitment to individuality and self-expression,” reads the accompanying campaign material. “Having captivated audiences with powerful portrayals of complex, culturally resonant characters, all three talents demonstrate a dedication to craft and artistic excellence that reflects David Yurman’s rich heritage and enduring values.”
paras.zh: “Navarette 和 Ha 因其独特的创意视角和 2026 年文化定义表演而受到认可，体现了 David Yurman 对个性和自我表达的坚定承诺，”随附的活动材料中写道。 “这三位天才通过对复杂、具有文化共鸣​​的角色的有力描绘吸引了观众，他们都表现出了对工艺和卓越艺术的奉献精神，反映了大卫·雅曼丰富的遗产和持久的价值观。”

paras.en: David Yurman’s 2026 holiday campaign was directed by Bradford Young and photographed by Drew Vickers. The full campaign debuts Nov. 2 on David Yurman’s website and social channels. Visit DavidYurman.com to shop the full gifting assortment, and see a few more standouts below.
paras.zh: David Yurman 的 2026 年假日宣传活动由 Bradford Young 执导，Drew Vickers 掌镜。完整的活动将于 11 月 2 日在 David Yurman 的网站和社交渠道上首次亮相。请访问 DavidYurman.com 购买全套礼品品类，并查看下面更多精选产品。

paras.en: David Yurman Sculpted Cable Flex Bracelet
paras.zh: David Yurman 雕刻电缆弯曲手链

paras.en: Available in classic white, yellow and rose gold with colorless diamonds, plus rose gold with cognac diamonds and black rhodium with black diamonds.
paras.zh: 有经典的白金、黄金和玫瑰金（镶无色钻石）、玫瑰金（镶白兰地钻石）和黑铑（镶黑钻石）可供选择。

articles.title: A Royal Surprise: ‘The Remarried Empress’ Releases One Day Early on Disney+ and Hulu
articles.author: Patrick Brzeski

paras.en: In a surprise gift to fans, Disney+ and Hulu are moving up the royal arrival of The Remarried Empress, bringing the lavish Korean fantasy romance to viewers Nov. 3, one day ahead of its previously announced premiere.
paras.zh: 作为给粉丝的一份惊喜礼物，Disney+ 和 Hulu 提前预告了《再婚皇后》的皇家到来，将这部奢华的韩国奇幻爱情片于 11 月 3 日（比之前宣布的首播提前一天）为观众带来。

paras.en: Stars Shin Min-a, Ju Ji-hoon, Lee Jong-suk and Lee Se-young revealed the change Tuesday at a press conference in Seoul. The first four episodes will be available at launch, with Disney describing the early release as a thank you to fans for their support.
paras.zh: 明星申敏儿、朱智勋、李钟硕和李世英周二在首尔举行的新闻发布会上透露了这一变化。前四集将在发布时提供，迪士尼称提前发布是为了感谢粉丝的支持。

paras.en: The rest of the 10-episode series’ rollout remains unchanged: Two new episodes will arrive each Wednesday beginning Nov. 11, with the final pair streaming Nov. 25.
paras.zh: 这部 10 集剧集的其余部分保持不变：从 11 月 11 日开始每周三播出两集新剧，最后两集将于 11 月 25 日播出。

paras.en: Based on the hit Naver Webtoon, The Remarried Empress combines palace intrigue, romantic betrayal and an impossibly elegant heroine determined to claim her own future. Shin plays Navier, the empress of the Eastern Empire, whose marriage unravels when her husband, Emperor Sovieshu (Ju), falls for escaped slave girl Rashta (Lee Se-young). Navier agrees to his request for a divorce on one condition: She must be permitted to marry her own budding love — Crown Prince Heinrey (Lee Jong-suk) of the rival Western Kingdom.
paras.zh: 改编自热门网络漫画《再婚皇后》，结合了宫廷阴谋、浪漫的背叛和一位决心夺取自己未来的优雅得难以置信的女主角。申饰演东帝国皇后纳维尔，当她的丈夫索维舒皇帝（朱饰）爱上逃亡女奴拉什塔（李世英饰）时，她的婚姻破裂了。纳维尔同意他的离婚请求，但有一个条件：必须允许她嫁给自己的新欢——竞争对手西方王国的王储海因里（李钟硕饰）。

paras.en: The series was adapted for the screen by Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol and directed by Cho Suwon, whose credits include Still 17 and Pinocchio.
paras.zh: 该剧由 Yeoh Geena 和 Hyun Choongyeol 改编成电影，并由 Cho Suwon 执导，其作品包括《Still 17》和《匹诺曹》。

paras.en: The early premiere announcement follows the series’ sold-out preview screenings at the Busan International Film Festival in October. According to Disney, the show’s trailer generated more than 13 million views across YouTube and social media platforms in its first 48 hours, while the wildly popular original webtoon on which the show is based has amassed nearly three billion views.
paras.zh: 该剧于 10 月在釜山国际电影节上试映，门票全部售罄，随后宣布提前首映。据迪士尼称，该剧的预告片在播出后的 48 小时内在 YouTube 和社交媒体平台上获得了超过 1300 万次观看，而该剧所依据的广受欢迎的原创网络漫画也获得了近 30 亿次观看。

articles.title: U.S. reportedly strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Vance hopes for ‘negotiated settlement’ with Tehran

paras.en: The U.S. reportedly carried out strikes against Iran on Monday even as Vice President JD Vance expressed hopes of reaching a "negotiated settlement" with Tehran.
paras.zh: 据报道，美国周一对伊朗进行了打击，尽管副总统万斯表示希望与德黑兰达成“谈判解决方案”。

paras.en: America attacked Iran's Qeshm Island on Monday, U.S. officials told The Wall Street Journal, which added that Washington has been carrying out "limited strikes" against the country in recent weeks. The military campaign against Iran has been kept quiet on purpose so as not to signal any intention of major combat escalation, the report said, quoting an unnamed official.
paras.zh: 美国官员告诉《华尔街日报》，美国周一袭击了伊朗的格什姆岛，该报补充说，华盛顿最近几周一直在对该国进行“有限的打击”。报道援引一位未透露姓名的官员的话称，针对伊朗的军事行动一直有意保持沉默，以免表明任何重大战斗升级的意图。

paras.en: Qeshm Island, off Iran's southern coast, is the largest island in the Persian Gulf. Located near the Strait of Hormuz, it has emerged as a potential U.S. target amid reports that anti-ship missiles, mines, drones and attack craft are being kept there in underground tunnels.
paras.zh: 格什姆岛位于伊朗南部海岸附近，是波斯湾最大的岛屿。它位于霍尔木兹海峡附近，有报道称其地下隧道中存放着反舰导弹、水雷、无人机和攻击机，因此它已成为美国的潜在目标。

paras.en: President Donald Trump's administration has been talking down risks of an all-out war with Iran, with Vance being the latest to claim "good progress" in talks with Iran.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统的政府一直在谈论与伊朗爆发全面战争的风险，万斯是最新一个声称与伊朗谈判“取得良好进展”的人。

paras.en: "The president and I both feel really good about the prospect of potentially coming to a negotiated settlement," Vance told CNN on Monday.
paras.zh: 万斯周一告诉美国有线电视新闻网：“总统和我都对通过谈判达成解决方案的前景感到非常满意。”

paras.en: He added, though, that Iranians are "unpredictable" and Trump retains "kinetic and non-kinetic" options against Tehran. Vance said that Washington has not set any deadline for reaching a peace deal with Iran.
paras.zh: 不过，他补充说，伊朗人“不可预测”，特朗普保留了针对德黑兰的“动能和非动能”选项。万斯表示，华盛顿尚未设定与伊朗达成和平协议的最后期限。

paras.en: Trump said earlier Monday that the U.S. had to go to war with Iran to stop the country from having "a nuclear weapon," that "we're not going to allow Iran ever to have a nuclear weapon. And they understand that."
paras.zh: 特朗普周一早些时候表示，美国必须与伊朗开战，以阻止该国拥有“核武器”，“我们不会允许伊朗拥有核武器。他们明白这一点。”

paras.en: Last month, the president had said the U.S. will not attack Iran before the midterm elections, after polls ahead of the ballot showed that support for the war had dwindled, with only 31% of Americans supporting the military action.
paras.zh: 上个月，总统曾表示，美国不会在中期选举前攻击伊朗，因为投票前的民意调查显示，对战争的支持有所下降，只有 31% 的美国人支持军事行动。

paras.en: Trump told Fox News in an interview Monday night that the U.S. had to take a "little detour" to Iran to stop the country from having nuclear weapons.
paras.zh: 特朗普周一晚间接受福克斯新闻采访时表示，美国必须绕道伊朗，以阻止该国拥有核武器。

paras.en: The president said that the U.S. has bombed out all of Iran's potential nuclear power, but he might target Pickaxe Mountain next. Located south of Iran's Natanz enrichment plant, Pickaxe Mountain houses an underground nuclear facility.
paras.zh: 总统表示，美国已经轰炸了伊朗所有潜在的核力量，但他的下一个目标可能是镐山。镐山位于伊朗纳坦兹浓缩工厂以南，拥有一座地下核设施。

paras.en: "We might have to go after Pickaxe, but that's not a big deal," Trump said, adding the U.S. could destroy it in one hour.
paras.zh: 特朗普说：“我们可能不得不追捕镐，但这没什么大不了的。”他补充说，美国可以在一小时内摧毁它。

paras.en: On Nov. 1, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio had also said Trump would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically," and prefers not to use military force.
paras.zh: 11月1日，美国国务卿卢比奥也表示，特朗普希望通过“外交”方式解决伊朗战争，不愿使用武力。

articles.title: Lovable CEO says AI is collapsing barriers to starting a business

paras.en: Lovable CEO says AI is collapsing barriers to starting a business
paras.zh: 可爱的首席执行官表示人工智能正在消除创业障碍

paras.en: AI is making it easier for people to turn an idea into an app, website or even a business — without needing the same level of technical expertise as before.
paras.zh: 人工智能使人们能够更轻松地将想法转化为应用程序、网站甚至业务，而无需像以前那样具备相同水平的技术专业知识。

paras.en: Lovable CEO Anton Osika joins CNBC's Arjun Kharpal to explain how AI-powered software development is changing entrepreneurship, product development and the role of developers. He discusses how Lovable has evolved from a platform for building apps and websites with plain-English prompts into a broader tool for helping entrepreneurs build, run and grow their businesses.
paras.zh: Lovable 首席执行官 Anton Osika 与 CNBC 的 Arjun Kharpal 一起解释人工智能驱动的软件开发如何改变创业、产品开发和开发人员的角色。他讨论了 Lovable 如何从一个用于构建具有简单英语提示的应用程序和网站的平台发展成为一个帮助企业家建立、运营和发展业务的更广泛的工具。

paras.en: They also discuss AI agents, the future of work, competition from the biggest AI labs, regulation and whether Europe can produce the next generation of global AI companies.
paras.zh: 他们还讨论了人工智能代理、工作的未来、来自最大人工智能实验室的竞争、监管以及欧洲是否能够培育出下一代全球人工智能公司。

articles.title: North Korea denies links to Binance hack as researchers trace stolen billions

paras.en: North Korea rejected allegations linking Pyongyang to the estimated $6.3 billion Binance hack, calling the accusation a “grave political provocation,” according to state media.
paras.zh: 据官方媒体报道，朝鲜否认了将平壤与币安遭受的价值 63 亿美元的黑客攻击联系起来的指控，称这一指控是“严重的政治挑衅”。

paras.en: Kim Yo Jong, sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, denounced the FBI's attribution of the attack to North Korea-linked hacking group TraderTraitor, Yohnap reported Tuesday, citing the state-run Korean Central News Agency.
paras.zh: Yohnap 周二援引国营朝鲜中央通讯社报道称，朝鲜领导人金正恩的妹妹金与正谴责联邦调查局将这次袭击归咎于与朝鲜有关的黑客组织 TraderTraitor。

paras.en: Blockchain analytics firms including Elliptic and Chainalysis have also linked the attack and subsequent movement of the stolen funds to North Korea-linked actors.
paras.zh: Elliptic 和 Chainaanalysis 等区块链分析公司也将这次攻击和随后被盗资金的转移与与朝鲜有关的行为者联系起来。

paras.en: "The FBI is trying to brand the DPRK as a 'cyber criminal state', claiming that it obtained information that a hacking organization 'supported' by the DPRK was involved in the incident," Kim said, according to KCNA.
paras.zh: 据朝中社报道，金正恩表示，“联邦调查局正试图将朝鲜列为‘网络犯罪国家’，声称其获得了朝鲜‘支持’的黑客组织参与此次事件的信息。”

paras.en: She accused Washington of misleading international public opinion by portraying cybercrimes around the world as the work of North Korea.
paras.zh: 她指责华盛顿将世界各地的网络犯罪描述为朝鲜所为，从而误导国际舆论。

paras.en: Separately, Binance said Tuesday it would begin progressively reopening withdrawals for additional crypto assets across more networks, expanding its phased restoration of services following last week's hack.
paras.zh: 另外，币安周二表示，将开始在更多网络上逐步重新开放额外加密资产的提现，扩大上周黑客攻击后的分阶段服务恢复。

paras.en: The denial comes as blockchain analytics firms trace billions of dollars in cryptocurrency stolen from Binance through thousands of wallets across multiple blockchains.
paras.zh: 这一否认是在区块链分析公司通过多个区块链的数千个钱包追踪从币安盗取的数十亿美元的加密货币时发出的。

paras.en: Elliptic and Chainalysis said hackers linked to North Korea have used increasingly complex techniques to obscure the trail of the funds.
paras.zh: Elliptic 和 Chainaanalysis 表示，与朝鲜有关的黑客使用越来越复杂的技术来掩盖资金的踪迹。

paras.en: In the first four days after the attack, the hackers used roughly 12,000 wallets across 11 blockchains and conducted more than 40,000 transactions, Elliptic said in a report Monday. The activity appeared highly complex and automated, with an average of one new wallet used every 25 seconds.
paras.zh: Elliptic 在周一的一份报告中表示，在攻击发生后的前四天内，黑客使用了 11 个区块链上的大约 12,000 个钱包，并进行了 40,000 多笔交易。该活动显得高度复杂和自动化，平均每 25 秒就有一个新钱包被使用。

paras.en: Much of the laundering activity initially took place on the Tron blockchain, where stolen funds were distributed across about 7,700 addresses before being moved to Ethereum through cross-chain bridges, according to Elliptic. At least $147 million had been transferred out of Tron through such bridges.
paras.zh: 据 Elliptic 称，大部分洗钱活动最初发生在 Tron 区块链上，被盗资金分布在大约 7,700 个地址上，然后通过跨链桥转移到以太坊。通过此类桥梁，至少 1.47 亿美元已从 Tron 转出。

paras.en: The hackers also used decentralized exchanges to swap stolen stablecoins into cryptocurrencies that cannot be frozen by their issuers, including ether. Elliptic said roughly $786 million in stablecoins was converted before issuers including Tether and Circle froze the remaining assets.
paras.zh: 黑客还利用去中心化交易所将被盗的稳定币兑换成无法被发行人冻结的加密货币，包括以太币。 Elliptic 表示，在 Tether 和 Circle 等发行人冻结剩余资产之前，大约有 7.86 亿美元的稳定币已被转换。

paras.en: The laundering operation has since expanded to other blockchains, including Solana. Chainalysis said North Korea-linked actors had begun a new phase of laundering after moving more than $500 million through intermediary wallets on Tron.
paras.zh: 此后，洗钱活动已扩展到其他区块链，包括 Solana。 Chainaanalysis 表示，在通过 Tron 上的中间钱包转移超过 5 亿美元后，与朝鲜有关的参与者已经开始了新的洗钱阶段。

paras.en: Elliptic also identified the first signs of bitcoin mixing, a technique designed to make transactions harder to trace. About 28 bitcoin, worth $2.2 million, had passed through 18 mixing transactions as of early Monday, the firm said.
paras.zh: Elliptic 还发现了比特币混合的最初迹象，这是一种旨在使交易更难以追踪的技术。该公司表示，截至周一早些时候，价值 220 万美元的约 28 个比特币已通过 18 笔混合交易。

paras.en: Despite the extensive movement of funds, about $2.85 billion — or 44% of exactly $6.43 billion stolen as reported by Elliptic — has been frozen or seized, while roughly $3.24 billion remains in addresses linked to the theft, mostly in bitcoin and ether.
paras.zh: 尽管资金流动广泛，但仍有约 28.5 亿美元（即 Elliptic 报告的被盗 64.3 亿美元中的 44%）被冻结或扣押，而与盗窃相关的地址中仍有约 32.4 亿美元，其中大部分是比特币和以太币。

paras.en: The firm said only a negligible amount of stolen funds appeared to have been cashed out, with most of the activity involving transfers or conversions between cryptocurrencies rather than exchanges into spendable funds.
paras.zh: 该公司表示，被盗资金似乎只有微不足道的部分被兑现，大部分活动涉及加密货币之间的转移或转换，而不是兑换成可支出资金。

paras.en: Elliptic said the laundering has moved slower than after the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, when North Korean hackers moved all the stolen ether within 10 days. It expects the remaining funds to be gradually converted into bitcoin and potentially cashed out through over-the-counter brokers and exchanges over several months.
paras.zh: Elliptic 表示，洗钱活动的进展速度比 2025 年 2 月 Bybit 黑客攻击价值 15 亿美元之后的速度要慢，当时朝鲜黑客在 10 天内转移了所有被盗的以太币。它预计剩余资金将逐渐转换为比特币，并可能在几个月内通过场外经纪人和交易所兑现。

paras.en: Binance added it has covered about 95% of the affected amount, with the remaining 5% consisting of less liquid tokens that take longer to source. The exchange said it was working with industry partners to acquire the remaining assets.
paras.zh: 币安补充说，它已经覆盖了大约 95% 的受影响金额，其余 5% 是流动性较低、需要更长时间才能获取的代币。该交易所表示，正在与行业合作伙伴合作收购剩余资产。

articles.title: Boo! See the universe’s spookiest sights in time for Halloween

paras.en: As ghosts, skeletons and spiders roam the streets trick-or-treating on Halloween night, they’ll have cosmic company. Throughout outer space lie stars and galaxies that resemble creepy creatures, spooky skulls and galactic ghouls. And while there’s no candy in outer space (though there is sugar), these colorful images are a treat in and of themselves.
paras.zh: 当鬼魂、骷髅和蜘蛛在万圣节之夜在街上游荡，玩“不给糖就捣蛋”的游戏时，他们会有宇宙的陪伴。整个外太空遍布着类似于令人毛骨悚然的生物、幽灵头骨和银河食尸鬼的恒星和星系。虽然外太空没有糖果（尽管有糖），但这些色彩缤纷的图像本身就是一种享受。

paras.en: Skeletons and disembodied heads are a hallmark of Halloween, but this phantasmic apparition, called the exposed cranium nebula, lurks above us all year long. Its brainlike appearance stems from the different phases of star death. First, the dying star ejects a bunch of hydrogen, which forms the white outer bubble, then heavier material, which creates the orange “brain” within.
paras.zh: 骷髅和无实体的头颅是万圣节的标志，但这个被称为裸露颅骨星云的幻影全年潜伏在我们头顶。它的类似大脑的外观源于恒星死亡的不同阶段。首先，垂死的恒星喷射出一堆氢，形成白色的外部气泡，然后是较重的物质，在内部形成橙色的“大脑”。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The name of this nebula sounds like the title of a scary story. Called “the Ghost of Cassiopea,” its gas and dust glows like a haunted spirit because of hydrogen interacting with ultraviolet radiation from a star in the constellation Cassiopeia the Queen. When the two mix, the gas glows red, and the blue haze comes from light reflecting off space dust.
paras.zh: 这个星云的名字听起来就像一个恐怖故事的标题。它被称为“仙后座幽灵”，由于氢与仙后座恒星的紫外线辐射相互作用，它的气体和尘埃像闹鬼的灵魂一样发光。当两者混合时，气体发出红光，蓝色的雾气来自太空尘埃反射的光。

paras.en: This nebula, called the Red Spider Nebula, is scuttling around space while its central star, glowing bright red in the middle, ejects bursts of gas and dust. These filaments, made up mostly of hydrogen, form the spider’s “legs.”
paras.zh: 这个被称为红蜘蛛星云的星云正在太空中快速移动，而它的中心恒星在中间发出鲜红色的光芒，喷射出大量的气体和尘埃。这些主要由氢组成的细丝形成了蜘蛛的“腿”。

paras.en: We all know the stories about black cats on Halloween, but what about space cats? The Cat’s Head Nebula is a collection of gas and young stars sitting within the Carina Nebula. Although the shape will someday dissipate, for now it resembles a cat turned to the right, with a glowing red eye that’s likely a young star.
paras.zh: 我们都知道万圣节黑猫的故事，但是太空猫呢？猫头星云是船底座星云内气体和年轻恒星的集合。虽然这个形状有一天会消失，但目前它就像一只向右转的猫，眼睛发着红光，很可能是一颗年轻的星星。

paras.en: The aptly named Phantom galaxy lies 32 million light-years away in the Pisces constellation. It’s called that because it has low surface brightness and is difficult to spot—but with a head-on spiral view that resembles a portal to another dimension, it certainly lives up to its haunted name.
paras.zh: 这个名为幻影星系的名字恰如其分，位于双鱼座，距我们 3200 万光年。之所以这样称呼它，是因为它的表面亮度较低，很难被发现，但正面的螺旋视图就像通往另一个维度的门户，它确实名副其实。

articles.title: How to ‘fall back’ this weekend without losing your mind

paras.en: At 2 A.M. on Sunday, most of the U.S. will set the clocks back by an hour. With the switch to standard time, we’ll get earlier sunshine and darker evenings—and an extra hour of sleep.
paras.zh: 凌晨 2 点周日，美国大部分地区会将时钟拨慢一小时。改用标准时间后，我们将获得更早的阳光和更暗的夜晚，以及额外一小时的睡眠。

paras.en: Research suggests standard time better aligns with our circadian rhythm, or internal clock, and reduces the risk of health complications. But changing to standard time comes with some risks, too, experts say.
paras.zh: 研究表明，标准时间更符合我们的昼夜节律或内部时钟，并降低出现健康并发症的风险。但专家表示，改变标准时间也会带来一些风险。

paras.en: Between “falling back” to standard time in November and “springing forward” to daylight saving time (DST) in March, experts say the switch to DST is the bigger disruption. In the days after the March time change, scientists have measured higher rates of lost sleep and an uptick in heart attacks. After the time change in November, however, those risks are lower.
paras.zh: 专家表示，在 11 月“回退”至标准时间和 3 月“前进”至夏令时 (DST) 之间，切换到 DST 带来的干扰更大。在三月时间变更后的几天里，科学家们测量到睡眠不足率更高，心脏病发作率也有所上升。然而，在 11 月时间变更后，这些风险就会降低。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Some research suggests rates of stroke go up around both spring and fall clock changes, although the risk of death is higher in the spring, says Beth Malow, a professor of neurology and pediatrics at Vanderbilt University.
paras.zh: 范德比尔特大学神经病学和儿科教授贝丝·马洛表示，一些研究表明，春季和秋季时钟变化期间中风的发病率会上升，尽管春季的死亡风险较高。

paras.en: On standard time, early risers get the benefit of a little more morning sunlight. Morning light is “one of the strongest forces” that aligns our bodies’ circadian rhythm with the outside world, Malow says. That alignment helps us wake up in the morning and drift off at night more easily.
paras.zh: 在标准时间，早起的人可以享受到更多的早晨阳光。马洛说，晨光是“最强大的力量之一”，它使我们身体的昼夜节律与外界保持一致。这种排列可以帮助我们在早上醒来并在晚上更容易入睡。

paras.en: After the fall time change, you might wake up well after the sun comes up—but that poses less of a risk than cutting off your body’s internal clock early, says Jamie Zeitzer, a professor and a sleep scientist at Stanford University. “You’re basically sleeping in,” he adds.
paras.zh: 斯坦福大学教授兼睡眠科学家杰米·蔡泽尔 (Jamie Zeitzer) 表示，秋季时间改变后，你可能会在太阳升起后很长时间醒来，但这比提前切断体内生物钟带来的风险要小。 “你基本上是在睡懒觉，”他补充道。

paras.en: In fact, given the overall benefits of standard time, top medical organizations, including the American Medical Association, Sleep Research Society and American Academy of Sleep Medicine have fought efforts to make DST permanent—a frequent hobbyhorse in Congress.
paras.zh: 事实上，考虑到标准时间的总体好处，包括美国医学会、睡眠研究协会和美国睡眠医学会在内的顶级医疗组织一直在努力使夏令时永久化，这也是国会经常关注的话题。

paras.en: A major downside to standard time, however, is less time spent outdoors. Some studies also suggest moving commuting times nearer to dusk in the fall increases the risk of vehicle collisions with deer and other wildlife, which are more active around sunset.
paras.zh: 然而，标准时间的一个主要缺点是户外时间较少。一些研究还表明，秋季通勤时间接近黄昏会增加车辆与鹿和其他野生动物发生碰撞的风险，因为鹿和其他野生动物在日落时更加活跃。

paras.en: There are certain steps you can take to ensure a more smooth transition, experts say.
paras.zh: 专家表示，您可以采取某些步骤来确保更顺利的过渡。

paras.en: Number one, don’t go into a clock change while sleep-deprived, Malow says. And try to get as much exposure to morning light as possible throughout the season. (If you’re able to access one, a light box can be helpful for this on dark mornings in the spring.) Stay alert during dark commutes, when visibility may be limited, whether they’re on a spring morning or a fall evening, Malow adds. And if you’re consistently struggling with sleep, consider seeing a doctor.
paras.zh: 马洛说，第一，不要在睡眠不足的情况下改变时钟。并在整个季节尝试尽可能多地接触晨光。 （如果你能找到一个灯箱，在春天黑暗的早晨，灯箱可能会有所帮助。）马洛补充道，无论是在春天的早晨还是秋天的晚上，在黑暗的通勤期间，当能见度可能有限时，都要保持警惕。如果您一直困扰睡眠，请考虑去看医生。

paras.en: In the fall, you may need to take extra care to get regular evening exercise in. And if you, like many Americans, aren’t getting enough shut-eye on most nights, consider using the clock change to set a new sleep habit, Malow says.
paras.zh: 在秋天，你可能需要格外小心，定期进行晚间锻炼。马洛说，如果你像许多美国人一样，在大多数晚上都没有得到足够的睡眠，可以考虑利用时钟变化来养成新的睡眠习惯。

paras.en: If your usual bedtime is 11 P.M., for instance, try going to bed when you’re tired instead—after the time change, that will be when the clocks read about 10 P.M.—and try to stick to the new schedule. “Take advantage of the fact that your body’s now going to be ready to go to bed earlier,” she says.
paras.zh: 例如，如果您通常的就寝时间是晚上 11 点，请尝试在感到疲倦时上床睡觉（时间更改后，时钟指向晚上 10 点左右），并尝试遵守新的作息时间。 “利用你的身体现在准备早点睡觉的事实，”她说。

paras.en: If nothing else, relish “sleeping in,” Zeitzer says. “Enjoy the extra hour of sleep.”
paras.zh: 蔡策说，如果没有别的事，那就享受“睡懒觉”吧。 “享受额外的一小时睡眠。”

articles.title: How your brain can turn your own reflection into something unrecognizable

paras.en: It’s Halloween night. Someone has dared you to turn off the lights and stand in front of the mirror. The rules are simple, stare into your reflection and say her name three times.
paras.zh: 这是万圣节之夜。有人挑战你关掉灯并站在镜子前。规则很简单，凝视你的倒影并说出她的名字三遍。

paras.en: According to the creepy urban legend, a terrifying figure will appear in the glass. Depending on which version of the story you follow, she might be a bloodied woman, a witch or a ghost seeking revenge. Sometimes, she simply appears behind you. In more sinister versions, she reaches out of the mirror.
paras.zh: 根据令人毛骨悚然的都市传说，玻璃中会出现一个可怕的身影。根据您所关注的故事版本，她可能是一个血淋淋的女人、一个女巫或一个寻求复仇的鬼魂。有时，她只是出现在你身后。在更险恶的版本中，她把手伸到镜子外面。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Most of us encountered some variation of this story as children. Those brave enough to have tried it may even swear they saw a monstrous face appear in the mirror before them.
paras.zh: 我们大多数人小时候都遇到过这个故事的一些变体。那些勇敢尝试过的人甚至可能发誓他们看到镜子里出现了一张可怕的脸。

paras.en: As tempting as it might be to believe that the monster you saw in mirror was something supernatural, the real explanation is perhaps even stranger. Your brain is perfectly capable of turning your own reflection into something you barely recognize.
paras.zh: 尽管人们很容易相信你在镜子中看到的怪物是超自然的东西，但真正的解释可能更奇怪。你的大脑完全有能力将你自己的倒影变成你几乎不认识的东西。

paras.en: In 2010, Italian psychologist Giovanni Caputo published a study with the intriguing title Strange-face-in-the-mirror illusion. He asked 66 volunteers to sit approximately 40 centimeters from a mirror in a dimly lit room and look at their own faces for one minute.
paras.zh: 2010年，意大利心理学家乔瓦尼·卡普托（Giovanni Caputo）发表了一项研究，其标题很有趣：镜中怪脸错觉。他让 66 名志愿者坐在光线昏暗的房间里，距离镜子约 40 厘米，看着自己的脸一分钟。

paras.en: Around two-thirds reported significant distortions of their faces. More than a quarter described seeing an unfamiliar person, while others reported fantastical beings, animals or the faces of relatives – sometimes deceased. Some changes began after less than a minute.
paras.zh: 大约三分之二的人表示他们的脸部严重扭曲。超过四分之一的人描述看到了一个陌生的人，而其他人则报告了奇异的生物、动物或亲戚的面孔——有时是已故的亲戚。不到一分钟后，一些变化就开始了。

paras.en: The participants weren’t being asked to summon ghosts. They were simply looking at themselves. So why would something as familiar as our own face suddenly become strange?
paras.zh: 参与者并没有被要求召唤鬼魂。他们只是在看着自己。那么为什么像我们自己的脸这样熟悉的东西会突然变得陌生呢？

paras.en: The explanation partly lies in the 1804 work done by Swiss physician Ignaz Paul Vital Troxler who described a curious phenomenon. When we fix our gaze on one point, objects elsewhere in our visual field can gradually fade from awareness. This is now known as the Troxler effect, or Troxler fading.
paras.zh: 部分解释源于瑞士医生 Ignaz Paul Vital Troxler 1804 年所做的工作，他描述了一个奇怪的现象。当我们将目光固定在一点上时，视野中其他地方的物体就会逐渐从我们的意识中消失。这现在被称为 Troxler 效应或 Troxler 衰落。

paras.en: This effect happens partly because sensory neurons, which detect and transmit information about what we see, adapt to relatively constant stimulation. Our visual system is particularly interested in change: movement, shifting contrast and anything that might require our attention.
paras.zh: 发生这种效应的部分原因是感觉神经元（负责检测和传输我们所看到的信息）适应相对恒定的刺激。我们的视觉系统对变化特别感兴趣：运动、变化的对比度以及任何可能需要我们注意的东西。

paras.en: Normally, we hardly notice this process. Even when we believe we’re staring steadily, our eyes make tiny movements that continually refresh visual information. But prolonged fixation can allow relatively stable features, particularly those away from the centre of our gaze, to become less distinct.
paras.zh: 通常情况下，我们很难注意到这个过程。即使我们相信自己正在稳定地凝视，我们的眼睛也会做出微小的运动，不断刷新视觉信息。但长时间注视会使相对稳定的特征，尤其是那些远离我们视线中心的特征变得不那么清晰。

paras.en: Now imagine applying this to your face. When you stare at your own eyes in a mirror, the surrounding features remain relatively stationary. The contours of your cheeks, the edges of your nose and the outline of your mouth provide a fairly constant pattern of information.
paras.zh: 现在想象一下将其应用到您的脸上。当你在镜子中凝视自己的眼睛时，周围的特征保持相对静止。脸颊的轮廓、鼻子的边缘和嘴巴的轮廓提供了相当恒定的信息模式。

paras.en: But in dim light, those features are already harder to distinguish—so the Troxler effect alone cannot explain why someone might see an entirely different face. For that, we need to consider how the brain recognizes faces.
paras.zh: 但在昏暗的光线下，这些特征已经很难区分——因此特罗克斯勒效应本身无法解释为什么有人可能会看到一张完全不同的脸。为此，我们需要考虑大脑如何识别面孔。

paras.en: Human beings are extraordinarily sensitive to faces. We can recognize familiar people from surprisingly little visual information and detect subtle changes in expression.
paras.zh: 人类对面孔异常敏感。我们可以从少得惊人的视觉信息中认出熟悉的人，并察觉表情的细微变化。

paras.en: This ability involves a network of brain regions, including the fusiform face area, which responds particularly strongly to faces. Rather than analyzing every feature independently, our visual system processes the relationships between them—including the distance between the eyes, the position of the nose and the arrangement of facial features.
paras.zh: 这种能力涉及大脑区域网络，包括对面部反应特别强烈的梭状面部区域。我们的视觉系统不是独立分析每个特征，而是处理它们之间的关系，包括眼睛之间的距离、鼻子的位置和面部特征的排列。

paras.en: When you look into a mirror, your brain isn’t simply recording what is in front of you. It interprets visual information using previous experience and expectations—and there’s perhaps no face you know better than your own. But under dim lighting, the information arriving from your eyes becomes less reliable. Shadows obscure features, contrast diminishes and the relationships between parts of the face become harder to resolve.
paras.zh: 当你照镜子时，你的大脑不仅仅是记录你面前的事物。它利用以前的经验和期望来解释视觉信息——也许没有一张脸比你自己更了解。但在昏暗的灯光下，从眼睛传来的信息就变得不太可靠。阴影模糊了特征，对比度减弱，面部各部分之间的关​​系变得更难以解析。

paras.en: The brain must continue interpreting this increasingly ambiguous information. Sometimes the result is a distorted version of your own face. Sometimes it resembles another person altogether.
paras.zh: 大脑必须继续解释这些日益模糊的信息。有时结果是你自己的脸被扭曲了。有时它完全像另一个人。

paras.en: The mechanisms behind these illusions are still under investigation. But what makes the experience disturbing is that the reflection remains recognizably human while no longer appearing to belong to you.
paras.zh: 这些错觉背后的机制仍在研究中。但令人不安的是，倒影仍然是人类的，但似乎不再属于你。

paras.en: Long before children began summoning Bloody Mary, reflective surfaces were associated with spirits, prophecy and the dead.
paras.zh: 早在孩子们开始召唤血腥玛丽之前，反光表面就与灵魂、预言和死者联系在一起。

paras.en: The ancient practice of catoptromancy involved divination using mirrors. Related traditions of scrying involved gazing into reflective surfaces in the hope of seeing visions or messages hidden from ordinary sight.
paras.zh: 古代的投光术涉及使用镜子进行占卜。占卜的相关传统包括凝视反光表面，希望看到隐藏在普通视线中的景象或信息。

paras.en: Mirrors also acquired significance in mourning traditions. In some communities, they were covered following a death because of the belief they could trap the soul or reveal the dead. Other traditions have different explanations for covering mirrors – including setting aside concerns about personal appearance during mourning.
paras.zh: 镜子在哀悼传统中也具有重要意义。在一些社区，死者死后会被遮盖，因为他们相信它们可以困住灵魂或揭示死者的身份。其他传统对遮盖镜子有不同的解释，包括在哀悼期间不考虑个人仪表。

paras.en: We cannot conclude that visual illusions gave rise to these customs. But it’s intriguing that prolonged staring, low illumination and the expectation of seeing something unusual feature in both supernatural mirror rituals and experiments producing perceptual distortions.
paras.zh: 我们不能断定视觉错觉导致了这些习俗。 But it’s intriguing that prolonged staring, low illumination and the expectation of seeing something unusual feature in both supernatural mirror rituals and experiments producing perceptual distortions.

paras.en: The Bloody Mary ritual adds another ingredient: anticipation. You expect something frightening, and that expectation may influence how you interpret ambiguous shadows and unfamiliar features.
paras.zh: 血腥玛丽仪式增加了另一个要素：期待。你期待一些可怕的东西，这种期望可能会影响你如何解释模棱两可的阴影和不熟悉的特征。

paras.en: In this way, the ritual creates the very conditions in which something unsettling might appear. The legend tells you what to expect, and your visual system may provide something that seems to confirm it. So, this Halloween, remember that you don’t need to believe in ghosts for something strange to happen.
paras.zh: 通过这种方式，仪式创造了可能出现令人不安的事情的条件。图例告诉你会发生什么，你的视觉系统可能会提供一些似乎证实它的东西。所以，这个万圣节，请记住，你不需要相信有鬼魂，就会发生奇怪的事情。

paras.en: This article was first published by The Conversation. Read the original article here.
paras.zh: 本文最初由《对话》发表。在这里阅读原文。

articles.title: Comets probably didn’t deliver life’s building blocks to Earth
articles.author: Skyler Ware

paras.en: The chemical building blocks that gave rise to life on Earth probably didn’t come from comets.
paras.zh: 地球上孕育生命的化学成分可能并非来自彗星。

paras.en: Most comets would have been traveling too fast and at too steep an angle to Earth for prebiotic compounds to survive impact with the planet, researchers contend October 28 in Scientific Reports. While the study doesn’t completely rule out the possibility that comets brought these molecules to Earth, it contradicts the long-standing idea that comets seeded Earth with the chemicals necessary for life to arise.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 10 月 28 日的《科学报告》中指出，大多数彗星运行速度太快，与地球的角度太陡，以至于生命起源前的化合物无法在撞击地球时幸存下来。虽然这项研究并没有完全排除彗星将这些分子带到地球的可能性，但它与长期以来的观点相矛盾，即彗星在地球上播下了生命产生所需的化学物质。

paras.en: “Even though we see that comets contain all of these molecules in really high concentrations, it’s not straightforward to go from there to saying we’re going to have all of these available for prebiotic chemistry on the surface of the Earth,” says Richard Anslow, a planetary scientist at the Met Office, the national meteorological service for the United Kingdom in Exeter.
paras.zh: 英国气象局行星科学家理查德·安斯洛（Richard Anslow）表示：“尽管我们发现彗星中含有非常高浓度的所有这些分子，但从那里到我们将在地球表面拥有可用于生命起源前化学的所有这些分子并不简单。”

paras.en: Comets carry carbon- and nitrogen-containing molecules left over from early in the solar system’s formation. These molecules can react to form biologically important compounds like sugars and DNA. Scientists have long thought that comets could have delivered these building blocks to Earth when they collided with the planet during its first billion years.
paras.zh: 彗星携带着太阳系形成早期遗留下来的含碳和氮分子。这些分子可以发生反应，形成具有重要生物学意义的化合物，如糖和 DNA。长期以来，科学家们一直认为，彗星在地球诞生的第一个十亿年期间与地球相撞时，可能将这些构件带到了地球上。

paras.en: But it’s important to revisit these ideas as our understanding of both comets and the early solar system improves, says Nicolle Zellner, a physicist at Albion College in Michigan who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 但随着我们对彗星和早期太阳系的了解不断加深，重新审视这些想法很重要，密歇根州阿尔比恩学院的物理学家尼科尔·泽尔纳（Nicolle Zellner）没有参与这项研究，他说。

paras.en: In the new work, Anslow and colleagues used computer simulations to predict the likelihood that a chemical called hydrogen cyanide would survive a comet’s journey through Earth’s present atmosphere and its impact with the planet’s surface. The early Earth’s atmosphere was probably much denser, so would have been even more destructive.
paras.zh: 在这项新工作中，安斯洛和同事使用计算机模拟来预测一种名为氰化氢的化学物质在彗星穿越地球现有大气层的旅程及其对地球表面的影响中幸存下来的可能性。早期地球的大气层可能密度更大，因此更具破坏性。

paras.en: The strong chemical bond between the carbon and nitrogen atoms in hydrogen cyanide can release energy that drives later chemical reactions necessary for life. It also makes the molecule particularly stable compared to other carbon-based chemicals.
paras.zh: 氰化氢中碳原子和氮原子之间的牢固化学键可以释放能量，驱动随后生命所需的化学反应。与其他碳基化学品相比，它还使该分子特别稳定。

paras.en: “It’s probably one of the more robust molecules to surviving impacts,” Anslow says. “So if things look bad for hydrogen cyanide, then we think it’s going to be much harder for other, more complicated molecules that are more likely to be broken down during these impacts.”
paras.zh: “它可能是在撞击中幸存下来的更强大的分子之一，”安斯洛说。 “因此，如果氰化氢的情况看起来很糟糕，那么我们认为对于其他更复杂的分子来说，情况会变得更加困难，因为这些分子在这些影响期间更有可能被分解。”

paras.en: Based on the simulations, a comet impact that kept hydrogen cyanide intact would be extremely unlikely, the team found. On average, the simulations suggest that only one impact would have been able to deliver a meaningful amount of hydrogen cyanide to the planet’s surface over more than a billion years. For hydrogen cyanide to survive the crash, the comet would have to be larger than 100 meters across, slow moving and traveling at an oblique angle to Earth.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，根据模拟，彗星撞击使氰化氢保持完整的可能性极小。平均而言，模拟表明，在十亿多年的时间里，只有一次撞击就能向地球表面释放大量氰化氢。为了让氰化氢在撞击中幸存下来，彗星的直径必须大于 100 米，缓慢移动，并以与地球倾斜的角度行进。

paras.en: A comet that met those narrow criteria would also have had to crash into land, rather than an ocean, to kick off any biologically useful chemistry. If the comet landed in the ocean, any hydrogen cyanide that survived would be diluted too quickly to trigger those reactions.
paras.zh: A comet that met those narrow criteria would also have had to crash into land, rather than an ocean, to kick off any biologically useful chemistry.如果彗星降落在海洋中，任何幸存的氰化氢都会被稀释得太快而无法引发这些反应。

paras.en: While still improbable, comets may have been more likely to deliver carbon-based molecules to Mars than to Earth, the simulations showed. Mars’ thinner atmosphere and smaller size meant that comets would impact at lower speeds. That could mean that more compounds could survive the collision.
paras.zh: 模拟显示，尽管可能性仍然不大，但彗星可能更有可能将碳基分子运送到火星而不是地球。火星的大气层较稀薄，尺寸较小，这意味着彗星将以较低的速度撞击。这可能意味着更多的化合物可以在碰撞中幸存下来。

paras.en: If Earth’s carbon-based chemicals didn’t come from comets, they may have come from carbon-rich asteroids called carbonaceous chondrites, says Gordon Osinski, a planetary geologist at Western University in London, Canada, who was not involved in the study. Other sources might have included volcanoes and hydrothermal vents.
paras.zh: 加拿大伦敦西部大学的行星地质学家戈登·奥辛斯基（未参与这项研究）表示，如果地球上的碳基化学物质不是来自彗星，它们可能来自富含碳的小行星，即碳质球粒陨石。其他来源可能包括火山和热液喷口。

paras.en: The study “definitely will make people think twice about comets being the originator for the delivery of organics,” Osinski says. “I hope other people will try to reproduce these results [and] then potentially try something similar with carbonaceous chondrites as well.”
paras.zh: 奥辛斯基说，这项研究“肯定会让人们重新思考彗星是有机物输送的起源”。 “我希望其他人能够尝试重现这些结果，然后也可能尝试用碳质球粒陨石进行类似的尝试。”

articles.title: A striking Mars cloud may be born from surprising physics
articles.author: Allie Skalnik

paras.en: One of Mars’ strangest clouds may rely on unusual physics to emerge.
paras.zh: 火星最奇怪的云之一可能依赖于不寻常的物理现象而出现。

paras.en: The Red Planet’s ribbonlike cloud — which stretches as long as four Grand Canyons laid end-to-end — may form without a speck of starting material to seed it, researchers report October 7 in Nature Geoscience. This manner of forming clouds, called homogenous nucleation, was thought to be possible on paper but not to occur naturally.
paras.zh: 研究人员 10 月 7 日在《自然地球科学》杂志上报告称，这颗红色星球的带状云——其长度相当于四个首尾相接的大峡谷——可能在没有任何起始材料的情况下形成。这种形成云的方式被称为同质成核，人们认为在纸上是可能的，但不会自然发生。

paras.en: Tiny particles such as dust or salt floating in the air seed typical clouds on Earth. But that cloud physics doesn’t seem to apply to the Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud. Beyond its impressive length, this wisp of water ice is remarkably consistent, forming daily in the same spot roughly 45 kilometers high on the slope of a Martian volcano for several months each year.
paras.zh: 空气中漂浮的灰尘或盐等微小颗粒在地球上形成了典型的云。但这种云物理学似乎并不适用于阿尔西亚蒙斯拉长云。除了令人印象深刻的长度之外，这缕水冰的形成也非常一致，每年有几个月每天都会在火星火山斜坡上约 45 公里高的同一地点形成。

paras.en: The team tried and tried but couldn’t reproduce the cloud’s formation, including its lengthy tail and consistent cycle, with computer models employing standard cloud physics, says François Forget, an astrophysicist at the Laboratoire de Météorologie Dynamique, or LMD, in Paris.
paras.zh: 巴黎气象动态实验室 (LMD) 的天体物理学家弗朗索瓦·福吉特 (François Forget) 表示，该团队进行了多次尝试，但无法利用采用标准云物理的计算机模型重现云的形成，包括其长尾和一致的周期。

paras.en: There’s no shortage of dust on Mars. The trouble is that high up in a thin Martian atmosphere, few cloud-forming dust particles stay suspended. Instead, they probably clump together and eventually fall, says planetary physicist Jorge Hernández-Bernal, who did the work at LMD. This left cloud formation without seeds as the most convincing explanation, he says.
paras.zh: 火星上不乏尘埃。问题在于，在火星稀薄大气层的高处，几乎没有形成云的尘埃颗粒保持悬浮状态。相反，它们可能会聚集在一起并最终坠落，在 LMD 从事这项工作的行星物理学家 Jorge Hernández-Bernal 表示。他说，这使得没有种子的云形成成为最令人信服的解释。

paras.en: Every day during some seasons on Mars, a long wispy cloud emerges along the flanks of the Arsia Mons volcano, as seen in the observations video spanning three Martian hours. How that cloud forms has been a mystery. A new simulation, bottom, included unusual physics, in which clouds form without starting material. That approach replicated the shape and timing of Mars’ Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud for the first time.
paras.zh: 正如在火星上三个小时的观测视频中所看到的那样，在火星上的某些季节里，每天都会沿着阿尔西亚蒙斯火山的侧面出现一缕长长的细云。这种云是如何形成的一直是个谜。底部的新模拟包括不寻常的物理现象，其中云在没有起始材料的情况下形成。这种方法首次复制了火星阿尔西亚蒙斯拉长云的形状和时间。

paras.en: The team’s model suggests that the eye-catching plume originates when air flowing across the volcano triggers a rapid lifting of a moist parcel of air. The decrease in pressure at that altitude lets the air parcel expand, rapidly cooling it.
paras.zh: 该团队的模型表明，引人注目的羽流源自流经火山的空气触发潮湿空气团的快速上升。该高度压力的降低使空气团膨胀，从而迅速冷却。

paras.en: The newly cooled air now has 100,000 times more moisture than it can hold, the team’s model suggests. This excess moisture undergoes homogenous nucleation, rapidly forming more stable ice crystals. Winds sweep the forming cloud outward, creating the cloud’s distinctive long shape.
paras.zh: 该团队的模型表明，新冷却的空气现在的湿度是其所能容纳的湿度的 100,000 倍。这些多余的水分会发生均匀成核，迅速形成更稳定的冰晶。风将正在形成的云向外扫，形成云独特的长形状。

paras.en: While the model doesn’t perfectly match satellite observations, it does capture how the phenomenon that leads to the cold air pocket reoccurs day after day, just like the real cloud does.
paras.zh: 虽然该模型并不完全符合卫星观测结果，但它确实捕捉到了导致冷气团的现象如何日复一日地重复出现，就像真正的云一样。

paras.en: The study was surprising because “homogeneous nucleation is generally treated in our field as this theoretical concept,” says Samuel Atwood, an atmospheric and planetary scientist at the University of Maryland, Baltimore County and NASA Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Md., who was not associated with the study.
paras.zh: 这项研究令人惊讶，因为“在我们的领域，均质成核通常被视为这一理论概念，”马里兰大学巴尔的摩分校和马里兰州格林贝尔特美国宇航局戈达德太空飞行中心的大气和行星科学家塞缪尔·阿特伍德（Samuel Atwood）表示，他并未参与这项研究。

paras.en: “It’s a pretty compelling story that they’re telling with the model, but it’s only one view or one perspective on it,” Atwood says, adding that future measurements supporting the team’s finding will provide more certainty. Hernández-Bernal says that he plans to validate the study by testing alternative explanations.
paras.zh: 阿特伍德说：“他们用模型讲述的故事非常引人注目，但这只是一种观点或一种观点。”他补充说，支持团队发现的未来测量将提供更多确定性。埃尔南德斯-贝纳尔表示，他计划通过测试其他解释来验证这项研究。

paras.en: Even beyond Mars, the study provides food for thought. Previous studies have suggested that on Earth, meteor smoke provides particles for cloud formation in an upper layer of the atmosphere called the mesosphere, though a few studies have suggested homogenous nucleation could be responsible. Now that scientists are proposing homogenous nucleation on Mars, Hernández-Bernal says, “maybe there will be an increased interest in investigating this on Earth.”
paras.zh: 即使在火星之外，这项研究也值得深思。先前的研究表明，在地球上，流星烟雾为大气上层（称为中间层）云的形成提供了颗粒，尽管一些研究表明均质成核可能是造成这种现象的原因。埃尔南德斯-贝纳尔说，现在科学家们提出在火星上进行同质成核，“也许人们对在地球上研究这一点的兴趣会增加。”

articles.title: Some of the world’s biggest bats are getting smaller
articles.author: Jake Buehler

paras.en: These big bats aren’t quite the behemoths they used to be.
paras.zh: 这些大蝙蝠不再是以前的庞然大物了。

paras.en: With a leathery wingspan of up to a meter and a half, fruit bats —some of which are called flying foxes — feel a bit like they’ve flapped out of a fantasy novel. Though flying foxes include the world’s largest bats, one species in Madagascar appears to be shrinking, researchers report October 29 in the Journal of Mammalogy. Hunting pressure by humans may be why.
paras.zh: 果蝠（其中一些被称为狐蝠）的皮革翼展长达一米半，感觉有点像奇幻小说中的翅膀。研究人员 10 月 29 日在《哺乳动物学杂志》上报告称，尽管狐蝠包括世界上最大的蝙蝠，但马达加斯加的一种蝙蝠似乎正在萎缩。人类的狩猎压力可能就是原因。

paras.en: The first hints that the bats might be shrinking came from scientific collections at the Field Museum in Chicago. Researchers at the museum — including flying vertebrate ecologist Emily Cornelius Ruhs and conservation biologist Steven Goodman — noticed something strange about the preserved specimens of Malagasy flying foxes (Pteropus rufus).
paras.zh: 蝙蝠可能正在缩小的第一个暗示来自芝加哥菲尔德博物馆的科学收藏。博物馆的研究人员——包括飞行脊椎动物生态学家艾米丽·科尼利厄斯·鲁斯（Emily Cornelius Ruhs）和保护生物学家史蒂文·古德曼（Steven Goodman）——注意到保存下来的马达加斯加狐蝠（Pteropus rufus）标本的一些奇怪之处。

paras.en: “It seemed like the [flying foxes] in the collections were a lot larger than the ones that [field scientists] had been catching in recent years in Madagascar,” says Ruhs.
paras.zh: “这些藏品中的[狐蝠]似乎比[实地科学家]近年来在马达加斯加捕获的狐蝠要大得多，”鲁斯说。

paras.en: To see if newer specimens were indeed smaller than older specimens, and to understand why, the researchers began taking detailed measurements of the bats. The team logged measurements of 12 different features of the skull and teeth over a total of 121 specimens stored within nine museums. The specimens were collected over more than 150 years, up to the present day.
paras.zh: 为了了解新样本是否确实比旧样本小，并了解原因，研究人员开始对蝙蝠进行详细测量。该团队对 9 个博物馆中存放的总共 121 个标本进行了 12 种不同头骨和牙齿特征的测量。这些标本的采集时间已超过 150 年，直至今日。

paras.en: Bats collected prior to the 1980s had skulls that were on average 3.6 millimeters longer, or about 6 percent longer, than those collected after the 1980s. Possible causes of the shrinkage included effects from climate change or habitat loss. But the timing of the shrinkage also lined up with the commercialization of flying fox hunting.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 80 年代之前收集的蝙蝠的头骨比 1980 年代之后收集的蝙蝠平均长 3.6 毫米，即长约 6%。造成面积缩小的可能原因包括气候变化或栖息地丧失的影响。但减少的时间也与狐蝠狩猎的商业化相一致。

paras.en: “Bats are eaten in Madagascar in certain villages and cultures,” Ruhs says. Up until the 1980s, the animals were mostly hunted on a very small scale to provide food for a family or small community. But around that time, people started selling more bats at markets and restaurants.
paras.zh: “在马达加斯加的某些村庄和文化中，人们会吃蝙蝠，”鲁斯说。直到 20 世纪 80 年代，这些动物大多被小规模猎杀，为家庭或小社区提供食物。但大约在那个时候，人们开始在市场和餐馆出售更多的蝙蝠。

paras.en: As hunting pressure increased, the biggest bats in the population may have been selectively targeted since they provide the “most bang for your buck” Ruhs says.
paras.zh: 鲁斯说，随着狩猎压力的增加，种群中最大的蝙蝠可能会成为选择性目标，因为它们“最划算”。

paras.en: It’s possible that the smaller size could have long-term impacts on the population, says Emma Stone, a conservation biologist at the University of Bath in England. “Species are specifically adapted to their environments and adaptation takes place over thousands of years,” she says. Changes in the animals’ physical traits or adaptations caused by human pressures might make the bats less able to respond to environmental, climate or disease stresses.
paras.zh: 英国巴斯大学的保护生物学家艾玛·斯通表示，较小的体型可能会对种群产生长期影响。 “物种特别适应其环境，并且适应过程需要数千年的时间，”她说。由人类压力引起的动物身体特征或适应的变化可能会降低蝙蝠对环境、气候或疾病压力的反应能力。

paras.en: The bats’ population has dwindled as well. There were an estimated 300,000 Malagasy flying foxes in Madagascar in the early 2000s. Researchers estimate the number has dropped two-thirds since then. The new findings raise concerns about how the bats’ shrinking bodies might be a bellwether for species-wide conservation risks. Future work on the bats’ genetics could tell researchers how modern populations are faring, Ruhs says. Other fruit bat species are also hunted and eaten in Madagascar, she notes, so seeing if similar shrinkage is happening in those species might be interesting.
paras.zh: 蝙蝠的数量也减少了。 2000 年代初，马达加斯加估计有 30 万只马达加斯加狐蝠。研究人员估计，自那时以来，这个数字已经下降了三分之二。这些新发现引发了人们的担忧，即蝙蝠日益缩小的身体可能成为整个物种保护风险的风向标。鲁斯说，未来对蝙蝠遗传学的研究可以告诉研究人员现代蝙蝠的生存状况。她指出，其他果蝠物种也在马达加斯加被猎杀和食用，因此看看这些物种是否也发生类似的萎缩可能会很有趣。

paras.en: “These are important food sources for people. But I think there is something to be said for understanding how to manage [their harvesting] a little bit more,” Ruhs says. “If this population isn’t doing so well, how do we overcome the needs of the people who live there while also protecting species?”
paras.zh: “这些对人们来说是重要的食物来源。但我认为，为了更好地理解如何管理[它们的收获]，有一些话要说，”鲁斯说。 “如果这个种群的情况不太好，我们如何满足居住在那里的人们的需求，同时保护物种？”

articles.title: Inca Mummies Reveal Drugs Used During Human Sacrifice
articles.author: Michelle Starr

paras.en: They could almost have closed their eyes and slipped beyond the boundary between life and death yesterday; so perfect is their preservation.
paras.zh: 昨天他们几乎可以闭上眼睛，滑过生与死的界限；它们的保存如此完美。

paras.en: Yet the children whose bodies were uncovered on frozen mountaintops in Argentina and Peru died hundreds of years ago – and no natural death, either.
paras.zh: 然而，在阿根廷和秘鲁的冰冻山顶上发现尸体的儿童已经在数百年前死亡，而且也不是自然死亡。

paras.en: They were sacrificed by their people, the Inca, to serve as messengers for the gods in a ritual known as capacocha, their small bodies laid to rest with honor and care.
paras.zh: 他们被他们的印加人牺牲，作为众神的使者，在一种被称为“capacocha”的仪式中，他们的小尸体得到了尊重和照顾。

paras.en: And the time leading up to their deaths may have been tended with just as much care. According to a new analysis of their bodies, eight children sacrificed as part of capacocha rites were plied with a variety of drugs in the months to weeks before they died – possibly to ease the ordeal that lay ahead.
paras.zh: 他们死亡前的那段时间可能也受到了同样多的照顾。根据对他们尸体的最新分析，八名在卡帕科查仪式中被牺牲的儿童在死前数月至数周内服用了各种药物，这可能是为了缓解即将面临的磨难。

paras.en: "The children were considered sacred messengers who would continue to play an important role after death," archaeologist Dagmara Socha of the University of Warsaw told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 华沙大学的考古学家达格马拉·索查（Dagmara Socha）告诉 ScienceAlert：“这些孩子被认为是神圣的使者，他们死后将继续发挥重要作用。”

paras.en: "Their preparation may therefore have been intended to help them endure the journey and reach their final destination in the best possible condition."
paras.zh: “因此，他们的准备可能是为了帮助他们忍受这段旅程，并以最好的状态到达最终目的地。”

paras.en: Capacocha was among the most important religious ceremonies of the Inca Empire, performed to mark significant events such as the death or accession of a ruler, major festivals or celebrations, or to appease the gods in times of natural disaster.
paras.zh: 卡帕科查是印加帝国最重要的宗教仪式之一，用于纪念统治者的死亡或即位、重大节日或庆祝活动等重大事件，或在自然灾害时期安抚众神。

paras.en: Children were selected for sacrifice based upon qualities such as exceptional beauty and physical purity, from across the four corners of the Inca Empire.
paras.zh: 来自印加帝国四个角落的儿童是根据非凡的美丽和身体纯洁等品质被挑选出来进行牺牲的。

paras.en: They were often taken to the imperial capital of Cusco, where they participated in elaborate ceremonies before being sent to sacred sites throughout the empire. These processions could take months, traversing vast distances and difficult terrain before reaching their destinations.
paras.zh: 他们经常被带到帝国首都库斯科，在那里参加精心设计的仪式，然后被送往帝国各地的圣地。这些游行可能需要数月时间，穿越遥远的距离和崎岖的地形才能到达目的地。

paras.en: Some of the most sacred sites were high in the Andean mountains, where the children were buried with fine textiles, pottery, and precious figurines as offerings to the gods.
paras.zh: 一些最神圣的地点位于安第斯山脉的高处，孩子们埋葬在那里，里面埋葬着精美的纺织品、陶器和珍贵的雕像，作为献给神的祭品。

paras.en: It's long been known that these children were given drugs before they died, with traces of substances such as cocaine and alcohol found on multiple mummies.
paras.zh: 人们早就知道这些孩子在死前被注射了毒品，在多具木乃伊上发现了可卡因和酒精等微量物质。

paras.en: "Our main question was which psychoactive substances were given to children during the capacocha ritual and what purpose they served," Socha explained.
paras.zh: “我们的主要问题是在卡帕科查仪式期间向儿童提供了哪些精神活性物质以及它们的目的是什么，”索查解释道。

paras.en: "We wanted to understand whether they were used for medicinal reasons, to improve the children's wellbeing, or as part of religious practices involving altered states of consciousness."
paras.zh: “我们想了解它们是否被用于医疗目的、改善儿童的健康，或者作为涉及改变意识状态的宗教活动的一部分。”

paras.en: The answers, if there were any to be found, were most likely to be locked away in the bodies of the sacrificed children, mummified in the cold, low-oxygen environment in the Andean peaks.
paras.zh: 如果有任何答案的话，答案很可能被锁在被牺牲的儿童的尸体里，这些儿童在安第斯山峰寒冷、低氧的环境中被制成木乃伊。

paras.en: The researchers collected hair and nail samples from eight such mummies, dating to around 500 years ago.
paras.zh: 研究人员从八具这样的木乃伊身上收集了头发和指甲样本，其历史可以追溯到大约 500 年前。

paras.en: Keratin-rich tissues preserve chemical traces of substances consumed during life. As they grow, these traces become locked inside, allowing researchers to reconstruct aspects of a person's drug use in the weeks or months before death.
paras.zh: 富含角蛋白的组织保存了生命中消耗的物质的化学痕迹。随着它们的生长，这些痕迹被锁在里面，使研究人员能够重建一个人在死亡前几周或几个月内吸毒的各个方面。

paras.en: The researchers tested the samples for a range of psychoactive compounds, including stimulants, hallucinogens, and substances associated with medicinal plants.
paras.zh: 研究人员测试了样品中的一系列精神活性化合物，包括兴奋剂、致幻剂和与药用植物有关的物质。

paras.en: Coca use was widespread – which is perhaps not a huge surprise. The researchers detected cocaine and its metabolite benzoylecgonine in all six hair samples, consistent with the consumption of coca leaves – a practice deeply embedded in Andean culture.
paras.zh: 古柯的使用很广泛——这也许并不令人意外。研究人员在所有六个头发样本中检测到了可卡因及其代谢物苯甲酰爱康宁，这与食用古柯叶的情况一致——这种做法深深植根于安第斯文化中。

paras.en: Chewing coca leaves can help suppress hunger and fatigue, and may have helped the children endure the physical demands of their journeys through the mountains.
paras.zh: 咀嚼古柯叶可以帮助抑制饥饿和疲劳，并可能帮助孩子们忍受翻山越岭的身体需求。

paras.en: The researchers also detected cocaethylene in samples from some of the children. This compound is produced by the liver when cocaine and alcohol are present in the body at the same time – suggesting that these children had consumed both.
paras.zh: 研究人员还在一些儿童的样本中检测到了可卡乙烯。当可卡因和酒精同时存在于体内时，肝脏会产生这种化合物，这表明这些孩子同时摄入了这两种物质。

paras.en: The alcohol was likely consumed in the form of chicha, a fermented maize beer that played an important role in Inca religious ceremonies.
paras.zh: 这些酒精很可能以奇恰酒的形式消耗，这是一种发酵的玉米啤酒，在印加宗教仪式中发挥着重要作用。

paras.en: One especially tantalizing finding was harmine, detected in the nails of a 14-year-old girl known as the Ampato Maiden, or Juanita.
paras.zh: 一项特别诱人的发现是骆驼蓬碱，它在一名 14 岁女孩安帕托少女 (Ampato Maiden) 或胡安妮塔 (Juanita) 的指甲中检测到。

paras.en: Harmine is a psychoactive compound found in several plants, including Banisteriopsis caapi, a vine native to the Amazon rainforest and used in the preparation of ayahuasca. It inhibits an enzyme involved in breaking down certain neurotransmitters and may have mood-altering effects.
paras.zh: 骆驼蓬碱是一种在多种植物中发现的精神活性化合物，其中包括 Banisteriopsis caapi，一种原产于亚马逊雨林的藤本植物，用于制备死藤水。它抑制参与分解某些神经递质的酶，并可能具有改变情绪的作用。

paras.en: The researchers couldn't determine exactly which plant the girl had consumed, but its discovery in the Ampato Maiden follows its prior detection in two other child mummies from Mount Ampato and raises the interesting possibility that plants from the Amazon were transported to the Andes for ritual use.
paras.zh: 研究人员无法准确确定女孩食用的是哪种植物，但在安帕托少女中发现了这种植物，此前在安帕托山的另外两具儿童木乃伊中也发现了这种植物，并提出了一个有趣的可能性，即来自亚马逊的植物被运到安第斯山脉用于仪式用途。

paras.en: "What surprised me most was the diversity of the results," Socha said.
paras.zh: “最让我惊讶的是结果的多样性，”索查说。

paras.en: "Although coca consumption appears to have been common, we found considerable differences in the use of other substances. This suggests that the preparation of children was much more complex and varied than we previously thought."
paras.zh: “虽然古柯消费似乎很常见，但我们发现其他物质的使用存在相当大的差异。这表明儿童的准备工作比我们之前想象的要复杂和多样得多。”

paras.en: The researchers had also looked for evidence of substances that could induce hallucinations or altered states of consciousness, which might have played a role in preparing the children for their sacred duties.
paras.zh: 研究人员还寻找了可能引起幻觉或改变意识状态的物质的证据，这可能在孩子们为履行神圣职责做好准备方面发挥了作用。

paras.en: But here, the results told a rather different story.
paras.zh: 但在这里，结果却讲述了一个截然不同的故事。

paras.en: "The most important evidence is what we did not find," Socha said.
paras.zh: “最重要的证据是我们没有找到的，”索查说。

paras.en: "Despite testing for several hallucinogenic substances, including mescaline, DMT, and bufotenine, we found no traces of them in the analyzed samples."
paras.zh: “尽管对包括麦司卡林、DMT 和蟾蜍宁在内的几种致幻物质进行了测试，但我们在分析的样品中没有发现它们的痕迹。”

paras.en: Although Socha and her colleagues could not rule out a one-time use during the final stages of capacocha, which may have left no traces in hair and nails, the lack of hallucinogens suggests that the children may have been given drugs primarily to ease the physical and emotional hardships of their final journeys through the Andes, rather than to induce hallucinations.
paras.zh: 尽管索查和她的同事不能排除在卡帕科查的最后阶段一次性使用的可能性，这可能不会在头发和指甲上留下任何痕迹，但缺乏致幻剂表明，孩子们服用药物可能主要是为了缓解他们在穿越安第斯山脉的最后旅程中身体和情感上的困难，而不是诱发幻觉。

paras.en: One of the mummies offers a particularly poignant window into what those final months were like for some.
paras.zh: 其中一具木乃伊提供了一个特别令人心酸的窗口，让我们了解一些人最后几个月的生活。

paras.en: The hair of the mummy of an eight-year-old girl found on Mount Chuscha in Argentina preserved about six months of chemical history. By examining different parts of the hair, the researchers could trace the changes that may have occurred in that time.
paras.zh: 在阿根廷楚沙山发现的一名八岁女孩木乃伊的头发保存了大约六个月的化学历史。通过检查头发的不同部分，研究人员可以追踪当时可能发生的变化。

paras.en: Her coca intake seems to have fluctuated over those months, then dropped in the final month before she died – when she may also have begun ingesting alcohol
paras.zh: 她的古柯摄入量在这几个月里似乎有所波动，然后在她去世前的最后一个月下降——当时她可能也开始摄入酒精

paras.en: Socha cautions that this apparent change could also reflect differences in how the compounds became incorporated into the girl's hair, rather than a change in what she consumed – but there was no mistaking the evidence that she had consumed both.
paras.zh: 索查警告说，这种明显的变化也可能反映了这些化合物融入女孩头发的方式的差异，而不是她所吃东西的变化——但毫无疑问，有证据表明她同时吃过这两种化合物。

paras.en: The differences between the children may also be a clue about diversity within the Inca Empire.
paras.zh: 孩子们之间的差异也可能是印加帝国内部多样性的线索。

paras.en: "The Inca Empire included many different communities, religious traditions, and local deities. Although capacocha was an imperial ceremony, our results suggest that its practice was not identical everywhere," Socha said.
paras.zh: “印加帝国包括许多不同的社区、宗教传统和地方神灵。尽管卡帕科查是一种皇家仪式，但我们的研究结果表明，各地的做法并不相同，”索查说。

paras.en: The team hopes to investigate the substances used in these ceremonies in greater detail, for more insights into the children's origins, their lives before being selected for capacocha, and the preparations they underwent.
paras.zh: 研究小组希望更详细地调查这些仪式中使用的物质，以便更多地了解孩子们的起源、他们在被选中参加卡帕科查之前的生活以及他们所经历的准备工作。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Socha and her colleagues are also surveying sacred mountain sites in the Andes using technologies including drones, LiDAR, and ground-penetrating radar, hoping to build a more complete picture of the Inca's ritual landscape.
paras.zh: 与此同时，索查和她的同事还在利用无人机、激光雷达和探地雷达等技术对安第斯山脉的圣山遗址进行勘察，希望能够更全面地了解印加的仪式景观。

paras.en: "Mountain deities had their own characteristics and were believed to influence different aspects of people's lives, particularly water, climate, and agricultural fertility," Socha explained.
paras.zh: “山神有自己的特点，人们相信它们会影响人们生活的不同方面，特别是水、气候和农业肥力，”索查解释道。

paras.en: "It is possible that the differences we observe reflect the specific requirements of these deities and local religious traditions.
paras.zh: “我们观察到的差异可能反映了这些神灵和当地宗教传统的具体要求。

paras.en: "This reminds us that the Inca Empire was not a culturally uniform society. Imperial religious practices could incorporate considerable regional diversity."
paras.zh: “这提醒我们，印加帝国并不是一个文化统一的社会。帝国的宗教习俗可以包含相当大的地区多样性。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Antiquity.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《古代》杂志上。

articles.title: Just 3 Lines of Math Rule Out Time Travel in Many Possible Universes, Physicist Says
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Time travel is a dream shared by pretty much all of us.
paras.zh: 时间旅行是我们几乎所有人共同的梦想。

paras.en: But the dearth of visitors from the future – and the dismal turnout at the famed time traveler party – is alarming for hopefuls.
paras.zh: 但来自未来的游客的匮乏，以及著名的时间旅行者聚会的出席人数惨淡，令满怀希望的人感到震惊。

paras.en: Still, hypothetical time travel ideas abound, including traversable wormholes propped open by undiscovered exotic states of matter, and a rocket ship skirting billions of light-years around a spinning Universe to end up back in its past.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，假想的时间旅行想法仍然比比皆是，包括由未被发现的奇异物质态支撑的可穿越虫洞，以及一艘围绕旋转宇宙数十亿光年的火箭飞船最终回到过去。

paras.en: But a new study presents a surprisingly simple numerical basis for ruling out closed time loops in a wide class of possible universes, based on a single mathematical proof.
paras.zh: 但一项新的研究提出了一个令人惊讶的简单数值基础，基于单一的数学证明，可以排除多种可能宇宙中的闭合时间循环。

paras.en: In yet-to-be peer-reviewed research, posted to the preprint repository arXiv, physicist Hongsheng Zhang from the University of Jinan in China repurposed a long-standing equation to offer a new numerical prohibition against time travel – further dashing our hopes of a history-bending romp as promised by Bill & Ted's Excellent Adventure.
paras.zh: 在预印本存储库 arXiv 上发布的尚未经过同行评审的研究中，中国济南大学的物理学家张洪生重新利用了一个长期存在的方程，为时间旅行提供了新的数值禁止——进一步破灭了我们对比尔和泰德的《卓越冒险》中所承诺的扭转历史的嬉戏的希望。

paras.en: The research used the "null eikonal equation," an old tool for exploring how light propagates, to surprising effect.
paras.zh: 该研究使用了“零 eikonal 方程”，这是一种探索光如何传播的古老工具，取得了令人惊讶的效果。

paras.en: "The first is how little the theorem needs. The proof runs to three lines and uses exactly one fact about directions: a light-like direction can never be perpendicular to a traveller's direction in time," Zhang told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: “首先是这个定理需要的东西有多么少。证明只有三行，并且只使用了一个关于方向的事实：类似光的方向永远不可能垂直于旅行者的时间方向，”张告诉 ScienceAlert。

paras.en: "From that alone it follows that a certain function must grow along every possible journey, so no journey can return to its starting event."
paras.zh: “仅从这一点就可以看出，某种功能必须沿着每一个可能的旅程发展，因此没有旅程可以返回到它的起始事件。”

paras.en: So a light beam can never be at a 90-degree angle (orthogonal) to the path of any entity moving through time – like a particle or a time traveler with a notepad full of winning lottery numbers – which means a certain quantity always increases along their journey, so they can never loop back.
paras.zh: 因此，光束永远不会与任何在时间中移动的实体的路径成 90 度角（正交）——就像一个粒子或一个带有写满中奖彩票号码的记事本的时间旅行者——这意味着一定的数量总是在他们的旅程中增加，所以他们永远不会回环。

paras.en: In other words, in such universes only forward movement is possible. As if driving down an endless one-way street with no service roads, turnarounds, or even an extended shoulder where one could pull over to enact a sneaky (illegal) U-turn.
paras.zh: 换句话说，在这样的宇宙中，只有向前运动是可能的。就好像沿着一条无尽的单行道行驶，没有辅助道路、转弯，甚至没有延伸的路肩，人们可以靠边停车偷偷地（非法）掉头。

paras.en: And, really, this is the basis of time travel, which has much different definitions depending on whether one is talking science or science fiction:
paras.zh: 事实上，这就是时间旅行的基础，根据人们谈论的是科学还是科幻小说，它有很多不同的定义：

paras.en: "People expect a result about time travel to need heavy machinery, energy conditions, quantum effects, maybe a singularity. It needs none of that. The whole content is bookkeeping about directions," Zhang adds.
paras.zh: “人们期望关于时间旅行的结果需要重型机械、能源条件、量子效应，也许还有奇点。它不需要这些。整个内容都是关于方向的簿记，”张补充道。

paras.en: The equational model used in this work offers a fourth family of criteria to prohibit closed time loops, supplementing the following three families:
paras.zh: 这项工作中使用的方程模型提供了第四个系列的标准来禁止闭合时间循环，补充了以下三个系列：

paras.en: First, the time function criteria state that time loops are ruled out if a universal clock can be defined that always ticks forward along every possible path.
paras.zh: 首先，时间函数标准规定，如果可以定义一个始终沿着每个可能路径向前滴答的通用时钟，则排除时间循环。

paras.en: Second, the energy condition criteria mandate that energy and gravity work in non-negative ways, disallowing time travel because it would require negative energy or "exotic matter".
paras.zh: 其次，能量条件标准要求能量和重力以非负的方式起作用，不允许时间旅行，因为它需要负能量或“奇异物质”。

paras.en: Third, topological criteria deal with the shape and connectivity of spacetime, linking time loops to the structure of the boundary where a time-travel region would begin.
paras.zh: 第三，拓扑标准涉及时空的形状和连通性，将时间循环与时间旅行区域开始的边界结构联系起来。

paras.en: Fortunately, this work adds an extra tool to theorists' time-traveling toolkit, allowing a relatively easy algebraic way to rule out numerical time-travel scenarios without messy mathematics that account for the greater Universe and its chaos.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，这项工作为理论家的时间旅行工具箱添加了一个额外的工具，允许一种相对简单的代数方法来排除数值时间旅行场景，而无需使用混乱的数学来解释更大的宇宙及其混乱。

paras.en: Another unexpected revelation is that one needs to find a way to turn part of the Universe into a churro to create a closed, time-traveling loop.
paras.zh: 另一个意想不到的启示是，人们需要找到一种方法将宇宙的一部分变成油条，以创建一个封闭的时间旅行循环。

paras.en: "So the surprise is that a question about the causal structure of an entire universe collapses into one scalar equation, and that the culprit is not spin. It is twist."
paras.zh: “所以令人惊讶的是，关于整个宇宙因果结构的问题可以分解为一个标量方程，而罪魁祸首不是自旋。而是扭曲。”

paras.en: Indeed, this is one of two escape routes that would allow time loops to exist, because a "sufficient condition is useful only if we know how it can fail."
paras.zh: 事实上，这是允许时间循环存在的两条逃生路线之一，因为“只有当我们知道它如何失败时，充分条件才有用。”

paras.en: As hinted, both escapes basically rely on spacetime folding back on itself to create a loop. This could happen locally, such as around a massive spinning black hole that turns spacetime into a pretzel, or if the layout of the Universe somehow doubles back on itself topologically.
paras.zh: 正如所暗示的，两种逃逸基本上都依赖于时空自身折叠来创建一个循环。这可能发生在局部，例如在一个巨大的旋转黑洞周围，将时空变成椒盐卷饼，或者如果宇宙的布局以某种方式在拓扑上加倍回来。

paras.en: Overall, this work splits the Universe based on light, rather than by moments of spacetime, which sidesteps our understanding of time.
paras.zh: 总的来说，这项工作是根据光而不是时空时刻来分裂宇宙，这回避了我们对时间的理解。

paras.en: "It is accurate to say we slice spacetime by light rather than by space. But the slices are not the paths of light; they are surfaces that light itself can inhabit."
paras.zh: “准确地说，我们是用光而不是空间来切片时空。但切片不是光的路径；它们是光本身可以居住的表面。”

paras.en: "Why does this help? An ordinary slice of space requires you to choose a moment, a moment requires a clock, and a clock requires an observer. A slice of light requires none of these. It is fixed by the geometry alone," Zhang explains.
paras.zh: “为什么这有帮助？一块普通的空间需要你选择一个时刻，一个时刻需要一个时钟，而一个时钟需要一个观察者。一片光不需要这些。它仅由几何形状固定，”张解释道。

paras.en: Finally, this offers a thought-and-math experiment of the type that has been influential throughout scientific history, allowing us to explore the abstruse principles that define our existence and possibilities.
paras.zh: 最后，这提供了一种在整个科学史上具有影响力的思想和数学实验，使我们能够探索定义我们的存在和可能性的深奥原理。

paras.en: But the Universe, as always, has the final say, Zhang concludes:
paras.zh: 但宇宙一如既往，拥有最终决定权，张总结道：

paras.en: "What it does not do is tell us whether nature permits any of this. That remains open, and it is the question I would most like to see answered."
paras.zh: “它没有告诉我们大自然是否允许这样做。这个问题仍然悬而未决，也是我最希望看到答案的问题。”

paras.en: But we are a step closer: "If you want a time machine, you now know exactly what you must break."
paras.zh: 但我们更近了一步：“如果你想要一台时间机器，你现在就知道必须打破什么。”

paras.en: The research has not yet been peer-reviewed, but a preprint is available on arXiv.
paras.zh: 该研究尚未经过同行评审，但 arXiv 上提供了预印本。

articles.title: A Huge Earthquake in Japan 7,300 Years Ago Pushed The Limits of Human Resourcefulness
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: The Kikai-Akahoya volcanic eruption is one of the most destructive in history:
paras.zh: Kikai-Akahoya 火山喷发是历史上最具破坏性的火山喷发之一：

paras.en: Around 5250 BCE, almost 7,300 years ago, off the southwestern coast of Japan, it spewed massive amounts of magma and volcanic material from beneath the seabed in a series of blasts.
paras.zh: 大约在公元前 5250 年，也就是近 7,300 年前，日本西南海岸附近发生了一系列爆炸，从海底喷出了大量岩浆和火山物质。

paras.en: For the Jomon foraging communities of Japan at that time, it must've been a cataclysmic event of incomprehensible proportions. Scoring 7 out of 8 on the volcanic explosivity index, it's the sort of event that happens once every 500–1,000 years.
paras.zh: 对于当时日本的绳纹觅食社区来说，这一定是一场难以理解的灾难性事件。火山爆发指数为 7 分（满分 8 分），这种事件每 500-1000 年就会发生一次。

paras.en: Since evidence for the eruption was first discovered in the 1970s, experts have debated what its impacts were.
paras.zh: 自从 20 世纪 70 年代首次发现火山爆发的证据以来，专家们一直在争论其影响是什么。

paras.en: Clearly, the damage done by the eruption would've been extensive – but it's not clear if and when surrounding societies were able to recover, and to what extent, in the years that followed.
paras.zh: 显然，火山喷发造成的损害将是巨大的，但尚不清楚周边社会是否能够、何时能够恢复，以及在接下来的几年里恢复到什么程度。

paras.en: In a new study published in Science Advances, an international team of researchers has taken a closer look at the consequences of the Kikai-Akahoya volcanic eruption, finding that in some areas at least, humans were more resourceful and adaptable than had previously been thought.
paras.zh: 在《科学进展》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，一个国际研究小组仔细研究了 Kikai-Akahoya 火山喷发的后果，发现至少在某些地区，人类比以前想象的更足智多谋、适应能力更强。

paras.en: "This eruption must have been devastating, exploding out of the seabed with little warning," says archaeologist Peter Jordan, from Lund University in Sweden.
paras.zh: 瑞典隆德大学的考古学家彼得乔丹说：“这次火山喷发一定是毁灭性的，在没有任何预警的情况下从海底爆炸出来。”

paras.en: "It battered the Japanese islands with powerful earthquakes and enormous tsunamis, and then blanketed the landscape with meters of volcanic ash."
paras.zh: “它以强烈的地震和巨大的海啸袭击了日本岛屿，然后用数米厚的火山灰覆盖了大地。”

paras.en: The researchers looked at 540 existing archaeological samples collected across Japan, dated from 8,000 to 6,500 years ago – several hundred years before and after the eruption.
paras.zh: 研究人员对日本各地收集的 540 个现有考古样本进行了研究，这些样本的年代可追溯到 8,000 至 6,500 年前，即火山喷发前后的数百年。

paras.en: By tracking how many radiocarbon-dated finds (such as charcoal or bones) came from before and after the eruption in each region, they were able to assess population activity.
paras.zh: 通过追踪每个地区火山爆发前后有多少放射性碳测年发现物（例如木炭或骨头），他们能够评估人口活动。

paras.en: Some parts of the impact zone became uninhabitable for a very long time, the researchers found.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，撞击区的某些部分在很长一段时间内变得无法居住。

paras.en: In other areas, there was evidence of people moving to new places, learning new skills, and adapting to a new way of life.
paras.zh: 在其他地区，有证据表明人们搬到新的地方，学习新的技能，并适应新的生活方式。

paras.en: "The disaster caused major loss of life," says archaeologist Enrico Crema, from Cambridge University in the UK.
paras.zh: 英国剑桥大学的考古学家恩里科·克雷马说：“这场灾难造成了重大人员伤亡。”

paras.en: "However, survivors migrated, forged new social relations, innovated new kinds of economy, and appear to have found creative ways to exist and later thrive in the new post-disaster conditions."
paras.zh: “然而，幸存者迁移，建立了新的社会关系，创新了新型经济，似乎找到了创造性的生存方式，并在新的灾后条件下蓬勃发展。”

paras.en: The researchers found that traditional Jomon forager populations may already have been declining in southern Kyushu, closest to the eruption, even before it happened.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，在距离火山喷发最近的九州南部，甚至在火山喷发之前，传统绳纹觅食者的数量可能就已经在下降。

paras.en: In contrast, the size and number of communities in the north of the island were on the rise before the eruption – and this trend continued afterward. This resilience may be evidence of affected groups moving away from the disaster area, the study suggests.
paras.zh: 相比之下，该岛北部社区的规模和数量在火山喷发前一直在增加，而且这种趋势在喷发后仍在继续。研究表明，这种恢复力可能是受影响群体离开灾区的证据。

paras.en: Marine life seems to have recovered the quickest, and the movement of Japan's prehistoric people followed. The researchers suggest inland survivors may have made their way to the coasts and adapted to a new way of living there.
paras.zh: 海洋生物似乎恢复得最快，日本史前人类的迁徙也紧随其后。研究人员认为，内陆幸存者可能已经前往海岸并适应了那里的新生活方式。

paras.en: "Even in the most impossible situations, survivors and communities have choices, however limited," says Jordan.
paras.zh: “即使在最不可能的情况下，幸存者和社区也有选择，无论选择多么有限，”乔丹说。

paras.en: "They need to act and make decisions; they need to adjust, collaborate, and find new connections and social networks."
paras.zh: “他们需要采取行动并做出决定；他们需要调整、协作并寻找新的联系和社交网络。”

paras.en: The researchers also found that some more distant areas of Japan, such as around Ise Bay, where population numbers had been increasing, saw this growth halt and even decline in certain areas.
paras.zh: 研究人员还发现，日本一些较远的地区，例如伊势湾周围，人口数量一直在增加，但某些地区的人口增长停止甚至下降。

paras.en: The team thinks this may be due to short-term cooling triggered by the eruption or an as-yet-unidentified effect of climate change.
paras.zh: 研究小组认为，这可能是由于火山喷发引发的短期降温或气候变化尚未确定的影响所致。

paras.en: Or it may possibly be down to a loss of food sources: Grazing in ash-covered landscapes may have worn down the teeth of deer and boar, shortening their lives.
paras.zh: 或者可能是由于食物来源的丧失：在灰烬覆盖的地区放牧可能磨损了鹿和野猪的牙齿，缩短了它们的寿命。

paras.en: The findings give us a better idea of how humankind can respond to natural disasters and dig deep to survive – something which is becoming ever more relevant in a world that's seeing major shifts in climate and weather.
paras.zh: 这些发现让我们更好地了解人类如何应对自然灾害并深入挖掘生存——这在气候和天气发生重大变化的世界中变得越来越重要。

paras.en: "This study helps in creating a deeper understanding of the contingent ways in which cultures and societies cope with sudden shocks and catastrophes," says Jordan.
paras.zh: 乔丹说：“这项研究有助于更深入地了解文化和社会应对突发冲击和灾难的偶然方式。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two

paras.en: Scientists just found a loophole that could let black holes split in two
paras.zh: 科学家刚刚发现了一个可以让黑洞一分为二的漏洞

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered a possible loophole in the laws that normally prevent black holes from splitting apart, suggesting that extremely fast-spinning black holes might divide into two. The surprising finding raises the possibility of an entirely new black hole phenomenon that future telescopes could potentially detect.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现了通常阻止黑洞分裂的法律中可能存在的漏洞，这表明旋转速度极快的黑洞可能会一分为二。这一令人惊讶的发现提出了未来望远镜可能探测到的全新黑洞现象的可能性。

paras.en: Black holes are known for merging when two of them collide, but could the reverse ever happen? Could a single black hole somehow divide into two smaller ones? A new theoretical study suggests that this extraordinary possibility may not be entirely ruled out by physics, although the conditions required would be extreme.
paras.zh: 众所周知，黑洞在两个碰撞时会合并，但相反的情况会发生吗？一个黑洞能否以某种方式分裂成两个较小的黑洞？一项新的理论研究表明，物理学可能无法完全排除这种非凡的可能性，尽管所需的条件非常极端。

paras.en: The research, published in Physical Review D under the title "When Black Holes Admit Pair-of-pants Topologies," examines the physical laws that keep black holes intact and whether certain circumstances could allow them to break apart.
paras.zh: 这项研究发表在《物理评论 D》上，标题为“当黑洞承认裤子拓扑时”，研究了保持黑洞完整的物理定律，以及某些情况是否会允许它们分裂。

paras.en: "In our study, we investigate which physical laws normally prevent a black hole from splitting into two. We also investigate if certain circumstances may allow a split to happen," says Francesco Sannino, co-author of the study and a professor of physics at University of Naples Federico II in Italy and Quantum Field Theory Center at University of Southern Denmark.
paras.zh: 该研究的合著者、意大利那不勒斯费德里科二世大学和南丹麦大学量子场论中心的物理学教授弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺（Francesco Sannino）表示：“在我们的研究中，我们研究了哪些物理定律通常会阻止黑洞分裂成两半。我们还研究了某些情况是否可能允许分裂发生。”

paras.en: The research team also included Giacomo Cacciapaglia, a researcher with the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) at the Laboratoire de Physique Théorique et Hautes Énergies, a joint CNRS and Sorbonne Université laboratory in Paris. Additional contributors were Manuel Del Piano and Vania Vellucci, both from the Quantum Field Theory Center at the University of Southern Denmark.
paras.zh: 该研究小组还包括法国国家科学研究中心（CNRS）物理理论和高级能源实验室（法国国家科学研究中心和巴黎索邦大学的联合实验室）的研究员贾科莫·卡恰帕利亚（Giacomo Cacciapaglia）。其他贡献者包括来自南丹麦大学量子场论中心的 Manuel Del Piano 和 Vania Vellucci。

paras.en: Why Black Holes Normally Cannot Split Apart
paras.zh: 为什么黑洞通常不能分裂

paras.en: One of the biggest obstacles to a black hole splitting comes from thermodynamics, the branch of physics that governs how energy behaves and how physical systems change.
paras.zh: 黑洞分裂的最大障碍之一来自热力学，它是控制能量行为和物理系统如何变化的物理学分支。

paras.en: A central concept is entropy, which describes how many different microscopic arrangements a system can have while appearing unchanged from the outside. Black holes have entropy, and this property places important limits on what can happen to them.
paras.zh: 一个核心概念是熵，它描述了一个系统在从外部看起来没有变化的情况下可以有多少种不同的微观排列。黑洞具有熵，这一特性对它们可能发生的事情施加了重要的限制。

paras.en: For a black hole that is not rotating, dividing into two smaller black holes would reduce the total entropy. Such a decrease makes the process thermodynamically unfavorable, helping explain why black holes do not ordinarily break apart.
paras.zh: 对于不旋转的黑洞，分成两个较小的黑洞会减少总熵。这种减少使得该过程在热力学上不利，这有助于解释为什么黑洞通常不会分裂。

paras.en: However, the researchers found that the situation could change dramatically when a black hole spins at an exceptionally high speed.
paras.zh: 然而，研究人员发现，当黑洞以极高的速度旋转时，情况可能会发生巨大变化。

paras.en: Extreme Rotation Could Allow Black Holes to Split
paras.zh: 极端旋转可能导致黑洞分裂

paras.en: The team's calculations suggest that rapid rotation may create a narrow opening in the physical rules that normally prevent black holes from dividing. In principle, a sufficiently fast spinning black hole could overcome the usual thermodynamic restriction.
paras.zh: 该团队的计算表明，快速旋转可能会在通常阻止黑洞分裂的物理规则中产生一个狭窄的开口。原则上，足够快旋转的黑洞可以克服通常的热力学限制。

paras.en: But there is another major obstacle. Even if a black hole could divide, the two resulting objects would need to move far enough apart to avoid immediately merging again.
paras.zh: 但还有另一个主要障碍。即使黑洞可以分裂，产生的两个物体也需要移动得足够远，以避免立即再次合并。

paras.en: "But the two resulting black holes must also be able to separate rather than immediately fall back together. When we include this requirement, the window largely closes again, except possibly for black holes rotating close to their maximum possible rate," says Francesco Sannino.
paras.zh: “但是由此产生的两个黑洞也必须能够分离，而不是立即回落到一起。当我们考虑到这一要求时，窗口基本上会再次关闭，除非黑洞旋转速度接近其最大可能速度，”弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺说。

paras.en: The study's unusual title refers to the shape that a black hole's boundary would trace through space and time if such a split occurred. This boundary, called the horizon, would begin as a single structure before separating into two distinct branches.
paras.zh: 这项研究的不同寻常的标题指的是如果发生这种分裂，黑洞的边界在空间和时间上所描绘出的形状。这个边界称为地平线，最初是一个单一的结构，然后分成两个不同的分支。

paras.en: Viewed across time, the resulting shape would resemble a pair of trousers, with one upper section dividing into two "legs." This is the idea behind the term "pair-of-pants topologies."
paras.zh: 从时间上看，最终的形状类似于一条裤子，上半部分分为两条“腿”。这就是术语“裤子拓扑”背后的想法。

paras.en: Extra Dimensions Offer Another Possibility
paras.zh: 额外的尺寸提供了另一种可能性

paras.en: The researchers also investigated more unusual scenarios involving theories in which space has additional dimensions beyond the three we experience in everyday life.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了更不寻常的场景，其中涉及的理论是，空间具有超出我们日常生活中所经历的三个维度的额外维度。

paras.en: Physicists have already identified objects resembling black holes in some of these theoretical models that can become unstable and start breaking apart. These possibilities suggest that the familiar rules governing black holes may not apply in the same way under more exotic conditions.
paras.zh: 物理学家已经在其中一些理论模型中发现了类似黑洞的物体，这些物体可能会变得不稳定并开始分裂。这些可能性表明，在更奇特的条件下，熟悉的黑洞规则可能不会以同样的方式适用。

paras.en: In certain cases, splitting could even become thermodynamically favorable, especially when one of the two resulting black holes is much smaller than the other.
paras.zh: 在某些情况下，分裂甚至可能在热力学上变得有利，特别是当产生的两个黑洞之一比另一个小得多时。

paras.en: However, a process being allowed or favored by thermodynamics does not necessarily mean it will happen. Researchers still need to determine whether such fragmentation can physically occur and what conditions would make it possible.
paras.zh: 然而，热力学允许或支持的过程并不一定意味着它会发生。研究人员仍然需要确定这种碎片是否会在物理上发生以及什么条件可以实现。

paras.en: Could Astronomers Detect a Black Hole Splitting?
paras.zh: 天文学家能探测到黑洞分裂吗？

paras.en: The scientists are now working to better understand how likely these events might be. The answer may depend on aspects of gravity that go beyond Einstein's theory, making the problem especially challenging.
paras.zh: 科学家们现在正在努力更好地了解这些事件发生的可能性。答案可能取决于超出爱因斯坦理论的引力方面，这使得这个问题特别具有挑战性。

paras.en: "We cannot yet give a single probability for a black hole to split. It depends on how gravity behaves beyond Einstein's theory, and we are working to quantify this. We expect small primordial black holes to be more prone to splitting than much larger astrophysical black holes. We may detect a split indirectly: gamma-ray telescopes such as Fermi-LAT can search for signals from tiny black-hole fragments that might form during mergers," says Francesco Sannino.
paras.zh: “我们还不能给出黑洞分裂的单一概率。这取决于引力在爱因斯坦理论之外的表现，我们正在努力量化这一点。我们预计小型原始黑洞比大得多的天体物理黑洞更容易分裂。我们可以间接检测到分裂：像费米-LAT这样的伽马射线望远镜可以从合并过程中可能形成的微小黑洞碎片中搜索信号，”弗朗西斯科·桑尼诺说。

paras.en: Although there is currently no confirmed observation of a black hole splitting, the possibility of detecting signals from tiny fragments offers a potential way to investigate the idea.
