paras.en: Feltman: So is there any controversy about whether what OpenAI and Anthropic are presenting are actually solutions to these problems, that they’re solved?
paras.zh: Feltman：那么 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 所提出的内容是否实际上是这些问题的解决方案，是否已经解决，是否存在任何争议？

paras.en: Hall: Right. So that’s the other side of the coin is that, usually, you know, math research is published in journals or on preprint servers or in conferences. It’s discussed among mathematicians.
paras.zh: 霍尔：对。 So that’s the other side of the coin is that, usually, you know, math research is published in journals or on preprint servers or in conferences. It’s discussed among mathematicians.

paras.en: These don’t really follow the same blueprint there. These are just kind of, like, put in GitHub repos as just a collection of AI-generated text and programming that they claim not only shows that the result is true but also has verified it in a programming language called Lean, which is meant specifically for mathematics.
paras.zh: 这些并没有真正遵循相同的蓝图。 These are just kind of, like, put in GitHub repos as just a collection of AI-generated text and programming that they claim not only shows that the result is true but also has verified it in a programming language called Lean, which is meant specifically for mathematics.

paras.en: So definitely the aspect of, like, how intelligible these results are and what kind of insights people are gaining from them has been a huge point of controversy—and you know, who gets the credit when a model is just outputting a bunch of ideas that we don’t really know exactly what they’re building off of.
paras.zh: 因此，这些结果的可理解性以及人们从中获得什么样的见解肯定是一个巨大的争议点——而且你知道，当一个模型只是输出一堆我们并不真正知道它们是基于什么构建的想法时，谁会得到功劳。

paras.en: Feltman: It’s like when that monkey took a selfie, except I had more respect for both the monkey and the photographer than I unfortunately do for a lot of AI companies. Well, what are the potential benefits to the mathematics community of these proofs being out there? You know, are there any upsides?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：就像那只猴子自拍一样，只不过我对猴子和摄影师的尊重比对许多人工智能公司的尊重要多。 Well, what are the potential benefits to the mathematics community of these proofs being out there?你知道，有什么好处吗？

paras.en: Hall: You know with previous drops, there has been efforts from the communities to go through the proof, really, you know, with a very fine-tooth comb and turn it into something that is expository and something that we can look at the techniques for and really understand some sort of mathematical insight for it.
paras.zh: Hall：你知道，在之前的发布中，社区一直在努力仔细地梳理证明，并将其变成说明性的东西，我们可以研究其技术并真正理解其某种数学见解。

paras.en: You know, the hope is that solutions like these and the proof steps, even if they’re not written the best right now, can at some point down the line be turned into something that is useful. Like, you know, I can use the ideas from this to solve some other problem that I’ve seen elsewhere in my research.
paras.zh: 你知道，我们希望像这样的解决方案和证明步骤，即使它们现在写得不是最好的，也能在未来的某个时刻变成有用的东西。就像，你知道，我可以利用其中的想法来解决我在研究中其他地方看到的其他问题。

paras.en: Feltman: Well thank you so much for coming on to talk through this with us.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：非常感谢您接受我们的采访。

paras.en: Feltman: Now for some research on an extremely timely subject: daylight saving time. DST just ended for those of us in the United States—not counting several territories, including Puerto Rico, and the exempt states Hawaii and Arizona,minus the Navajo Nation, which does still observe DST. Complicated, right? And it’s not like “springing forward” and “falling back” are much fun to deal with, either. Research suggests that shifting our clocks back and forth by an hour takes a toll on the body and the mind.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：现在对一个非常及时的主题进行一些研究：夏令时。对于我们这些在美国的人来说，夏令时刚刚结束——不包括包括波多黎各在内的几个领土，以及豁免州夏威夷和亚利桑那州，不包括仍然遵守夏令时的纳瓦霍族保留地。 Complicated, right?而且“前进”和“后退”也不是很有趣。研究表明，将时钟来回调整一小时会对身体和精神造成损害。

paras.en: So it’s not surprising that this practice is pretty unpopular, and you might have celebrated when the House of Representatives passed the Sunshine Protection Act in July. That bill, which has yet to clear the Senate, would make DST permanent and therefore “preserve” an hour of afternoon sunlight as we head deeper into fall. Last week President Donald Trump blasted the Senate for failing to take a vote in time to implement permanent DST this year, claiming in a social media post that literally no one wanted to change their clocks. While that’s characteristically hyperbolic, recent survey data does suggest that almost half of U.S. adults are opposed to all the falling and springing.
paras.zh: 因此，这种做法非常不受欢迎也就不足为奇了，当众议院 7 月份通过《阳光保护法案》时，您可能会庆祝。该法案尚未获得参议院批准，该法案将使夏令时永久化，从而在我们进入深秋时“保留”一个小时的午后阳光。上周，唐纳德·特朗普总统抨击参议院今年未能及时投票实施永久性夏令时，并在社交媒体上发帖称，实际上没有人愿意改变自己的时钟。虽然这是典型的双曲线，但最近的调查数据确实表明，近一半的美国成年人反对所有的跌倒和反弹。

paras.en: But according to a new analysis published in Current Biology, making DST permanent could have serious, dangerous consequences for school-age children. Researchers at the University of Washington who study how school start times impact adolescent health decided to quantify exactly how many more trips to school would happen in darkness if we switched to year-round DST. They found that the Sunshine Protection Act would lead to more than two billion dark morning commutes for children. They also confirmed that fatal morning crashes involving kids aged five to 18 are more likely to occur if the sun has yet to rise. So those additional dark commutes really do pose a risk.
paras.zh: 但根据《当代生物学》发表的一项新分析，永久实行夏令时可能会给学龄儿童带来严重、危险的后果。华盛顿大学研究开学时间如何影响青少年健康的研究人员决定量化，如果我们改用全年夏令时，在黑暗中上学的次数将会增加。他们发现，阳光保护法案将导致超过 20 亿儿童在黑暗的早晨通勤。他们还证实，如果太阳尚未升起，涉及 5 至 18 岁儿童的致命早晨车祸更有可能发生。因此，这些额外的黑暗通勤确实会带来风险。

paras.en: The researchers aren’t arguing in favor of continuing to swap our clocks back and forth; in fact, they point out that while permanent DST would be the worst-case scenario for dark school commutes, our current system creates twice as many dark mornings as would occur under permanent standard time.
paras.zh: 研究人员并不赞成继续来回调换我们的时钟；而是赞成继续调换我们的时钟。事实上，他们指出，虽然永久夏令时将是黑暗学校通勤的最坏情况，但我们当前的系统造成的黑暗早晨是永久标准时间下的两倍。

paras.en: Listen: I’m as bummed out by an afternoon sunset as anyone else. But as long as we can get rid of the twice-a-year upheaval, I’m personally good with whatever. And keeping kids safe as they wait for the bus—or, even better, as they walk or bike to school, because we love a pedestrian-friendly commute—seems pretty worthwhile to me.
paras.zh: 听着：我和其他人一样对下午的日落感到沮丧。但只要我们能够摆脱每年两次的动荡，我个人就可以接受任何事情。在我看来，确保孩子们在等公交车时的安全——或者更好的是，在他们步行或骑自行车上学时，因为我们喜欢步行或骑自行车上学——对我来说似乎非常值得。

paras.en: That’s all for this week’s science news roundup. We’ll be back on Wednesday to talk about how soybeans quietly swept the nation and on Friday we’re going to talk about how AI swept everywhere.
paras.zh: 这就是本周科学新闻综述的全部内容。我们将在周三回来讨论大豆如何悄然席卷全国，周五我们将讨论人工智能如何席卷各地。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great week!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。祝你度过愉快的一周！

articles.title: How to tell if a voice recording is AI-generated

paras.en: I’ve long been intrigued by the technology needed to virtually clone my own voice. Just three years ago this effort involved multiple hours of recorded speech and a host of specialized tools to create a quick quote that sounded even remotely like me. Now I can do it with just a few seconds of audio and a couple of clicks—and it takes an expert to recognize that it’s fake.
paras.zh: 长期以来，我一直对虚拟克隆自己的声音所需的技术很感兴趣。就在三年前，这项工作涉及多个小时的录音语音和大量专用工具来创建听起来甚至与我有一点相似的快速引言。现在，我只需几秒钟的音频和几次点击就可以做到这一点，而且需要专家才能识别出它是假的。

paras.en: Why would I do this? I have a background in acoustic analysis, and as the technology has advanced, I’ve been curious to test it and track any tells that reveal the clone as a fake. So last week I again cloned my voice, this time using a free, open-source tool. If that sounds easy, it’s because it is, says Sarah Barrington, a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Berkeley, who studies artificial intelligence voice cloning. At most, a cloning service might ask the user to affirm their right to copy a voice.
paras.zh: 我为什么要这样做？ I have a background in acoustic analysis, and as the technology has advanced, I’ve been curious to test it and track any tells that reveal the clone as a fake.因此，上周我再次克隆了我的声音，这次使用的是免费的开源工具。 If that sounds easy, it’s because it is, says Sarah Barrington, a doctoral candidate at the University of California, Berkeley, who studies artificial intelligence voice cloning.克隆服务最多可能会要求用户确认他们复制声音的权利。

paras.en: “There are platforms online that will advertise as few as three seconds’ worth of someone’s voice to create a clone,” Barrington says. Voice cloning, she explains, went, “kind of overnight, from quite technical to immediately consumer-accessible.” In a demonstration in her lectures, for example, Barrington clones her own voice from a YouTube clip in a mere 90 seconds.
paras.zh: 巴林顿说：“有些在线平台会宣传某人的声音，只需三秒钟即可创建克隆。”她解释说，语音克隆“一夜之间就从技术性很强变成了消费者可以立即使用的技术”。例如，在她的讲座演示中，Barrington 仅用了 90 秒就从 YouTube 剪辑中克隆了自己的声音。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: This level of accessibility has drawn the attention of scammers. Reuters reported in September that someone posing as a lawyer and using a cloned voice persuaded a large Italian private bank to wire around €95 million (about $105 million) abroad.
paras.zh: 这种级别的可访问性引起了诈骗者的注意。路透社 9 月份报道称，有人冒充律师并使用克隆声音说服一家大型意大利私人银行向国外电汇约 9500 万欧元（约合 1.05 亿美元）。

paras.en: Our ears are, in general, bad at distinguishing between real and cloned voices. Barrington and her colleagues conducted a study where they played real and cloned voices of 220 different speakers to more than 600 listeners. About half of these listeners were asked to flag voices they thought were artificially generated, and they did so successfully 60 percent of the time. In a separate test, when the other half of listeners heard a clone and a real speaker side by side, they judged them to be the same person about 80 percent of the time.
paras.zh: 一般来说，我们的耳朵不擅长区分真实的声音和克隆的声音。 Barrington 和她的同事进行了一项研究，他们向 600 多名听众播放​​ 220 个不同说话者的真实声音和克隆声音。 About half of these listeners were asked to flag voices they thought were artificially generated, and they did so successfully 60 percent of the time. In a separate test, when the other half of listeners heard a clone and a real speaker side by side, they judged them to be the same person about 80 percent of the time.

paras.en: In the past, cloned voices could be discerned based on breaths, pauses and disfluencies such as “ums.” Essentially, the voices were too polished—too unnatural. This is no longer the case. Ums, ahs, breaths and other inflections are now added intentionally to better mask the clone. Researchers are instead training AI models to detect clones based on measurements associated with the sound wave itself, a process involving something called audio forensics.
paras.zh: 过去，克隆声音可以根据呼吸、停顿和“嗯”等不连贯的声音来识别。从本质上讲，声音太优美了——太不自然了。现在情况已不再如此。现在故意添加了嗯、啊、呼吸和其他变化，以更好地掩盖克隆。研究人员正在训练人工智能模型，根据与声波本身相关的测量结果来检测克隆，这一过程涉及到音频取证。

paras.en: By zooming in on the waveform of my own voice far enough, I can see each tiny vibration of my own vocal folds as a repetitive bump in signal. Tiny variations in the length of those cycles, known as jitter, and the height of their peaks, known as shimmer, are some of the many features that can be weighed together by a detection model to tell if a voice is AI-generated.
paras.zh: 通过将自己声音的波形放大得足够远，我可以将自己声带的每一个微小振动视为信号中的重复凸起。这些周期长度的微小变化（称为抖动）和峰值高度（称为闪烁）是检测模型可以权衡的众多特征中的一部分，以判断语音是否是人工智能生成的。

paras.en: Even the best detectors have blind spots, however. AI models can be tuned to detect the signatures of one cloning company’s tools or perhaps a few, but that ability “often does not transfer well to other providers,” Barrington says. For example, spectral analysis, which visualizes the change in audio frequencies over time, can reveal quirks of particular cloning tools, but there is no single measure that works across all of them.
paras.zh: 然而，即使是最好的探测器也有盲点。巴林顿说，可以调整人工智能模型来检测一个或几个克隆公司工具的签名，但这种能力“通常不能很好地转移到其他提供商”。例如，频谱分析可以可视化音频随时间的变化，可以揭示特定克隆工具的怪癖，但没有一种方法可以适用于所有这些工具。

paras.en: “You would expect to immediately see giveaways,” Barrington says. “That is absolutely not the case.” In other words, no single measurement can show that a recording is fake. You need a suite of tools. (To further complicate things, a phone call minimizes or degrades much of a voice’s key forensic detail, making clones even harder to spot.)
paras.zh: “You would expect to immediately see giveaways,” Barrington says. “绝对不是这样的。” In other words, no single measurement can show that a recording is fake.您需要一套工具。 (To further complicate things, a phone call minimizes or degrades much of a voice’s key forensic detail, making clones even harder to spot.)

paras.en: In my own testing, I compared two dozen sentences that I had spoken and the clone’s versions of the same sentences. Sentences recorded with a heater humming in the background showed that the clone’s jitter was statistically indistinguishable from mine, though its shimmer was steadier. In a quiet room, however, the clone came out measurably cleaner, with less noise under the tone in all 12 sentences, even after a simulated phone call.
paras.zh: 在我自己的测试中，我比较了我说过的两打句子和克隆人的相同句子的版本。在背景中加热器嗡嗡作响的情况下记录的句子表明，克隆人的抖动在统计上与我的没有区别，尽管它的闪光更稳定。然而，在安静的房间里，即使在模拟电话通话之后，克隆的声音也明显干净得多，所有 12 个句子的语气中的噪音都更少。

paras.en: For now, one of the most promising ways to distinguish AI-cloned voices from real ones may be embedded in the cloning technology itself. Some companies that make AI audio tools, such as Google, hide an inaudible watermark in the created audio. This watermark makes small changes throughout the sound that are too faint to hear but can be read by a detector later—and these changes go with the audio file wherever it is shared.
paras.zh: 目前，区分人工智能克隆声音和真实声音的最有前途的方法之一可能是嵌入克隆技术本身。一些制造人工智能音频工具的公司（例如谷歌）在创建的音频中隐藏了听不见的水印。此水印会在整个声音中产生微小的变化，这些变化太微弱而无法听到，但稍后可以被检测器读取 - 并且这些变化会随着音频文件的共享而变化。

paras.en: These watermarks are powerful, but they are not foolproof; someone might alter a recording enough to erase such a mark. And even when they are available, they may not be required: watermarks are optional on some open-source programs that offer them. Still, Barrington says that, like a locked door, a good watermark can “keep out 99 [percent] of the bad cases.” And for the rest—our audio forensics techniques will have to keep evolving as fast as the cloning tools are.
paras.zh: 这些水印功能强大，但并非万无一失；有人可能会改变录音足以删除这样的标记。即使它们可用，也可能不是必需的：在某些提供水印的开源程序中，水印是可选的。尽管如此，巴林顿表示，就像一扇锁着的门一样，好的水印可以“阻止 99% 的不良情况”。对于其余的，我们的音频取证技术必须与克隆工具一样快速发展。

articles.title: This bull and donkey show interspecies homosexual bonds can run deep

paras.en: Of all the things you might see on your lunch break, a bull having sex with a male donkey is likely low on the list. But ecologists “always have an eye on the horizon,” says André Beirão da Cruz. And when he and fellow Ph.D. candidate Martina Francesconi stopped for a bite during a field research trip in Ethiopia, that is exactly what they saw.
paras.zh: 在你午休时可能看到的所有事物中，一头公牛与一头公驴发生性关系可能排在最后。但生态学家“始终关注地平线”，安德烈·贝朗·达·克鲁斯 (André Beirão da Cruz) 说。当他和他的博士同事。候选人玛蒂娜·弗朗西斯科尼 (Martina Francesconi) 在埃塞俄比亚实地考察期间停下来吃了一口，这正是他们所看到的。

paras.en: “We were not sure if we had actually seen it or if it was some type of mirage,” says da Cruz, who’s completing his Ph.D. in ecology at the University of Pisa in Italy and the NOVA University of Lisbon in Portugal.
paras.zh: “我们不确定我们是否真的看到过它，或者它是否是某种海市蜃楼，”即将完成博士学位的达克鲁兹说。意大利比萨大学和葡萄牙里斯本 NOVA 大学生态学博士学位。

paras.en: This is the story of Achille and Patroclo, a domesticated bull and a male donkey, respectively, that live on an Ethiopian plateau and often graze together. In a new paper, da Cruz and his colleagues describe the deep bond between the two animals, who were named for the ancient Greek hero Achilles and his lover Patroclus. During the ecologists’ observations, Achille and Patroclo’s relationship involved dozens of sexual interactions and indicated a strong social connection.
paras.zh: 这是阿奇勒和帕特罗克洛的故事，阿奇勒和帕特罗克洛分别是一头家牛和一头公驴，生活在埃塞俄比亚高原上，经常一起吃草。在一篇新论文中，达克鲁兹和他的同事描述了这两种动物之间深厚的联系，它们以古希腊英雄阿喀琉斯和他的情人帕特罗克洛斯的名字命名。在生态学家的观察中，阿奇勒和帕特罗克洛的关系涉及数十次性互动，表明了强大的社会联系。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The case study, the researchers say, may offer a window into the complexities of animals’ same-sex behaviors.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，该案例研究可能为了解动物同性行为的复杂性提供了一个窗口。

paras.en: “Most of the time, people and researchers start with an idea in the field, and they are focused on that in a very strict and tight way,” says Elisabetta Palagi, senior author of the paper and an ecologist at the University of Pisa. “But this prevents people from looking around, and it is possible that this kind of interaction is much more frequent than has been reported.”
paras.zh: “大多数时候，人们和研究人员都是从该领域的一个想法开始，他们会以非常严格和严格的方式专注于这个想法，”该论文的资深作者、比萨大学的生态学家 Elisabetta Palagi 说。 “但这阻止了人们环顾四周，而且这种互动可能比报道的要频繁得多。”

paras.en: Achille and Patroclo have different owners but often graze in the same field; the researchers observed them for four days together and four days apart. In the four days together, Achille mounted Patroclo 51 times.
paras.zh: Achille 和 Patroclo 有不同的主人，但经常在同一块田地里吃草；研究人员对它们进行了四天的观察和四天的观察。在四天内，阿基尔骑乘帕特罗克洛 51 次。

paras.en: Same-sex sexual behavior among animals is well studied, but ecologists know far less about interspecies sexual behavior. The reciprocity in Achille and Patroclo’s behavior was most notable, Francesconi says: Patroclo was receptive when Achille mounted him but aggressive when any other bull was nearby. And the two animals’ interactions often went beyond just mounting, with the pair licking or rubbing against each other after sexual interactions. This suggests that sexual relationships between animals are far more complex than our current understanding, Francesconi adds.
paras.zh: 动物间的同性性行为已得到充分研究，但生态学家对物种间性行为的了解却少得多。弗朗西斯科尼说，阿基勒和帕特罗克洛的行为中的互惠性最为显着：当阿基勒骑上他时，帕特罗克洛很乐意接受，但当附近有任何其他公牛时，帕特罗克洛就会表现出攻击性。这两种动物的互动往往不仅仅是骑乘，它们在性交后还会互相舔舐或摩擦。弗朗西斯科尼补充道，这表明动物之间的性关系比我们目前的理解复杂得多。

paras.en: Vincent Savolainen, an ecologist at Imperial College London, who was not involved in the work, says the authors “show quite nicely that these two are not just a random dyad.”
paras.zh: 伦敦帝国理工学院的生态学家文森特·萨沃莱宁（Vincent Savolainen）没有参与这项工作，他说作者“很好地表明，这两者不仅仅是随机的二元组。”

paras.en: He adds, however, that Achille and Patroclo’s domestication may mean that their behavior does not reflect social traits or patterns among wild animals.
paras.zh: 然而，他补充说，阿奇勒和帕特罗克洛的驯化可能意味着它们的行为并不反映野生动物的社会特征或模式。

paras.en: “It’s important to publish and publicize this example just to show the diversity of what can happen, but it is obviously limited to two animals from two species that are domesticated,” Savolainen says. “If we want to make massive steps in the field of behavior ecology, you would want to study a larger group of wild animals.”
paras.zh: “发布和宣传这个例子很重要，只是为了展示可能发生的事情的多样性，但它显然仅限于两个驯化物种的两种动物，”萨沃莱宁说。 “如果我们想在行为生态学领域取得重大进展，你就需要研究更多的野生动物。”

paras.en: “What we know about interspecies sexual interactions is scarce,” Francesconi says. “And it’s mostly connected with a subject forcing the other or mistaken identity or something randomly going on by chance. But what’s not present in the literature is something recurrent, selective, and somehow voluntary and reciprocal.”
paras.zh: “我们对物种间性行为的了解很少，”弗朗西斯科尼说。 “这主要与一个主体强迫另一个人或错误的身份或偶然发生的事情有关。但文献中没有出现的是反复出现的、选择性的、某种程度上自愿和互惠的东西。”

paras.en: The research was published today in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 该研究今天发表在《当代生物学》上。

articles.title: Seabirds get jet lag, too — and it can throw them a bit off course
articles.author: Anirban Mukhopadhyay

paras.en: Jet lag isn’t just for travelers hurtling across time zones. Migratory birds may get it, too.
paras.zh: 时差不仅仅适用于跨越时区的旅客。候鸟也可能会感染。

paras.en: Manx shearwaters (Puffinus puffinus) fly fast enough to experience jet lag, researchers report October 29 in Science. Decades of tracking data from foraging flights revealed that rapid east-west journeys can throw the seabirds’ internal clocks out of sync with local time, causing them to misjudge the sun’s position and veer slightly off course.
paras.zh: 研究人员 10 月 29 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，马恩岛海鸥（Puffinus puffinus）飞得足够快，足以经历时差反应。数十年的觅食飞行跟踪数据显示，快速的东西向飞行会使海鸟的内部时钟与当地时间不同步，导致它们误判太阳的位置并稍微偏离航线。

paras.en: For animals crossing vast oceans, the sun can help them determine which direction to fly. But because the sun’s position in the sky changes throughout the day, these animals need an internal clock synchronized with natural local sun time to use it as a compass. This circadian rhythm helps them compensate for the sun’s apparent movement and stay on course.
paras.zh: 对于穿越浩瀚海洋的动物来说，太阳可以帮助它们确定飞行的方向。但由于太阳在天空中的位置全天都在变化，因此这些动物需要一个与当地自然太阳时间同步的内部时钟来将其用作指南针。这种昼夜节律有助于它们补偿太阳的明显运动并保持在轨道上。

paras.en: But when birds zip east or west, local time shifts faster than their internal clocks might adjust. Scientists have long predicted that this mismatch could confound the birds’ sun-based compasses, but testing the idea in the wild “has seemed impossible until now,” says Tim Guilford, a biologist at the University of Oxford.
paras.zh: 但是，当鸟类向东或向西飞翔时，当地时间的变化速度比它们的内部时钟调整的速度要快。科学家们早就预测，这种不匹配可能会干扰鸟类基于太阳的指南针，但牛津大学生物学家蒂姆·吉尔福德表示，在野外测试这一想法“到目前为止似乎是不可能的”。

paras.en: Over 20 years, Guilford and colleagues equipped 1,045 breeding Manx shearwaters with miniature GPS trackers. The trackers logged thousands of trips from United Kingdom breeding colonies to feeding grounds up to 1,000 kilometers away. The team focused on the return journeys, isolating 1,837 continuous homeward flights.
paras.zh: 20 多年来，Guilford 及其同事为 1,045 只正在繁殖的马恩岛海鸥配备了微型 GPS 跟踪器。追踪器记录了从英国繁殖地到最远 1000 公里外的觅食地的数千次行程。团队重点关注返程航班，隔离了1837个连续返航航班。

paras.en: Assuming the seabirds’ internal clocks were synchronized with local time at sunrise, the researchers calculated how flights should throw off their sun compass and compared those predictions with GPS tracking data. The birds veered as expected, by as much as 15 degrees from their intended direction.
paras.zh: 假设海鸟的内部时钟与当地时间日出时同步，研究人员计算了航班应如何摆脱太阳罗盘，并将这些预测与 GPS 跟踪数据进行比较。鸟儿按照预期转向，偏离预定方向多达 15 度。

paras.en: “But what really surprised us is that the small orientation errors … continue to be visible even when the birds were in sight of presumably familiar land,” Guilford says. While following a coastline, the birds should be able to use it as a guide to keep their course. But they either veered closer to shore or farther out to sea in line with their predicted sun compass errors. The pattern suggests that the birds use the sun compass alongside coastal cues, even when the two point in different directions.
paras.zh: “但真正令我们惊讶的是，即使这些鸟看到了可能熟悉的土地，微小的方向误差……仍然可见，”吉尔福德说。当沿着海岸线飞行时，鸟类应该能够利用它作为指南来保持航线。但根据预测的太阳罗盘误差，它们要么靠近海岸，要么远离海洋。该模式表明，鸟类使用太阳罗盘和沿海线索，即使两者指向不同的方向。

paras.en: The errors are small enough that they add only a few kilometers to the journey, not enough to prevent the Manx shearwaters from finding their way home.
paras.zh: 这些误差足够小，只增加了几公里的路程，不足以阻止马恩岛海鸥找到回家的路。

paras.en: This navigational tug-of-war excites Sangeeta Rani, a chronobiologist at the University of Lucknow in India. The findings, Rani says, hint at an ability that could serve these feathered fliers well as climate change and human activities alter familiar landscapes: The birds seem to process and integrate multiple navigational cues without relying blindly on any one of them.
paras.zh: 这场导航拔河比赛让印度勒克瑙大学的时间生物学家桑吉塔·拉尼 (Sangeeta Rani) 兴奋不已。拉尼说，这些发现暗示了一种可以为这些有羽毛的飞行者服务的能力，以及气候变化和人类活动改变熟悉的景观：鸟类似乎可以处理和整合多种导航线索，而不是盲目依赖其中任何一个。

paras.en: “After all, if I have marked a path for myself in the woods, my innate ability is not to mindlessly follow the markings,” Rani says. “It is to find out what’s missing and still find my way back.”
paras.zh: “毕竟，如果我在树林里为自己标出了一条道路，我与生俱来的能力就不会盲目地跟随这些标记，”拉尼说。 “我的目​​的是找出丢失的东西，同时还能找到回来的路。”

articles.title: Melting permafrost has birthed a new type of large landslide
articles.author: Nikk Ogasa

paras.en: In 2018, a strange and enormous landslide occurred in Canada’s Northwest Territories. A slab of earth roughly equivalent in volume to seven Great Pyramids of Giza suddenly began sliding downhill, leaving behind a barren scar in the forested landscape. But what puzzled scientists was that the slide had initiated in frozen ground that had been glued in place for years.
paras.zh: 2018年，加拿大西北地区发生了一场奇怪的巨大山体滑坡。一块体积大约相当于七座吉萨大金字塔的土板突然开始滑下山坡，在森林景观中留下了一道贫瘠的疤痕。但令科学家们感到困惑的是，滑坡是在多年来被粘在原地的冰冻地面上开始的。

paras.en: An analysis of the event reveals that it represents a new class of catastrophic landslides called permafrost detachment slides, researchers report in the Sept. 28 Geophysical Research Letters. The slides may be set in motion by wildfires that occurred decades earlier, destabilizing the ground and opening cracks through which water infiltrated deep underground. Over time, that water may have thawed the frozen layer from below, eventually unleashing the entire frozen layer in a catastrophic slide.
paras.zh: 研究人员在 9 月 28 日的《地球物理研究快报》中报告说，对这一事件的分析表明，它代表了一种新的灾难性山体滑坡，称为永久冻土分离滑坡。这些滑坡可能是由几十年前发生的野火引发的，破坏了地面的稳定并打开了裂缝，水通过裂缝渗透到地下深处。随着时间的推移，水可能会从下面融化冰冻层，最终导致整个冰冻层发生灾难性的滑坡。

paras.en: Large landslides don’t normally mobilize so much still-frozen material, and when they do begin in thawing layers they usually move slowly, says Dmitry Nicolsky, a geophysicist studying permafrost at the University of Alaska Fairbanks who was not involved in the study. But he says this new research suggests scientists need to better study what’s occurring beneath the surface in permafrost regions, because “we don’t know how [the ground] will move — it might go slowly or it might go catastrophically.”
paras.zh: 阿拉斯加大学费尔班克斯分校研究永久冻土的地球物理学家德米特里·尼科尔斯基（Dmitry Nicolsky）没有参与这项研究，他说，大型山体滑坡通常不会移动那么多仍然冻结的物质，当它们开始融化时，它们通常会缓慢移动。但他表示，这项新研究表明科学家需要更好地研究永久冻土地区地表以下发生的情况，因为“我们不知道[地面]将如何移动——它可能会缓慢移动，也可能会发生灾难性的后果。”

paras.en: The inspiration for the research manifested in 2019, when permafrost geologist Joseph Young, based at the University of Alberta in Edmonton, Canada, at the time, was helicoptering to a field site in the Northwest Territories to assist a colleague’s research. In some of the valleys out there, the slopes were “just collapsing with landslides everywhere,” says Young, who is now at an engineering firm in Edmonton. That was surprising because they were in an area where the permafrost — ground that has been frozen for at least two consecutive years — shouldn’t have been thawing much.
paras.zh: 这项研究的灵感体现在 2019 年，当时加拿大埃德蒙顿阿尔伯塔大学的永久冻土地质学家约瑟夫·杨 (Joseph Young) 乘直升机前往西北地区的一个现场，协助同事的研究。现在在埃德蒙顿一家工程公司工作的杨说，在一些山谷中，斜坡“正在崩塌，到处都是山体滑坡”。这是令人惊讶的，因为他们所在的地区永久冻土——至少连续两年被冻结的土地——不应该融化太多。

paras.en: Once on the ground, more puzzling details emerged. “Traditionally with permafrost, it melts from the top down, and that releases this slurry of muddy material,” Young says. But at some of the landslide sites, large blocks of still-frozen ground seemed to have been moved hundreds of meters, he says.
paras.zh: 一旦到达地面，更多令人费解的细节就出现了。 “传统上，永久冻土是从上到下融化的，从而释放出泥浆，”杨说。但他说，在一些山体滑坡地点，大块仍然冰冻的地面似乎已经移动了数百米。

paras.en: Young and his colleagues studied two of the largest slides in the region that had moved big chunks of permafrost. These were the 2018 slide, which mobilized 18 million cubic meters of earth and dammed the Redstone River, and another event in 2017 that moved 4.5 million cubic meters of material.
paras.zh: 杨和他的同事研究了该地区两个最大的滑坡，这些滑坡移动了大块永久冻土。其中包括 2018 年的滑坡事件，该事件移动了 1800 万立方米的土方并在红石河上筑坝，以及 2017 年的另一次滑坡事件，移动了 450 万立方米的材料。

paras.en: Field observations revealed that both events had initiated along flat sliding surfaces roughly 20 meters underground, where the permafrost layer’s base was identified. Meanwhile, satellite observations showed that the ground at both sites had been gradually moving meters each year for decades.
paras.zh: 现场观察显示，这两次事件都是沿着地下约 20 米的平坦滑动表面开始的，那里是永久冻土层的底部。与此同时，卫星观测显示，几十年来，这两个地点的地面每年都在逐渐移动数米。

paras.en: Young and his colleagues hypothesized that climate warming and wildfire had somehow played a role in causing the slides. They set up instruments nearby that tracked ground temperature from 2020 to 2022, focusing on spots either with undisturbed forest or where wildfire had burned about 25 years earlier.
paras.zh: 杨和他的同事假设气候变暖和野火在某种程度上导致了滑坡。他们在附近安装了仪器，追踪 2020 年至 2022 年的地面温度，重点关注森林未受干扰或大约 25 年前曾发生野火的地点。

paras.en: They then plugged that data into computer simulations to estimate how the ground would have evolved in the decades after a fire. Based on the results, the researchers concluded that wildfire and extreme summer temperatures can warm and weaken the frozen ground surface, causing it to start creeping and form tension cracks. As these cracks grow, water can penetrate deeper into the frozen ground and eventually reach beneath the permafrost layer, causing it to thaw from below and eventually detach.
paras.zh: 然后，他们将这些数据输入计算机模拟中，以估计火灾后几十年内地面将如何演变。根据结果​​，研究人员得出结论，野火和夏季极端气温会使冰冻地表变暖并削弱其强度，导致其开始蠕变并形成张力裂缝。随着这些裂缝的扩大，水可以更深地渗入冰冻地面，最终到达永久冻土层下方，导致其从下方融化并最终分离。

paras.en: More than 150 other slides in the region, identified via satellite observations, may also have been permafrost detachment slides, Young says. This could occur wherever there’s a relatively thin and warm permafrost layer and a rapid warming event to set things in motion, he says.
paras.zh: Young 说，通过卫星观测发现，该地区还有 150 多个其他滑坡，也可能是永久冻土分离滑坡。他说，只要有相对薄而温暖的永久冻土层，并且有快速变暖事件推动事物运转，这种情况就可能发生。

paras.en: Permafrost is thawing in cold regions around the world, and these huge slides are very visual manifestations of that, Young says. “This is a direct reality of a changing climate.”
paras.zh: 杨说，世界各地寒冷地区的永久冻土正在融化，这些巨大的滑坡是这一现象的直观表现。 “这是气候变化的直接现实。”

articles.title: Newborn survival improves when families receive financial support
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: Extra financial support during pregnancy and after birth can help more babies thrive in their earliest days.
paras.zh: 怀孕期间和产后的额外经济支持可以帮助更多的婴儿在最初的日子里茁壮成长。

paras.en: The Rx Kids program in Flint, Mich., launched in January 2024, provides extra cash to pregnant residents and their infants, unconditionally. Researchers compared neonatal deaths — those in the first four weeks of life — in 2025 with those in 2021 through 2024 in Flint. The city’s neonatal mortality rate dropped from 10 deaths per 1,000 live births to 5 deaths per 1,000 live births, researchers report November 2 in JAMA Pediatrics. The early neonatal mortality rate, covering deaths in the first week of life, fell from 8 per 1,000 to 2. For the rest of Michigan, rates were stable over the study’s time period.
paras.zh: 密歇根州弗林特市的 Rx Kids 计划于 2024 年 1 月启动，无条件为怀孕居民及其婴儿提供额外现金。研究人员将弗林特 2025 年和 2021 年至 2024 年的新生儿死亡人数（出生后前 4 周内的死亡人数）进行了比较。研究人员 11 月 2 日在《美国医学会儿科杂志》上发表报告称，该市新生儿死亡率从每 1,000 名活产儿 10 人死亡降至每 1,000 名活产儿 5 人死亡。早期新生儿死亡率（涵盖生命第一周内的死亡）从千分之八降至千分之二。在密歇根州其他地区，死亡率在研究期间保持稳定。

paras.en: “As a pediatrician, there is no outcome more important than babies surviving,” says Mona Hanna of the Michigan State University College of Human Medicine in Flint, who is also the founder and director of Rx Kids. “These early findings suggest that something as simple as providing families with financial support during pregnancy and infancy may help save babies’ lives.”
paras.zh: “作为一名儿科医生，没有比婴儿存活下来更重要的结果了，”位于弗林特的密歇根州立大学人类医学学院的莫娜·汉纳 (Mona Hanna) 说道，她也是 Rx Kids 的创始人兼董事。 “这些早期发现表明，像在怀孕和婴儿期为家庭提供经济支持这样简单的事情可能有助于挽救婴儿的生命。”

paras.en: Income tends to drop and expenses rise in the months before and after a birth, making the perinatal period especially difficult financially for many families. Economic precarity can expose moms and babies to health harms. For example, housing instability and homelessness is associated with preterm birth and low birth weight.
paras.zh: 产前和产后几个月的收入往往会下降，支出会增加，这使得围产期对许多家庭来说在经济上尤其困难。经济不稳定会使妈妈和婴儿的健康受到损害。例如，住房不稳定和无家可归与早产和低出生体重有关。

paras.en: Backed by public and private funds, Rx Kids got started in Flint, a city with a high rate of child poverty that has been dealing with the public health fallout of lead contamination in the water distribution system. Nearly 100 percent of the community participates in the program. Flint families receive $1,500 once during pregnancy and $500 per month in the baby’s first year. Anyone who is a resident, at least 16 weeks pregnant or with a newborn up to six months old can enroll. Families have put the extra cash toward diapers, transportation, housing and safe places for their babies to sleep, Hanna says.
paras.zh: 在公共和私人资金的支持下，Rx Kids 在弗林特启动，这是一个儿童贫困率很高的城市，一直在应对供水系统铅污染对公共健康的影响。近 100% 的社区参与了该计划。弗林特家庭在怀孕期间可领取一次 1,500 美元，婴儿第一年每月可领取 500 美元。任何怀孕至少 16 周或新生儿不超过 6 个月的居民都可以报名。汉纳说，家庭将额外的现金用于购买尿布、交通、住房和婴儿安全的睡眠场所。

paras.en: “Every day, we hear from moms who tell us, ‘I can breathe’ or ‘A weight has been lifted off my shoulders.’ They tell us they feel less stressed, more hopeful, more supported and more loved,” Hanna says.
paras.zh: “每天，我们都会听到妈妈们告诉我们，‘我可以呼吸了’或‘我肩上的担子卸下了。’她们告诉我们，她们感到压力减轻了，更有希望了，得到了更多的支持，也得到了更多的爱，”汉纳说。

paras.en: The support has had a measurable health impact, with studies linking the program to more access to prenatal care, a decrease in the preterm birth rate and in low-weight births and fewer neonatal intensive care admissions.
paras.zh: 这项支持对健康产生了可衡量的影响，研究表明该计划与更多获得产前护理、减少早产率和低体重出生以及减少新生儿重症监护入院联系起来。

paras.en: Rx Kids has now expanded to dozens of communities in Michigan and Ohio.
paras.zh: Rx Kids 现已扩展到密歇根州和俄亥俄州的数十个社区。

articles.title: A Strange New Theory Helps Explain Why Our Universe Has Only One Dimension of Time
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Over one hundred years ago, a pioneering thinker changed how we understand space and time.
paras.zh: 一百多年前，一位先驱思想家改变了我们理解空间和时间的方式。

paras.en: He told us that they're both intertwined in a fabric that permeates the cosmos, comprising three dimensions of space and one dimension of time.
paras.zh: 他告诉我们，它们都交织在一种渗透到宇宙中的结构中，由空间的三个维度和时间的一个维度组成。

paras.en: This now-famous visionary's name? The mustachioed Hermann Minkowski, of course – Albert Einstein's math teacher.
paras.zh: 这位现在著名的梦想家的名字是什么？当然是留着小胡子的赫尔曼·明可夫斯基——阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦的数学老师。

paras.en: And no, he did not flunk Einstein, who then added gravity to the flat "Minkowski spacetime" and 'birthed' a curved spacetime.
paras.zh: 不，他并没有让爱因斯坦不及格，爱因斯坦随后将引力添加到平坦的“闵可夫斯基时空”中，并“诞生”了一个弯曲的时空。

paras.en: In fact, one can say that Einstein flunked Hermann, as Einstein deemed Hermann's way of thinking "superfluous learnedness." At first, anyway.
paras.zh: 事实上，可以说爱因斯坦没及格赫尔曼，因为爱因斯坦认为赫尔曼的思维方式“多余的学识”。无论如何，一开始。

paras.en: But why does the Universe have three spatial dimensions and one temporal dimension? A weird new mathematical theory offers a surprising possibility:
paras.zh: 但为什么宇宙具有三个空间维度和一个时间维度呢？一种奇怪的新数学理论提供了一种令人惊讶的可能性：

paras.en: It's all due to the invisible building blocks, like puzzle pieces or LEGOs (or even K'NEX) that form the cosmos.
paras.zh: 这一切都是由于无形的构建块，例如构成宇宙的拼图或乐高积木（甚至 K'NEX）。

paras.en: In a preprint paper posted to arXiv, which has not yet been peer-reviewed, a trio of physicists from the University of Belgrade, in Serbia, simulated different cosmic geometries, out of virtual four-dimensional triangles, to see if they could give rise to our familiar mix of three dimensions of space and one of time.
paras.zh: 在 arXiv 上发布的一篇尚未经过同行评审的预印本论文中，来自塞尔维亚贝尔格莱德大学的三名物理学家利用虚拟的四维三角形模拟了不同的宇宙几何形状，看看它们是否能够产生我们熟悉的三维空间和一个时间维度的混合。

paras.en: The authors used a toy model of quantum gravity – which is itself mysterious and debated – to probe some complex cosmic mechanics without the messy real-Universe complications, like the laws of physics.
paras.zh: 作者使用了量子引力的玩具模型（该模型本身很神秘且备受争议）来探索一些复杂的宇宙力学，而无需像物理定律那样混乱的真实宇宙复杂性。

paras.en: This framework modeled what one may consider an immensely miniature Universe, decreasing from four to zero dimensions, like a hierarchical house of cards.
paras.zh: 这个框架模拟了人们可能认为的一个极其微型的宇宙，从四维降到零维，就像一个分层的纸牌屋。

paras.en: It began with the four-dimensional 4-simplices, which are made of three-dimensional tetrahedra, which are made of two-dimensional triangles, which are made of one-dimensional edges, which join together at zero-dimensional vertices.
paras.zh: 它从四维 4-单纯形开始，它们由三维四面体组成，二维四面体由二维三角形组成，二维三角形由一维边组成，在零维顶点处连接在一起。

paras.en: Like a famous quote about world-supporting turtles, it's simplices all the way down!
paras.zh: 就像关于支持世界的海龟的名言一样，它自始至终都是简单的！

paras.en: The researchers then randomized the edge lengths for these pieces, setting the minimum at the Planck length, a scale of 10-35 meters that represents the breakdown of our physical understanding.
paras.zh: 然后，研究人员对这些碎片的边长进行了随机化，将最小值设置为普朗克长度，即 10-35 米的范围，代表了我们物理理解的崩溃。

paras.en: The upper bound of this scale is the point at which the Universe stops behaving like a smooth continuum and starts acting like a jagged jigsaw puzzle. Observations from the Large Hadron Collider and the LIGO-Virgo gravitational wave network help set the size range: from the size of the whole Universe, around 1026 meters, down to a scale of 10-20 meters.
paras.zh: 这个尺度的上限是宇宙停止表现得像一个光滑的连续体并开始表现得像一个锯齿状拼图的点。大型强子对撞机和 LIGO-Virgo 引力波网络的观测有助于确定尺寸范围：从整个宇宙的大小（约 1026 米）到 10-20 米的尺度。

paras.en: So any jaggedness would only appear at a scale way lower than the size of an atom, which is not even close to visible.
paras.zh: 因此，任何锯齿只会出现在远低于原子大小的尺度上，甚至不接近可见。

paras.en: The researchers also considered three different topologies, or cosmic landscapes, made of approximately 100,000 simplices in three configurations.
paras.zh: 研究人员还考虑了三种不同的拓扑或宇宙景观，它们由三种配置的大约 100,000 个单纯形组成。

paras.en: First, a four-dimensional ball with a boundary.
paras.zh: 首先，一个有边界的四维球。

paras.en: Second, a four-dimensional sphere without a boundary, because it loops back on itself.
paras.zh: 其次，一个没有边界的四维球体，因为它自身循环。

paras.en: And, thirdly, a disconnected set of four-dimensional simplices, like 100,000 scattered puzzle pieces used as a control.
paras.zh: 第三，一组不相连的四维单纯形，就像用作控件的 100,000 个分散的拼图块。

paras.en: Finally, the researchers treated all the edges of the pieces either as space-like – akin to physical distances, represented using real numbers – or as time-like – akin to time intervals, represented using imaginary numbers, or a combination of the two.
paras.zh: 最后，研究人员将碎片的所有边缘视为类空间（类似于物理距离，使用实数表示）或类时间（类似于时间间隔，使用虚数表示），或两者的组合。

paras.en: Altogether, their final data pool included over 20 billion evaluations of these various simplices-based simulations.
paras.zh: 总之，他们的最终数据池包括对这些各种基于单纯形的模拟的超过 200 亿次评估。

paras.en: So, did a four-dimensional 'Universe' emerge?
paras.zh: 那么，四维“宇宙”是否出现了？

paras.en: Amazingly, yes. When you toss a bunch of randomized puzzle pieces in a mixer, strip away complex cosmic dynamics and forces, and let them assemble geometrically, up to about 85 percent of the time they organize into a spacetime with three spatial dimensions and one temporal dimension – according to mathematical signatures the researchers assigned to these dimensions.
paras.zh: 令人惊讶的是，是的。当你将一堆随机拼图放入混合器中时，剥离复杂的宇宙动力学和力，让它们以几何方式组装，最多大约 85% 的时间它们会组织成具有三个空间维度和一个时间维度的时空——根据研究人员分配给这些维度的数学签名。

paras.en: Some other weird configurations also pop out. Around 6 percent of the trials give a Euclidean signature: a frozen Universe with four spatial dimensions and no time.
paras.zh: 其他一些奇怪的配置也随之出现。大约 6% 的试验给出了欧几里得特征：一个具有四个空间维度且没有时间的冰冻宇宙。

paras.en: And, intriguingly, about 8 percent of the trials yielded a split Universe, with two dimensions of space and two dimensions of time.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，大约 8% 的试验产生了一个分裂的宇宙，具有二维空间和二维时间。

paras.en: However, this is only when you treat the edge lengths as space-like. Treating them as time-like, or as a mixture, yields signatures with two or even three dimensions of time, rather than the Minkowski-style Universe that we perceive as reality.
paras.zh: 然而，这仅适用于将边长视为类似空间的情况。将它们视为类时间或混合物，会产生具有两个甚至三个时间维度的特征，而不是我们视为现实的明可夫斯基式宇宙。

paras.en: So this presented one of the major surprises: one would think that both space-like and time-like edges would be necessary. Yet in this model, space-like edges alone were enough: edges of mismatched lengths often can only fit together in a geometry that includes a time direction
paras.zh: 因此，这带来了主要的惊喜之一：人们会认为类空间边缘和类时间边缘都是必要的。然而，在这个模型中，仅类似空间的边缘就足够了：长度不匹配的边缘通常只能在包含时间方向的几何形状中组合在一起

paras.en: Just as surprisingly, the topology didn't matter, making little difference whether the global shape of the Universe was a ball, sphere, or just a jumble of puzzle pieces, perhaps suggesting that the split between space and time is set locally. Or that the topological differences are invisible, or average out with enough puzzle pieces.
paras.zh: 同样令人惊讶的是，拓扑并不重要，无论宇宙的整体形状是球、球体还是一堆拼图，都没有什么区别，这也许表明空间和时间之间的划分是局部设定的。或者拓扑差异是不可见的，或者用足够的拼图来平均。

paras.en: Future research can include other dynamics, like physical laws, and various shapes, to further test "whether the spacetime signature can ultimately be understood as an emergent property of quantum geometry," the researchers conclude.
paras.zh: 研究人员总结道，未来的研究可以包括其他动力学，例如物理定律和各种形状，以进一步测试“时空特征是否最终可以被理解为量子几何的新兴属性”。

paras.en: The research is available as a preprint on arXiv and has not yet been peer-reviewed.
paras.zh: 该研究已作为预印本发布在 arXiv 上，尚未经过同行评审。

articles.title: Scientists Witness a Mysterious Sexual Bond Between a Bull And a Male Donkey
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: At least, that's one way of looking at an extraordinary relationship scientists discovered by chance during fieldwork in Ethiopia.
paras.zh: 至少，这是看待科学家在埃塞俄比亚实地考察期间偶然发现的非凡关系的一种方式。

paras.en: Over a series of observations, researchers documented an unusual sexual bond between a male donkey and a bull.
paras.zh: 通过一系列观察，研究人员记录了公驴和公牛之间不寻常的性关系。

paras.en: The observations, reported in Current Biology, show animal sexual behavior can be a more complex social phenomenon than we might realize, the team says.
paras.zh: 研究小组表示，发表在《当代生物学》上的观察结果表明，动物性行为可能是一种比我们想象的更复杂的社会现象。

paras.en: "Nature does not always respect the boundaries we draw around it," ethologist Elisabetta Palagi from the University of Pisa in Italy told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 意大利比萨大学的动物行为学家 Elisabetta Palagi 告诉 ScienceAlert：“大自然并不总是尊重我们为它划定的界限。”

paras.en: "Animal behavior is not a picture painted in black and white: It uses the whole palette, with all the colors of the rainbow."
paras.zh: “动物行为并不是一幅黑白画：它使用整个调色板，具有彩虹的所有颜色。”

paras.en: While same-sex sexual behavior (SSSB) is a widespread behavior among animals, observations of sex between animals of different species are much rarer.
paras.zh: 虽然同性性行为（SSSB）是动物中普遍存在的行为，但对不同物种动物之间性行为的观察却要少得多。

paras.en: Editor's note: The video below shows footage of the bull mounting the donkey.
paras.zh: 编者注：下面的视频显示了公牛骑驴的镜头。

paras.en: Yet the interactions observed by Palagi's team between Achille (a bull) and Patroclo (a male donkey) might be something even rarer still – a bond that possibly transcended the sexual encounters they shared.
paras.zh: 然而，帕拉吉的团队观察到的阿奇勒（一头公牛）和帕特罗克洛（一头公驴）之间的互动可能更为罕见——这种联系可能超越了他们共享的性接触。

paras.en: "Both animals had access to other potential partners, including individuals of their own species and of both sexes," Palagi said.
paras.zh: 帕拉吉说：“这两种动物都可以接触到其他潜在的伴侣，包括它们自己物种和性别的个体。”

paras.en: "Yet they repeatedly sought each other out."
paras.zh: “然而他们却不断地互相寻找。”

paras.en: The research team had traveled to the Ethiopian highlands to study gelada monkeys when they noticed by accident the interactions between Achille and Patroclo in a nearby grazing area.
paras.zh: 研究小组前往埃塞俄比亚高地研究狒狒，当时他们偶然注意到附近牧场中阿奇勒和帕特罗克洛之间的相互作用。

paras.en: Over a number of days, Achille was seen mounting Patroclo. Mounting was documented 51 times, with 34 of the events resulting in intromission (penile penetration).
paras.zh: 几天来，人们看到阿基尔骑上了帕特罗克洛。记录了 51 次安装事件，其中 34 次导致插入（阴茎插入）。

paras.en: Editor's note: Graphic image below of the bull mounting the donkey.
paras.zh: 编者注：下面是公牛骑驴的图片。

paras.en: When Achille tried the same thing with another male donkey in the pasture, the donkey showed clear avoidance behaviors, including a display of threatening facial expressions (ear flattening).
paras.zh: 当阿奇勒在牧场上对另一头雄性驴尝试同样的事情时，驴表现出明显的回避行为，包括表现出威胁性的面部表情（耳朵压扁）。

paras.en: In contrast, Patroclo never avoided or kicked away Achille, but instead appeared to present his hindquarters to the bull, and both animals engaged in other acts that caught the researchers' attention.
paras.zh: 相比之下，帕特罗克洛从来没有回避或踢开阿基尔，而是似乎将他的后腿展示给公牛，并且两只动物都做出了引起研究人员注意的其他行为。

paras.en: "Achille and Patroclo were more likely to exchange affiliative behaviors, such as licking, rubbing and nuzzling, with each other than with other animals, and these interactions lasted longer. They also spent most of their observed time close together," Palagi said.
paras.zh: 帕拉吉说：“与其他动物相比，阿基尔和帕特罗克洛彼此之间更有可能交换亲和行为，例如舔、摩擦和用鼻子蹭，而且这些互动持续的时间更长。在观察到的大部分时间里，它们也都呆在一起。”

paras.en: "The sexual interactions were one component of a much broader, selective relationship."
paras.zh: “性互动是一种更广泛、选择性关系的组成部分。”

paras.en: According to the researchers, pre-mounting behaviors (involving acts such as licking and nuzzling) are not unexpected between animals, as they may help facilitate mounting.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，动物之间的预安装行为（包括舔和用鼻子蹭等行为）并不意外，因为它们可能有助于促进安装。

paras.en: But Patroclo and Achille's behavior was perhaps unusual, in that they engaged in post-mounting interactions much more often than any foreplay, suggesting there was more to their relationship than sex alone.
paras.zh: 但帕特罗克洛和阿基尔的行为也许很不寻常，因为他们在安装后的互动比任何前戏都多得多，这表明他们的关系不仅仅是性。

paras.en: "Although interpreting this behavior is challenging, the interactions observed between Achille and Patroclo, embedded in repeated, reciprocal, and mutual affiliative interactions, may also function as a signal of relationship quality," the researchers write in their paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在论文中写道：“尽管解释这种行为具有挑战性，但观察到的 Achille 和 Patroclo 之间的相互作用，嵌入重复的、相互的和相互依附的相互作用中，也可能充当关系质量的信号。”

paras.en: "Rather than being solely attributable to sexual arousal, these interactions appear to play a role in prolonging the social interaction beyond the sexual act."
paras.zh: “这些互动不仅仅归因于性唤起，而且似乎在延长性行为之外的社交互动方面发挥了作用。”

paras.en: On another occasion, when Achille mounted another donkey, Patroclo moved in close, as if to prevent further interactions between them, and Achille ended up interacting with Patroclo instead, including body licking.
paras.zh: 还有一次，当阿基尔骑上另一头驴时，帕特罗克洛靠得很近，似乎是为了防止他们之间进一步互动，而阿基尔最终却与帕特罗克洛进行了互动，包括舔身体。

paras.en: According to Palagi, this apparent selectivity and the consistency of their association were the most surprising part of the research, especially since the animals belonged to different owners and spent their nights apart, only encountering each other during daily grazing.
paras.zh: 帕拉吉表示，这种明显的选择性和它们之间关联的一致性是这项研究中最令人惊讶的部分，特别是因为这些动物属于不同的主人，并且晚上分开过夜，只有在日常放牧时才会相遇。

paras.en: "The mounting initially attracted our attention, but their repeated preference for each other's company became the most compelling part of the story," Palagi told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 帕拉吉告诉《ScienceAlert》：“这些安装最初引起了我们的注意，但他们对彼此公司的一再偏爱成为了故事中最引人注目的部分。”

paras.en: "Patroclo's behavior was particularly striking… His participation made the relationship especially intriguing."
paras.zh: “帕特罗克洛的行为特别引人注目……他的参与使这种关系特别有趣。”

paras.en: According to the researchers, Achille and Patroclo's interactions appear to be the first documented case of a sustained same-sex sexual relationship between a bull and a donkey.
paras.zh: 研究人员称，阿基尔和帕特罗克洛的互动似乎是第一个有记录的公牛和驴之间持续同性性关系的案例。

paras.en: While we can't know exactly what the relationship meant to them – and need to be careful not to interpret their interactions through an anthropomorphic lens – it's clear something was going on here, suggestive of a social bond that crossed a boundary between species.
paras.zh: 虽然我们无法确切知道这种关系对它们意味着什么——并且需要小心不要通过拟人化的镜头来解释它们的相互作用——但很明显这里正在发生一些事情，暗示着一种跨越物种界限的社会纽带。

paras.en: Whether that bond still exists is uncertain. After the study, Achille and Patroclo were moved to different grazing areas.
paras.zh: 这种联系是否仍然存在尚不确定。研究结束后，Achille 和 Patroclo 被转移到不同的放牧区域。

paras.en: The researchers hope to return to see if the animals resume their activities, and to investigate whether similar relationships are occurring between species more often than we realize.
paras.zh: 研究人员希望回来看看动物是否恢复活动，并调查物种之间类似的关系是否比我们意识到的更频繁地发生。

paras.en: "Unusual behavior can remain anecdotal simply because nobody has the opportunity to document it systematically," Palagi said.
paras.zh: “不寻常的行为可能只是轶事，因为没有人有机会系统地记录它，”帕拉吉说。

paras.en: "Nature's full palette becomes visible only when we are willing to notice the unexpected."
paras.zh: “只有当我们愿意注意到意想不到的事情时，大自然的全部调色板才会变得可见。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in Current Biology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《当代生物学》杂志上。

articles.title: Dinosaur Blood Cells Detected in 115-Million-Year-Old Fossil
articles.author: Michael Irving

paras.en: We've found plenty of dinosaur bones. We've found their teeth, skin, feathers, eggs, and even their poop.
paras.zh: 我们发现了大量的恐龙骨头。我们发现了它们的牙齿、皮肤、羽毛、蛋，甚至它们的粪便。

paras.en: A team led by scientists at Curtin University in Australia has identified what appear to be fossilized red blood cells, along with blood-derived molecules, preserved for over 100 million years, inside an unassuming dinosaur leg bone.
paras.zh: 由澳大利亚科廷大学科学家领导的一个研究小组在一块不起眼的恐龙腿骨中发现了似乎是化石的红细胞以及血液衍生分子，这些分子保存了 1 亿多年。

paras.en: If the claim sounds familiar, that's because several teams have claimed to detect proteins and cells in dinosaur fossils over the last few decades. But these finds have been difficult to replicate and confirm that the cells indeed belonged to the original animal, and weren't just outside contamination after death.
paras.zh: 如果这个说法听起来很熟悉，那是因为在过去的几十年里，有几个团队声称在恐龙化石中检测到了蛋白质和细胞。但这些发现很难复制并确认这些细胞确实属于原始动物，而不仅仅是死后的外部污染。

paras.en: In the new study, the identity of the suspected cells was backed up by chemical analysis.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，可疑细胞的身份得到了化学分析的支持。

paras.en: "Something that looks like a blood cell under a microscope is interesting, but morphology by itself isn't enough to establish its biological origin," Kliti Grice, organic geochemist at Curtin University, told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 科廷大学有机地球化学家 Kliti Grice 告诉 ScienceAlert：“显微镜下看起来像血细胞的东西很有趣，但形态本身不足以确定其生物起源。”

paras.en: "Our approach brings together microscopic observations with chemical evidence associated with the structures. The convergence of independent lines of evidence is much more powerful than saying, 'this looks like a red blood cell'."
paras.zh: “我们的方法将微观观察结果与与结构相关的化学证据结合起来。独立证据线的融合比说‘这看起来像红细胞’更有力。”

paras.en: The discovery was made in a fossil recovered from a mine in Brazil in 2008. These bones were from the right leg of an Aratasaurus museunacionali, a small theropod dinosaur that lived around 115 million years ago.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在 2008 年从巴西的一个矿井中发现的一块化石中发现的。这些骨头来自 Musunaacionali 阿拉塔龙的右腿，这是一种小型兽脚类恐龙，生活在大约 1.15 亿年前。

paras.en: On close inspection, fossilized vascular canals were detected inside the bones – and inside those canals, the team found a treasure trove of ellipsoidal microstructures.
paras.zh: 经过仔细检查，在骨头内部发现了化石血管，而在这些血管内，研究小组发现了椭圆形微观结构的宝库。

paras.en: "When we examined the Aratasaurus bone at the microscopic and chemical level, we encountered structures that were remarkably cell-like, in the order of right size, and a lot of them in the right location in the vascular canals," Grice said.
paras.zh: 格赖斯说：“当我们在显微镜和化学水平上检查阿拉塔龙的骨骼时，我们发现了非常类似细胞的结构，其大小顺序正确，而且其中很多位于血管管的正确位置。”

paras.en: "But as a scientist, excitement has to be followed very quickly by skepticism. The more extraordinary the observation, the more carefully you have to test alternative explanations."
paras.zh: “但作为一名科学家，兴奋之后必须很快出现怀疑。观察结果越非凡，你就越需要仔细地测试其他解释。”

paras.en: To do so, the team conducted a series of imaging, spectroscopic, and molecular analyses on the suspected cells, as well as the material surrounding the bones.
paras.zh: 为此，研究小组对可疑细胞以及骨骼周围的材料进行了一系列成像、光谱和分子分析。

paras.en: It was a possibility, for instance, that the microstructures were the preserved remains of fungi or other microbes that colonized the bones after death but before fossilization. But if that were the case, you'd expect to see traces of filaments, spores, biofilms, or other structures – and the team found none.
paras.zh: 例如，微观结构有可能是真菌或其他微生物的保存遗骸，它们在死后但在化石化之前在骨头上定居。但如果是这样的话，你会期望看到细丝、孢子、生物膜或其他结构的痕迹——但研究小组什么也没发现。

paras.en: Geochemical analysis also revealed no traces of pyrite mineralization or sedimentary grains that could masquerade as cellular structures.
paras.zh: 地球化学分析还显示，没有发现黄铁矿矿化或可能伪装成细胞结构的沉积颗粒的痕迹。

paras.en: While it's nice to find an absence of contaminants, it's even better to detect the presence of compounds linked to blood cells – specifically heme, a key molecule that helps blood cells carry oxygen.
paras.zh: 虽然很高兴发现不存在污染物，但更好的是检测与血细胞相关的化合物的存在，特别是血红素，这是一种帮助血细胞携带氧气的关键分子。

paras.en: High-performance liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry revealed the bone extract was dominated by heme B, very different from the molecular signatures in the surrounding rock, which seemed to have been produced by photosynthetic microbes.
paras.zh: 高效液相色谱-质谱分析显示，骨提取物以血红素 B 为主，与周围岩石中的分子特征非常不同，周围岩石似乎是由光合微生物产生的。

paras.en: The team also conducted elemental mapping to investigate which elements were associated with which parts of the fossil. The cell-like microstructures were found to be correlated with iron, carbon, and nitrogen – potential constituents of heme. The rest of the bone was made up of phosphorus, calcium, fluorine, and carbon.
paras.zh: 该团队还进行了元素测绘，以调查哪些元素与化石的哪些部分相关。研究发现细胞状微观结构与铁、碳和氮（血红素的潜在成分）相关。骨头的其余部分由磷、钙、氟和碳组成。

paras.en: Being around 115 million years old, this fossil marks the oldest known example of possible dinosaur blood cells – previous finds date back "only" about 80 million years at most.
paras.zh: 这块化石大约有 1.15 亿年的历史，标志着已知最古老的可能的恐龙血细胞的例子——之前的发现最多只能追溯到大约 8000 万年前。

paras.en: So how can these tiny, soft tissues persist for so long? The team suggests that it's largely due to the specific geological setting in which this Aratasaurus was preserved: a microbial mat in shallow waters almost completely starved of oxygen.
paras.zh: 那么这些微小的软组织如何能够持续这么长时间呢？研究小组认为，这很大程度上是由于这种阿拉塔龙被保存的特定地质环境：浅水中的微生物垫几乎完全缺乏氧气。

paras.en: "Our interpretation is that manganese mineralization may have contributed to stabilizing or replicating these extremely delicate structures during fossilization," Grice said.
paras.zh: 格莱斯说：“我们的解释是，锰矿化可能有助于在化石形成过程中稳定或复制这些极其脆弱的结构。”

paras.en: "Rather than imagining a pristine biological cell surviving unchanged for 115 million years, I think it is more useful to think of the original biological structure interacting with its surrounding geochemical environment. That may have created a mineralized record of something that would normally disappear very rapidly."
paras.zh: “我认为，与其想象一个原始生物细胞在 1.15 亿年里保持不变，不如考虑原始生物结构与其周围地球化学环境的相互作用。这可能创造了一种通常会很快消失的矿化记录。”

paras.en: Still, as with any potential landmark studies, it's important to temper excitement with a healthy dose of caution, while scientists perform follow-up studies on this and other specimens.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，与任何潜在的里程碑式研究一样，在科学家对这个标本和其他标本进行后续研究时，以适当的谨慎来缓和兴奋是很重要的。

paras.en: "The immediate priority is replication," said Grice.
paras.zh: “当务之急是复制，”格赖斯说。

paras.en: "We need to examine additional fossils, different geological settings and other parts of the dinosaur family tree using complementary microscopic, chemical and molecular techniques. If similar signals can be demonstrated independently, we can begin asking much bigger questions about preservation and, cautiously, about ancient physiology."
paras.zh: “我们需要使用互补的显微镜、化学和分子技术来检查更多的化石、不同的地质环境和恐龙谱系的其他部分。如果可以独立证明类似的信号，我们就可以开始提出有关保存的更大问题，并谨慎地提出有关古代生理学的更大问题。”

paras.en: Related: We Have The First Direct Evidence That Ticks Really Did Feast on Dinosaur Blood
paras.zh: 相关：我们有第一个直接证据表明蜱虫确实以恐龙血为食

paras.en: It means that the next big dino discovery might not come from a chance find in a desert dig, but from a curator rummaging through a forgotten drawer.
paras.zh: 这意味着下一个大型恐龙发现可能不是来自沙漠挖掘中的偶然发现，而是来自馆长在一个被遗忘的抽屉中翻找的结果。

paras.en: "What particularly excites me is that thousands of fossils already sitting in museum and university collections could potentially be revisited," said Grice.
paras.zh: 格赖斯说：“特别令我兴奋的是，博物馆和大学收藏的数千件化石可能会被重新审视。”

paras.en: "A specimen collected decades ago for anatomical study may also contain molecular, mineralogical, isotopic, and microscopic information that nobody thought to look for at the time."
paras.zh: “几十年前收集的用于解剖研究的标本可能还包含当时没有人想到要寻找的分子、矿物学、同位素和微观信息。”

paras.en: The research was published in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在《美国国家科学院院刊》杂志上。

articles.title: New diabetes implant uses electricity to lower blood sugar and promote weight loss

paras.en: New diabetes implant uses electricity to lower blood sugar and promote weight loss
paras.zh: 新型糖尿病植入物利用电力来降低血糖并促进减肥

paras.en: - Researchers have developed a remarkable new electronic implant that could transform type 2 diabetes treatment by lowering blood sugar without insulin or traditional drugs. The device uses a special electrically powered catalyst to convert excess glucose into a substance that the body eliminates through urine, potentially preventing unwanted energy from being stored as fat. In diabetic mice, the implant precisely controlled blood sugar and promoted weight loss.
paras.zh: - 研究人员开发出一种非凡的新型电子植入物，无需胰岛素或传统药物即可降低血糖，从而改变 2 型糖尿病的治疗方法。该设备使用特殊的电动催化剂将多余的葡萄糖转化为身体通过尿液排出的物质，从​​而可能防止不需要的能量被储存为脂肪。在糖尿病小鼠中，植入物精确控制血糖并促进体重减轻。

paras.en: An experimental electronic implant could offer an entirely new way to treat type 2 diabetes. Rather than relying on insulin or conventional medications, the device uses electricity to convert excess blood sugar into a substance that the body can eliminate. In early tests with diabetic mice, the technology successfully regulated blood sugar and also led to weight loss.
paras.zh: 实验性电子植入物可以提供一种治疗 2 型糖尿病的全新方法。该设备不依赖胰岛素​​或传统药物，而是利用电力将多余的血糖转化为身体可以消除的物质。在对糖尿病小鼠的早期测试中，该技术成功调节了血糖并导致体重减轻。

paras.en: The development comes as type 2 diabetes continues to affect a growing number of people worldwide. Unlike type 1 diabetes, type 2 is frequently associated with obesity, limited physical activity, and consuming more energy than the body needs over long periods.
paras.zh: 这一发展正值 2 型糖尿病继续影响全世界越来越多的人之际。与 1 型糖尿病不同，2 型糖尿病通常与肥胖、体力活动受限以及长期消耗超过身体所需的能量有关。

paras.en: Insulin injections can help reduce blood sugar by allowing muscle cells to absorb glucose from the bloodstream. However, insulin does not eliminate the underlying problem of excess energy. When the body does not use the glucose it absorbs, the surplus can eventually be converted into fat. This helps explain why some people with diabetes continue gaining weight even while receiving treatment.
paras.zh: 注射胰岛素可以让肌肉细胞从血液中吸收葡萄糖，从而帮助降低血糖。然而，胰岛素并不能消除能量过剩的根本问题。当身体不使用它吸收的葡萄糖时，多余的葡萄糖最终会转化为脂肪。这有助于解释为什么一些糖尿病患者即使在接受治疗时体重仍然增加。

paras.en: Researchers led by Martin Fussenegger, a professor in the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering at ETH Zurich in Basel, have developed an implant designed to address this problem differently. Their findings were published in the journal Science.
paras.zh: 由巴塞尔苏黎世联邦理工学院生物系统科学与工程系教授 Martin Fussenegger 领导的研究人员开发了一种植入物，旨在以不同的方式解决这个问题。他们的研究结果发表在《科学》杂志上。

paras.en: A New Diabetes Treatment Powered by Electricity
paras.zh: 一种新的电力驱动的糖尿病治疗方法

paras.en: Fussenegger and his colleagues have spent years developing technologies capable of controlling blood sugar. Their previous designs used engineered genetic networks, but these systems depended on living cells and other biological materials.
paras.zh: 富森格和他的同事花了数年时间开发能够控制血糖的技术。他们之前的设计使用了工程基因网络，但这些系统依赖于活细胞和其他生物材料。

paras.en: That dependence introduced several complications. Biological components can create challenges involving immune compatibility, long-term stability, production, and regulatory approval.
paras.zh: 这种依赖性带来了一些并发症。生物成分可能会带来涉及免疫相容性、长期稳定性、生产和监管审批的挑战。

paras.en: The researchers have now taken a different approach by creating a catalyst made entirely from inorganic materials. It performs its function without requiring living cells, enzymes, or other biological components.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在采取了不同的方法，创造了一种完全由无机材料制成的催化剂。它无需活细胞、酶或其他生物成分即可发挥其功能。

paras.en: At the heart of the implant is a piece of graphite felt covered with tiny clusters of gold. These gold structures are coated with even smaller platinum particles, creating a specially engineered surface that enables the chemical reaction needed to process glucose.
paras.zh: 植入物的中心是一块石墨毡，上面覆盖着微小的金簇。这些金结构上涂有更小的铂颗粒，形成了专门设计的表面，可以实现处理葡萄糖所需的化学反应。

paras.en: The researchers designed this nanoscale surface themselves. According to Fussenegger, the materials also demonstrated excellent biocompatibility during experimental testing, suggesting they can interact with living tissue without causing significant adverse reactions.
paras.zh: 研究人员自己设计了这种纳米级表面。 Fussenegger 表示，这些材料在实验测试中还表现出优异的生物相容性，表明它们可以与活体组织相互作用，而不会引起明显的不良反应。

paras.en: The system includes an electronic controller enclosed in a 3D-printed housing. Instead of relying on a conventional wired power connection, the implant receives energy wirelessly at a frequency of 13.56 MHz. This frequency is internationally allocated for industrial, scientific, and medical applications.
paras.zh: 该系统包括一个封装在 3D 打印外壳中的电子控制器。植入物不依赖传统的有线电源连接，而是以 13.56 MHz 的频率无线接收能量。该频率在国际上分配给工业、科学和医疗应用。

paras.en: How the Implant Removes Excess Blood Sugar
paras.zh: 植入物如何去除多余的血糖

paras.en: The technology works by transforming excess glucose into gluconate, a substance that can be eliminated from the body through urine.
paras.zh: 该技术的工作原理是将多余的葡萄糖转化为葡萄糖酸盐，这种物质可以通过尿液从体内排出。

paras.en: Normally, glucose provides energy for cells. When more glucose is available than the body needs, some of that excess energy can ultimately be stored as fat. By converting part of the glucose into gluconate, the implant prevents that portion from being metabolized and stored in tissues, potentially helping reduce fat accumulation.
paras.zh: 正常情况下，葡萄糖为细胞提供能量。当可用的葡萄糖多于身体所需时，一些多余的能量最终会以脂肪的形式储存起来。通过将部分葡萄糖转化为葡萄糖酸盐，植入物可以防止该部分被代谢并储存在组织中，从而可能有助于减少脂肪堆积。

paras.en: The entire process is designed to happen automatically, responding to changes in blood sugar as they occur.
paras.zh: 整个过程被设计为自动发生，响应血糖的变化。

paras.en: A conventional glucose sensor, similar to those worn on the upper arm by many people with diabetes, continuously measures glucose concentrations in tissue. When levels rise too high, such as after a meal, the sensor communicates through Bluetooth with a smartphone or smartwatch.
paras.zh: 传统的葡萄糖传感器类似于许多糖尿病患者佩戴在上臂的传感器，可以连续测量组织中的葡萄糖浓度。当水位升高得太高时，例如饭后，传感器会通过蓝牙与智能手机或智能手表进行通信。

paras.en: The connected device then activates the implant, supplying the electrical energy needed for the catalyst to convert glucose into gluconate.
paras.zh: 然后连接的设备激活植入物，提供催化剂将葡萄糖转化为葡萄糖酸盐所需的电能。

paras.en: Once glucose levels return to the desired range, the implant automatically shuts down. This feedback system, known as closed-loop control, is intended to prevent blood sugar from dropping dangerously low.
paras.zh: 一旦血糖水平恢复到所需范围，植入物就会自动关闭。这种反馈系统被称为闭环控制，旨在防止血糖降至危险的低水平。

paras.en: Blood Sugar Control and Weight Loss in Diabetic Mice
paras.zh: 糖尿病小鼠的血糖控制和体重减轻

paras.en: To evaluate the technology, the researchers first conducted a laboratory experiment using a reservoir containing 5 liters of a nutrient solution with glucose. That volume is approximately equal to the amount of blood circulating in an adult human body.
paras.zh: 为了评估这项技术，研究人员首先使用装有 5 升葡萄糖营养液的储液器进行了实验室实验。该体积大约等于成年人体内循环的血液量。

paras.en: The experiment demonstrated that the catalyst could convert glucose in a solution of this scale, an important step toward assessing its potential for medical applications.
paras.zh: 该实验表明，该催化剂可以在这种规模的溶液中转化葡萄糖，这是评估其医疗应用潜力的重要一步。

paras.en: The researchers then implanted the system in diabetic mice. The results showed that the device could precisely regulate the animals' blood sugar levels. The mice also lost weight, suggesting that converting excess glucose rather than allowing it to contribute to fat storage could offer an additional metabolic benefit.
paras.zh: 研究人员随后将该系统植入糖尿病小鼠体内。结果表明，该装置可以精确调节动物的血糖水平。小鼠的体重也减轻了，这表明转化多余的葡萄糖而不是让其有助于脂肪储存可以提供额外的代谢益处。

paras.en: Over six weeks of testing, the implant continued functioning reliably and was well tolerated by the animals.
paras.zh: 经过六周的测试，植入物持续可靠地发挥作用，并且动物的耐受性良好。

paras.en: "The system operates at a very low voltage, and our experiments showed no evidence of tissue damage from either electrical or thermal effects," says Fussenegger.
paras.zh: “该系统在非常低的电压下运行，我们的实验表明没有证据表明电效应或热效应造成组织损伤，”富塞内格说。

paras.en: Although these findings are promising, the device has not yet been tested in humans. Additional research will be necessary to determine whether the technology can operate safely and effectively in people with diabetes.
paras.zh: 尽管这些发现很有希望，但该设备尚未在人体上进行测试。还需要进行更多研究来确定该技术是否可以在糖尿病患者中安全有效地运行。

paras.en: Could Electronics Transform the Future of Diabetes Treatment?
paras.zh: 电子技术能否改变糖尿病治疗的未来？

paras.en: Fussenegger believes the technology could represent a fundamental change in how diabetes is managed. Rather than using medications to influence how the body processes glucose, an electronic device could directly control the amount of glucose available.
paras.zh: 富森格认为，这项技术可能代表糖尿病治疗方式的根本性改变。电子设备可以直接控制可用的葡萄糖量，而不是使用药物来影响身体处理葡萄糖的方式。

paras.en: "For decades, we have treated diabetes by telling the body how to manage glucose. We are now showing that we can take control of glucose directly, using electronics rather than drugs," he says. "And the catalyst only activates when glucose levels are too high."
paras.zh: “几十年来，我们通过告诉身体如何管理葡萄糖来治疗糖尿病。现在我们证明，我们可以使用电子设备而不是药物来直接控制葡萄糖，”他说。 “只有当葡萄糖水平过高时，催化剂才会激活。”

paras.en: The approach also creates opportunities to connect medical treatments with digital technologies, including the Internet of Things. This refers to networks of devices that exchange information and respond automatically to changing conditions.
paras.zh: 该方法还创造了将医疗治疗与数字技术（包括物联网）连接起来的机会。这是指交换信息并自动响应不断变化的条件的设备网络。

paras.en: The researchers envision electronically controlled treatments that could be manufactured at scale and integrated with existing digital health systems.
paras.zh: 研究人员设想可以大规模生产并与现有数字医疗系统集成的电子控制治疗方法。

paras.en: Their next objective is to turn the experimental implant into a medical device suitable for further development and eventual clinical testing.
paras.zh: 他们的下一个目标是将实验植入物转变为适合进一步开发和最终临床测试的医疗设备。

paras.en: One potential advantage is its relatively simple glucose conversion mechanism. Because the catalyst does not rely on cells or enzymes, the researchers believe some of the technical challenges associated with biological treatments could be easier to overcome.
paras.zh: 一个潜在的优势是其相对简单的葡萄糖转化机制。由于催化剂不依赖于细胞或酶，研究人员认为与生物处理相关的一些技术挑战可能更容易克服。

paras.en: Much of the supporting technology is also already available. Wireless power transmission systems and external electronic controllers are commercially established, meaning the team would not need to develop every component from scratch.
paras.zh: 许多支持技术也已经可用。无线电力传输系统和外部电子控制器已商业化，这意味着团队不需要从头开始开发每个组件。

paras.en: If future studies demonstrate similar benefits in humans, this approach could open the door to a new class of diabetes treatments in which smart electronic devices help regulate blood sugar directly, potentially reducing reliance on conventional medications.
paras.zh: 如果未来的研究证明对人类有类似的好处，这种方法可能会为新型糖尿病治疗打开大门，其中智能电子设备有助于直接调节血糖，从而有可能减少对传统药物的依赖。

paras.en: - Debasis Maity, Preetam Guha Ray, Peter Buchmann, Ghislaine Charpin-El Hamri, Martin Fussenegger. Wireless electrocatalytic closed-loop system for drug-free management of diabesity. Science, 2026; 394 (6822) DOI: 10.1126/science.ady8560
paras.zh: - Debasis Maity、Preetam Guha Ray、Peter Buchmann、Ghislaine Charpin-El Hamri、Martin Fussenegger。用于糖尿病无药物管理的无线电催化闭环系统。科学，2026； 394 (6822) DOI: 10.1126/science.ady8560

articles.title: Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation

paras.en: Experts say high blood pressure guidelines are missing half the equation
paras.zh: 专家称高血压指南遗漏了一半

paras.en: Cutting back on salt may not be enough to get the greatest benefits for blood pressure.
paras.zh: 减少盐的摄入量可能不足以获得最大的降血压益处。

paras.en: - Scientists are calling for a major rethink of how we manage high blood pressure, suggesting that eating more potassium could be just as important as cutting back on salt. A new report finds that combining increased potassium intake with reduced sodium consumption may offer greater benefits for blood pressure control than sodium reduction alone.
paras.zh: - 科学家呼吁重新思考如何控制高血压，这表明多吃钾可能与减少盐摄入量同样重要。一份新报告发现，增加钾摄入量和减少钠摄入量相结合可能比单独减少钠摄入量对血压控制有更大的好处。

paras.en: For decades, one of the most common recommendations for lowering high blood pressure has been simple: eat less salt. But a new scientific report suggests that this advice may be missing an equally important part of the equation.
paras.zh: 几十年来，降低高血压最常见的建议之一很简单：少吃盐。但一份新的科学报告表明，这一建议可能遗漏了同样重要的部分。

paras.en: Researchers say that increasing potassium intake, rather than focusing only on reducing sodium, could lead to better blood pressure control. By addressing both nutrients together, this approach could strengthen efforts to prevent hypertension and reduce the risk of serious cardiovascular problems.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，增加钾的摄入量，而不是仅仅注重减少钠的摄入量，可以更好地控制血压。通过同时处理这两种营养素，这种方法可以加强预防高血压和降低严重心血管问题的风险。

paras.en: The potential impact is enormous. High blood pressure, also known as hypertension, affects more than 1.28 billion adults worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease, including heart attacks and strokes. Although public health recommendations have traditionally emphasized cutting sodium, researchers now argue that getting enough potassium deserves just as much attention.
paras.zh: 潜在的影响是巨大的。高血压，也称为高血压，影响着全球超过 12.8 亿成年人，是心血管疾病（包括心脏病发作和中风）的主要危险因素。尽管公共卫生建议传统上强调减少钠摄入量，但研究人员现在认为，摄入足够的钾也值得同样重视。

paras.en: Why Potassium Matters for Blood Pressure
paras.zh: 为什么钾对血压很重要

paras.en: Sodium and potassium are essential minerals that help regulate fluid balance, nerve signaling, and muscle function. Both also influence blood pressure, but they affect the body in different ways.
paras.zh: 钠和钾是帮助调节体液平衡、神经信号和肌肉功能的必需矿物质。两者都会影响血压，但它们以不同的方式影响身体。

paras.en: Eating too much sodium can cause the body to retain additional fluid, increasing the pressure inside blood vessels. Potassium helps counter some of sodium's effects by supporting the kidneys in removing excess sodium through urine. It also contributes to the normal functioning of blood vessel walls, which plays an important role in maintaining healthy blood pressure.
paras.zh: 摄入过多的钠会导致身体滞留额外的液体，从而增加血管内的压力。钾通过支持肾脏通过尿液去除多余的钠，从而有助于抵消钠的一些影响。它还有助于血管壁的正常功能，这在维持健康血压方面发挥着重要作用。

paras.en: In a new report, physicians and health experts argue that dietary recommendations should address these two minerals together. Rather than treating sodium reduction as the primary solution, they propose combining it with greater potassium consumption to achieve stronger results.
paras.zh: 在一份新报告中，医生和健康专家认为饮食建议应该同时考虑这两种矿物质。他们建议将减少钠摄入量与增加钾消耗相结合，以获得更好的效果，而不是把减少钠摄入量作为主要解决方案。

paras.en: "It is time to view dietary interventions holistically because food components interact and physiology is integrative across systems," said Naomi Fukagawa, M.D. Ph.D., professor of medicine emerita at the Robert Larner, M.D. College of Medicine at the University of Vermont and first author on the report. "Growing evidence shows that increasing dietary potassium as well as reducing sodium intake work together to better manage hypertension."
paras.zh: 佛蒙特大学罗伯特·拉纳医学院名誉教授、该报告的第一作者深川直美医学博士说：“是时候从整体上看待饮食干预措施了，因为食物成分相互作用，而生理学在各个系统中是整合的。” “越来越多的证据表明，增加饮食中的钾和减少钠的摄入量可以共同更好地控制高血压。”

paras.en: A Major Rethink of Blood Pressure Guidelines
paras.zh: 对血压指南的重大反思

paras.en: The report, published in the peer-reviewed American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, was supported by the IAFNS Sodium in Food and Health Implications Committee.
paras.zh: 该报告发表在经过同行评审的《美国临床营养学杂志》上，并得到了 IAFNS 食品钠和健康影响委员会的支持。

paras.en: The researchers examined the scientific evidence underlying current sodium and potassium recommendations, along with practical ways to reduce sodium consumption and increase potassium intake. They also explored the obstacles to implementing these changes and identified areas where additional research and updated public health policies could help improve outcomes.
paras.zh: 研究人员研究了当前钠和钾建议的科学证据，以及减少钠消耗和增加钾摄入量的实用方法。他们还探讨了实施这些变革的障碍，并确定了额外研究和更新的公共卫生政策可以帮助改善结果的领域。

paras.en: One of the central concerns is that many people consume too much sodium while getting nowhere near enough potassium. Both dietary patterns can contribute to elevated blood pressure, making them important targets for prevention and treatment.
paras.zh: 核心问题之一是许多人摄入了过多的钠，而钾却远远不够。这两种饮食模式都会导致血压升高，因此成为预防和治疗的重要目标。

paras.en: Despite widespread efforts to encourage people to limit salt, average sodium consumption continues to exceed recommended levels. Meanwhile, potassium intake remains "far below optimal levels in both developed and developing nations," according to the authors.
paras.zh: 尽管人们广泛努力鼓励人们限制盐分，但平均钠摄入量仍然超过建议水平。与此同时，作者表示，钾摄入量“在发达国家和发展中国家都远远低于最佳水平”。

paras.en: This imbalance suggests that focusing primarily on what people should eat less of may be overlooking an important opportunity to improve cardiovascular health by encouraging them to consume more of a beneficial nutrient.
paras.zh: 这种不平衡表明，主要关注人们应该少吃什么可能会忽视通过鼓励人们摄入更多有益营养素来改善心血管健康的重要机会。

paras.en: Potassium is naturally present in many familiar foods, including fruits, vegetables, legumes, and dairy products. Bananas, potatoes, beans, leafy greens, and yogurt are examples of foods that can help increase potassium intake.
paras.zh: 钾天然存在于许多熟悉的食物中，包括水果、蔬菜、豆类和乳制品。香蕉、土豆、豆类、绿叶蔬菜和酸奶都是有助于增加钾摄入量的食物。

paras.en: Another possibility is replacing some sodium chloride, the main ingredient in ordinary table salt, with potassium salts. These substitutes can help reduce sodium while simultaneously increasing potassium, potentially addressing both dietary goals at once.
paras.zh: 另一种可能性是用钾盐代替一些氯化钠（普通食盐的主要成分）。这些替代品可以帮助减少钠的摄入，同时增加钾的摄入，有可能同时满足这两个饮食目标。

paras.en: However, creating these products presents challenges for food manufacturers. Adding too much potassium salt can produce an unpleasant metallic taste, limiting how much can be used without affecting flavor. Manufacturers must therefore find a balance that improves nutritional content while keeping foods appealing to consumers.
paras.zh: 然而，生产这些产品给食品制造商带来了挑战。添加过多的钾盐会产生令人不愉快的金属味，限制了在不影响风味的情况下可以使用的量。因此，制造商必须找到一种平衡点，既提高营养成分，又保持食品对消费者的吸引力。

paras.en: Increasing potassium is also not appropriate for everyone. People with kidney disease or those taking certain medications may have difficulty regulating potassium levels, so potassium supplements and potassium-based salt substitutes should be used with medical guidance when these concerns apply.
paras.zh: 增加钾的摄入量也并不适合所有人。患有肾脏疾病或服用某些药物的人可能难以调节钾水平，因此当出现这些问题时，应在医疗指导下使用钾补充剂和钾盐替代品。

paras.en: A New Strategy for Fighting High Blood Pressure
paras.zh: 对抗高血压的新策略

paras.en: The researchers emphasize that reducing sodium remains essential. Their proposal is not to abandon existing advice, but to expand it by recognizing that potassium intake is another major factor in blood pressure regulation.
paras.zh: 研究人员强调，减少钠摄入量仍然至关重要。他们的建议不是放弃现有的建议，而是通过认识到钾摄入量是血压调节的另一个主要因素来扩大建议范围。

paras.en: The authors conclude that "dietary sodium reduction is a foundational strategy for hypertension prevention and management. However, new evidence supports a broadening of the current approach that focuses solely on sodium reduction and provides equal emphasis on increasing potassium intake."
paras.zh: 作者得出的结论是，“饮食中减少钠摄入量是高血压预防和管理的基本策略。然而，新的证据支持扩大目前仅关注钠摄入量并同等重视增加钾摄入量的方法。”

paras.en: For the more than one billion people living with hypertension, this shift in thinking could have significant implications. Instead of concentrating almost exclusively on reducing salt, future dietary recommendations may increasingly emphasize the combined benefits of consuming less sodium and more potassium.
paras.zh: 对于超过十亿高血压患者来说，这种思维转变可能会产生重大影响。未来的饮食建议可能会越来越强调摄入更少的钠和更多的钾的综合益处，而不是几乎完全专注于减少盐分。

paras.en: The underlying message is straightforward: better blood pressure control may depend not only on what people remove from their diets, but also on what they add.
paras.zh: 潜在的信息很简单：更好的血压控制可能不仅取决于人们从饮食中去除什么，还取决于他们添加什么。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of Vermont. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由佛蒙特大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

paras.en: - Naomi K Fukagawa, Paul A Welling, Janice Johnson, Kristin Reimers, Soo-Yeun Lee, Patricia Zecca. Rethinking the impact of dietary sodium and potassium on blood pressure to advance public health. The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, 2026; 124 (2): 101396 DOI: 10.1016/j.ajcnut.2026.101396
paras.zh: - Naomi K Fukakawa、Paul A Welling、Janice Johnson、Kristin Reimers、Soo-Yeun Lee、Patricia Zecca。重新思考膳食钠和钾对血压的影响，以促进公众健康。美国临床营养杂志，2026； 124（2）：101396 DOI：10.1016/j.ajcnut.2026.101396

articles.title: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos

paras.en: IceCube detects ghost particles with 10 billion times the energy of solar neutrinos
paras.zh: IceCube探测到的幽灵粒子能量是太阳中微子的100亿倍

paras.en: - Mysterious particles called neutrinos constantly stream through our bodies, and scientists are now detecting incredibly powerful versions arriving from distant cosmic sources using a massive observatory buried in Antarctic ice. These elusive âghost particlesâ could hold extraordinary clues about the Big Bang, extreme cosmic events, and some of the universeâs greatest mysteries.
paras.zh: - 被称为中微子的神秘粒子不断地流过我们的身体，科学家们现在正在使用埋在南极冰层中的大型天文台探测来自遥远宇宙源的极其强大的中微子。这些难以捉摸的“幽灵粒子”可能蕴藏着有关大爆炸、极端宇宙事件以及一些宇宙最大奥秘的非凡线索。

paras.en: An enormous number of invisible particles are constantly traveling through Earth, passing through our bodies and continuing into space as though almost nothing stands in their way. Known as neutrinos, these mysterious particles are among the most difficult objects in the universe to detect. Yet scientists are finding ways to capture evidence of their passage, opening new opportunities to investigate the cosmos and its most extreme environments.
paras.zh: 大量看不见的粒子不断地穿过地球，穿过我们的身体，继续进入太空，就好像几乎没有什么能阻挡它们一样。这些神秘粒子被称为中微子，是宇宙中最难探测的物体之一。然而，科学家们正在寻找方法来捕获它们通过的证据，为研究宇宙及其最极端的环境提供新的机会。

paras.en: Neutrino research has played a remarkable role in modern physics. Discoveries involving these particles have contributed to five Nobel Prizes in Physics. This year, physicist Francis Halzen received the prestigious award "for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin."
paras.zh: 中微子研究在现代物理学中发挥了非凡的作用。涉及这些粒子的发现为五位诺贝尔物理学奖做出了贡献。今年，物理学家弗朗西斯·哈尔森（Francis Halzen）“因对冰立方中微子观测站和发现天体物理起源的高能中微子做出的决定性贡献”而获得了这一享有声望的奖项。

paras.en: George Fuller, a Distinguished Professor of Physics at the University of California San Diego, has studied nuclear physics, particle astrophysics, and cosmology for decades. He also collaborated with Halzen on an early scientific paper about IceCube. His expertise helps explain what makes neutrinos so unusual and why scientists built an enormous observatory deep within the Antarctic ice to study them.
paras.zh: 乔治·富勒是加州大学圣地亚哥分校的杰出物理学教授，几十年来一直研究核物理、粒子天体物理学和宇宙学。他还与 Halzen 合作撰写了一篇有关 IceCube 的早期科学论文。他的专业知识有助于解释中微子为何如此不寻常，以及为什么科学家在南极冰层深处建造了一个巨大的观测站来研究中微子。

paras.en: Neutrinos belong to a group known as elementary particles, which scientists believe have no smaller components. They come in three varieties, called electron, muon, and tau neutrinos. Unlike electrically charged particles, neutrinos have no electric charge. They do have mass, but it is extraordinarily small, potentially around 10 million times less than the mass of an electron. Their exact masses remain unknown, as does the mechanism responsible for producing them.
